projects.title: Show HN: Grist, open source coding harness
projects.author: pranav6226
projects.summary: I built a coding harness on top of the new Opencode v2, it started with the the idea of using the new jev model for routing easy tasks to cheaper models such as deepseek and hard tasks to models such as Opus 5.5. In total in separated it into 4 rungs - easy, medium, hard and frontier. Two more layers compound the savings: the Sol-Pi methodology based on the recently published paper which uses action fusion and observation packing and cuts roken usage within every tier. Doctrine injection loads your engineering standards into every session by default, so the agent writes code the way your team would. There is also a real control plane - escalation, permission and verification hooks so the agent surfaces uncertainty instead of being confidently wrong in silence. Run it using your own key from Openrouter or Vercel AI gateway key, we need this since one key is able to call the jev decision model as well as the llms for coding. One more thing I added was the ability to connect your Meta Muse to use this for coding tasks which has worked really well so far you can try it out by copying the promp for agent on the website. Two ways you can use it today is the Mac app and the cli. Honest limitations are documented, happy to take any questions. Repo: https://github.com/grist-ai/grist npm CLI: npm install -g grist-ai

projects.title: [开源推荐] LR-Agent：给 AI 编程补丁做连续维护压力测试
projects.author: LLR6

github.name: LLR6/LR-agent
github.description: 可验证的本地 AI Agent 实验台：隔离候选、工具执行、策略消融与未来演化压力测试。

projects.summary: LR-Agent 是一个 Python 编程 Agent 实验项目，关注“当前测试通过的补丁，遇到后续维护变化会怎样”。它在隔离工作区生成候选补丁并执行验证，再让仓库连续经历依赖、接口或功能变化，每一代重放原始检查，输出补丁生存和维护成本报告。适合对编程 Agent、软件测试和维护实验感兴趣的开发者；完整运行需要配置兼容模型接口。 亮点 候选补丁在独立工作区中修改与验证，比较依据包含实际命令退出码。 连续维护实验中，后一代继承前一代的代码，便于观察累积变化造成的回归。 原有测试和长期约束会被重新执行，保留可检查的实验工作区和报告。 提供 CLI、Web 界面、最小示例以及研究边界说明，欢迎提交最小反例。 目前是研究型工程原型。合成场景和维护成本指标属于启发式实验，不能证明现实未来正确性，也没有据此声称领先其他 Agent。完整实验会调用模型，时间与费用随配置而变化。 项目自荐，希望收集安装体验、维护场景设计和报告解释方面的反馈。

projects.summary: 一句话分工： Herdr = 让 Agent 一直跑着、并排管理 Herduck = 记住一项活的目标 / 做到哪了 / 卡在哪 / 下一步，以及能翻回去的记录 互补，不替代。 官网 https://www.herduck.com 仓库 https://github.com/wenhanweime/herduck 上一帖 https://www.v2ex.com/t/1243952 GitHub Discussion （求反馈） https://github.com/wenhanweime/herduck/discussions/2 也在 Herdr Show and tell 发了一帖： https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr/discussions/4822 已有能力（还很早期）： - 工作 / Agents / 项目 / 会话 四个入口 - 相关对话尽量自动收拢到同一项活（可配置；也有偏本地关键词的路径） - Agent 会话自动起名；闲置一段时间可睡眠，释放内存 - herduck 命令让 Agent 读 / 更新工作计划 - 兼容 Claude Code / Codex / OpenCode / Pi / Gemini CLI / Cursor ；快捷键尽量跟 Herdr 对齐 本轮对外动作： - 仓库 homepage 指向 herduck.com - README 首屏补了官网链接和 Demo 占位 - 开了反馈 Discussion 仍已知的坑：源码安装需要 Rust / Zig / just ； macOS 需按文档重签名；早期不稳定点欢迎 Issue 。 求反馈： 1. 自动把对话归到同一项活，误伤多不多？ 2. 闲着就睡的阈值是否合理？ 3. 和纯 Herdr 并用时，哪些界面显得重复？ 安装最短路径： ``` git clone https://github.com/wenhanweime/herduck.git cd herduck just install herduck ``` 欢迎 star / Issue / 一起维护。给 Herdr 用户补「隔天接得上」，不是抢跑 Agent 那一层。 少数派长文已投稿待审（大白话版）：多开 Agent 几天后，最烦的是隔天接不上

Kio is based on polymorphic lambda calculus with higher-kinded types. Kio has type-driven macros (elaborators) and it can statically check asserted equivalences using a normalizer. Kio is a minimalistic language. It doesn't have built-in effectful functions and it doesn't even have built-in string or numeric types. Instead programs declare the capabilities they need and the host supplies them. projects.title: Show HN: tokentape.io – A Bloomberg-style market terminal for the token economy
projects.author: turingfeel
projects.summary: I wanted a way to track the token economy the way you'd follow equities or other financial markets: who's gaining market share, who's cutting prices, which new models are actually getting used. OpenRouter publishes a lot of the live data, but it's spread across various pages and endpoints, mostly as snapshots, so I started collecting and organizing it. The historical data was the hard part. OpenRouter doesn't publish an archive, so I rebuilt it from the Wayback Machine. I indexed about 2 million archived OpenRouter URLs, downloaded close to a million captures, and wrote parsers for every page and API format the site has used since 2023. Most of the work was in reconciling the disparate feeds of data, iteratively building up and infilling the dataset via derivation. Hopefully some people might find it useful.

projects.title: Show HN: Ciao – Control coding agents from your phone
projects.author: bojanstef
projects.summary: Hi HN, I built Ciao to solve problems I was experiencing: 1. Connecting to a new host should be as seamless as possible. I SSH a lot nowadays, and I find the key sharing across devices cumbersome. 2. I get annoyed by setting up insert-your-favorite VPN on new machines. They're all great. I don't want to think about them. 3. There's a lot of harnesses: Claude Code and Codex now have decent mobile push notifications but what about Pi or xyz-shiny-new harness? The harness is another tool that should be abstracted out. 4. I want a single application that has the big picture of all of my agents. Tmux and Herdr are great but they don't have an overview of all my connected machines' agents. --- With Ciao you curl|sh the daemon --> run ciao pair --> point your phone's camera at the QR code --> and you're connected. It uses iroh for accountless and E2EE connection. There's an optional relay server for APNS which too is E2EE. One of my favorite aspects of agentic-engineering is being able to just have a lot of fun with programming. Among many features, I built a visually pleasing toggle between terminal-mode and native-chat-mode. If you install Ciao, come back here and tell me what you think. --- Full transparency: this is a repost from yesterday, it was a massive day in AI.

projects.title: Show HN: Perspica – A semantic diff for reviewing code
projects.author: sshah03

github.name: sshah03/perspica
github.description: Review code changes by what they do, not line by line.

projects.summary: I started using this a little over half a year ago to help me navigate through some large AI coded PRs people were submitting, because I felt like if I looked at the PR on Github I would just auto pass it through because I didn't want to deal with it. Thought I'd clean it up and share it in case this style of review was useful to anyone else. Obviously it relies on an LLM run to get true semantic groupings of what changes were done, and why, but can also be used without an LLM to get more mechanical groupings/group names of changes made, along with the right order to view them in. The manual tree-sitter parsed analysis is deliberately conservative for now, but if people want to avoid the LLM analysis I can spend more time on that. You can use it for other peoples PRs, or for your own when you've relied heavily on Claude Code or Codex for that particular PR. If the change came from your own Claude Code or Codex session, it reads your prompts and marks which changes you asked for and which the agent decided on its own as well to help you validate it before submitting for others to review. Demo video done on some public project PRs is in the repo; for a look at what it looks like when it pulls in information about your own claude/codex sessions you'll have to use it yourself for now, but I'll work on getting an example of that up soon so people can take a look before spending time to get this to work locally for themselves. I also added support for perforce style side by side diffing because I always kind of liked it, though it's not quite as slick yet.

projects.title: 【资源自荐】Agent Needs：免注册收集 AI Agent 工作流真实卡点的小站

projects.summary: 做了一个早期需求收集站 Agent Needs，想先弄清楚开发者实际使用 AI Agent 时卡在哪里，再决定值得做什么工具。目前处于免费、开放的需求发现阶段，没有支付或售卖功能，也还没有真实用户需求验证。 如果你在使用或开发 Agent，欢迎提交一次真实经历： 当时要完成什么任务？ 具体卡在了哪一步？ 现在怎么绕过去，出现频率和影响有多大？ 可以直接在网页填写，不需要注册、邮箱或钱包。也提供 POST /api/v1/needs 接口，便于在获得操作者授权后，从工作流提交问题。必填字段是 task（10–500 字符）、problem（20–2000 字符）和 consent: true；可选补充 agent、workaround、frequency、impact、buyer。 提交内容先进入私有待审核队列，审核后可能公开展示；提交前页面会提示这一点。请只提交有权分享的信息，不要填写密码、API Key、客户隐私或公司机密。目前这只是收集和验证需求的实验，不承诺每个问题都会获得解决。 欢迎 Agent 开发者、自动化工作流使用者体验并反馈。此投稿由 AI 助手协助整理并代为发布。

projects.summary: MSL Desktop：医学联络官的日常工作台 项目自荐。MSL（医学联络官）的日常工作会留下很多零散信息：拜访时专家的一句话、研究项目的新进展、等待回复的问题、下次交流要准备的资料。记录散开以后，后续跟进很容易丢掉背景。 MSL Desktop 把专家交流、临床与非临床项目、任务、等待事项、日历和资料放在一起。设计时坚持一句话：不要让记录工作变成比工作本身更耗费时间的事。 使用时可以先留下一句原话，让秘书结合已有项目准备整理建议；用户可以修改、暂缓或确认，确认后再写入正式事项。用户对方向的调整会纳入后续整理。AI 嵌在这些步骤中，日常工作仍由用户决定。 专家交流可以积累为带来源的洞察，后续拜访能够找回背景。 项目问答、简报和周月报依据工作台已有记录起草，使用前仍需核对。 工作数据与安装目录分开保存，支持本地备份及云盘文件夹同步，关联目录中的源文件只读。 新版微信入口中，普通文字直接记入收件箱；发送「召唤秘书」才打开五项菜单，可发起全局整理、生成每日简报、查看进度与待确认数量，或退出菜单。接收电脑需联网并运行工作台，建议仍在桌面端确认。 技术栈为 Tauri 2、Rust、Svelte 和 SQLite。当前提供 Windows x64 安装包，macOS 版本正在开发。 使用边界：远程模型需要配置自己的 API Key，相关记录和资料会发送给所选服务商，并产生该服务商的调用费用。请遵守所在机构的数据与合规要求；生成内容需人工核对，不用于自动作出临床决策。微信账号接入情况以微信服务返回为准。

projects.title: [FormulaAI] 更新：新增 VBA 代码生成 + 免登录使用
projects.author: clarecui
projects.summary: 接上次上线帖，FormulaAI 做了一次比较大的更新。 产品地址： https://formulaai.net —— 新增功能 1. VBA 代码生成 用自然语言描述需求，AI 生成可直接运行的 VBA 代码。 比如"给当前工作表加个按钮，点击后自动汇总所有部门的销售额"，返回的代码可以直接复制粘贴到 Excel 宏编辑器里运行。 实现思路：把用户需求 + 当前表格的列名/表头信息传给 DeepSeek ，prompt 里约束了 VBA 语法规范、必须加注释、变量声明等，输出质量还不错。 2. 免登录使用 之前必须登录才能用，现在匿名用户也能直接体验。上传文件、描述需求、AI 处理，全程不需要注册。只有保存历史记录、开通会员时才需要登录。 技术上就是把"必须登录"的中间件去掉，给匿名用户也分配了一个临时额度。 —— 为什么做这两个功能 上线后收集反馈，这两个需求出现频率最高： "能不能给我代码，我自己改" → VBA 生成 ​ "能不能不注册就用" → 免登录 本质上都是用户想要更多掌控感：一个掌控数据处理方式，一个掌控个人信息。 —— 目前完整功能列表 生成表格：描述需求 → AI 生成完整 Excel ​ 编辑表格：上传文件 → 描述需求 → AI 修改 → diff 对比 → 确认下载 ​ 生成 VBA：描述需求 → AI 生成 VBA 代码 ​ 免登录体验：打开即用 ​ 隐私保护：文件本地解析，不上传服务器，处理完即删 技术栈：Next.js + DeepSeek API + SheetJS + Supabase + Cloudflare Pages + 虎皮椒（微信支付） —— 数据情况 上线到现在，免登录这个改动对新用户转化率提升比较明显，具体数字等再观察一段时间。 VBA 生成功能用的人还不多，可能是因为会用 VBA 的用户本身就少，但用过的反馈都还不错。 —— 接下来的计划 继续看反馈决定优先级，目前在考虑的方向： 支持更多文件格式（ CSV 、Google Sheets ） ​ 批量处理多个文件 ​ 导出处理历史记录 有什么建议欢迎评论区交流。

projects.title: Show HN: Hypercolor – Epic RGB lighting control for everything
projects.author: hyperb1iss
projects.summary: Light it up with Hypercolor , a new RGB lighting orchestration platform for all platforms and all devices. Effects are web pages (or glsl), rendered by an internal browser GPU accelerated all the way to the pixels. It's pure rust from the Servo renderer to the WASM UI. Comes with 40+ effects, supports ambilight, display faces, system monitoring, screen casting, and audio. Device support is pretty good but it's early and this is where we need the most help! You can find the full support matrix on the site, and there is also an OpenRGB bridge as a fallback. There's support for a few unique devices too like the Ableton Push 2 and ROLI Blocks. My favorite thing about this engine is the ability to create multiple effect zones and manage them independently! My whole house runs on it now. projects.title: AI Agent 的能力上限由模型决定，行为的可靠性与一致性由规则体系决定。
projects.author: tntin
projects.summary: 在使用 AI Agent 开发项目的过程中，我的一些理解 以及 推荐一下我开发的工具： ## 一句话总结版 模型决定能力上限，规则决定底线与一致性； Agent 规则文档是给智能体用的长期执行手册，拒绝直接抄模板，聚焦你反复遇到的问题，写死动作与验收标准，约束长任务每一步的判断。 ## 正文 | 维度 | 模型层 | 规则层 | |---|---|---| | **决定因素** | 理解、推理、创作、工具调用的能力边界 | 目标拆解、工具白名单、权限审批、可验证性 | | **典型约束** | 成本与速度（复杂任务需大模型，简单判断用小模型） | 把“必须”“禁止”变成程序必经节点，而非仅靠模型复述 | | **失败模式** | “能做但太贵太慢” | “写了却跳过”“自由发挥导致乱写” | 模型负责“能做什么”，规则负责“按什么流程做、做到什么程度算完成”。两者缺一不可：没有模型，Agent 没有能力；没有规则，Agent 没有纪律。 ### 一：能力上限 模型的能力边界直接决定了 Agent 能完成的任务类型。但关键在于，**不是所有任务都需要调用最大最强的模型**——复杂规划用大模型，简单判断用小模型，这既是成本控制，也是速度优化的必然选择。 ### 二：规则的本质 “规则决定会不会乱写” 规则层的核心机制包括： - **目标与边界**：通过任务拆解、工具白名单、权限审批点，将模型的“自由发挥”约束为“按流程执行”；； - **避免“写了却跳过”** ：把“必须”“禁止”等约束变成程序必经节点，而非仅靠模型在提示词中复述——这是规则从“建议”升级为“强制”的关键。 ### 三：Agent 规则文档是长期执行手册 Agent 规则文档的定位是**权重极高的长期持久提示词**，接近系统提示词，在长任务的每一步持续约束 Agent 的判断，一般用 Markdown 编写。这与“临时 prompt”有本质区别：临时 prompt 解决单次交互，规则文档解决**跨任务、跨会话的一致性**。 系统提示词是 Agent 的“核心规则基石”，负责定义模型的角色定位、应答规范与能力边界，为全程对话定下基础框架。规则文档正是这一理念的具体载体。 ### 四：好规则写动作与验收，坏规则写价值观 这是最具操作性的判断： - **坏规则**：写抽象形容词（“回答要有审美”“方案要高级”），无法让 Agent 落地判断； - **好规则**：从日常反复踩坑的真实工作问题出发，写清楚**遇到这类问题时下一步要执行什么动作，以及怎么验收结果**。 一个完整的 Agent 规范应定义角色、场景、输入、输出、可做/不可做、工具边界、人工确认、失败处理、验收标准，把可观察的 Agent 行为验收清楚。可落地、可校验，才是好规则的检验标准。 ### 五：知识库工具 [knloop]( https://knloop.com) 是一个 Agent 原生知识库，让你的规则成为 Agent 的长期执行手册——你定义动作与验收标准，Agent 在每一步对照执行，全程可审计、可回滚。 [knloop]( https://knloop.com) 让你把规范、SOP 、QA 、复盘写成持久化的 .md 文档，Agent 通过 MCP 读取，按你的规范执行，产出写回同一个库。

projects.summary: 大家好，我是 ThunderTalk 的作者，想自荐一个完全在本机运行的 macOS 语音工具。 ThunderTalk 是一个 MIT 开源、免费的 Mac 语音工具箱，所有模型都在 Apple 芯片上本地运行，录音和文字不离开电脑。它对中文、英文和中英混说做了专门优化。 主要功能： 语音输入：在任何 App 里按快捷键说话，松开就把文字粘贴到光标处。可选 Qwen3-ASR、SenseVoice、Parakeet、MOSS 等多个本地模型。 录音转文字：拖入音频或视频，输出带时间戳的文稿，可以区分说话人，导出 TXT、Markdown、SRT、VTT 或 JSON。 文字转语音：VoxCPM2、IndexTTS-2.5、Kokoro 三个引擎，内置 14 个音色（影视解说、纪录片旁白、新闻主播、Vlog、播客等风格），每个音色都可以先试听。 声音克隆：录 5 到 15 秒自己的声音，就能用它朗读任意文字。 翻译（可选）：用 SeamlessM4T v2 边说边译。 几个实测数字（M3 Max）：VoxCPM2 和 IndexTTS 约为实时速度，Kokoro 在 CPU 上约为实时的 4 倍；生成的语音用独立的识别模型转回文字比对，中英文错误率为 0–3.4%。 安装：brew install --cask realallensong/tap/thundertalk，或从 GitHub Releases 下载。需要 Apple 芯片的 Mac，macOS 15 及以上。

projects.title: Show HN: SFML – A markup language for software factories, Terraform for agents
projects.author: mcwhittemore
projects.summary: SFML is a language specification for defining software factories. You can think of it as Terraform for your software development lifecycle. I started from a language spec to help think through both how a factory is defined and how a conforming runner processes it. The push to do this comes from leading teams where everyone has a unique coding setup, which results in different agentic coding processes. People also want to work together on improving that process. Right now they do it through shared AGENTS.md files and, in some cases, committed Claude and Codex settings files. But it hasn't led to the collaboration we all want. SFML is my attempt to help make that happen. My core bet is that the Unix philosophy applies to agentic coding just like it applies to all other coding: small steps with clear inputs and outputs, composed together to get results. Most agentic setups lean on ever-growing AGENTS.md files that quickly become unwieldy. Breaking them up helps, but then the agent has to rediscover and reassemble your process on every run. I'm pretty early in thinking about what SFML should be, and I'm hoping to hear from dissenters and collaborators here today, to push me to think more critically and to show me directions I haven't imagined yet. Thanks in advance for your feedback.

projects.title: Show HN: Relay – a harness for AI coding agents that recover and verify
projects.author: rsathwik07
projects.summary: I'm tired of AI coding agents which are good for 30 seconds and then completely fail on the slightest hiccup: a failing test, a temporarily unavailable dependency, an incorrect assumption. Sometimes I end up having to babysit these agents anyway. Relay is a harness for coding agents which takes advantage of the fact that agents are often good at doing something slightly wrong, and not so good at doing something correctly and completely. Relay repeatedly tries the task and on each failure, uses the output to find a better way to do it. It does this by running the task in a loop: attempt the task, run the checks in a fresh sandbox, on failure read the error and retry instead, until the checks pass. What it learned from a run is retained, so that it doesn't repeat the same mistake, and when the checks eventually pass, it will ship the change as a normal git PR - no hidden state, no magic, the diff is human readable. A few specifics: - it runs locally, is free, and doesn't require an account to run the local agent - it uses a top-tier model to plan/review, and cheaper models to actually write code (for cost reasons) - happy to discuss why this is a good idea and why it isn't - the checks run in an isolated sandbox for each task, rather than "trusting" the agent - currently supports [list actual models/integrations - Opus 5.5, GPT-6, etc] - there's a paid tier for running this unattended across multiple repos with shared sandbox minutes, the actual agent is free. It's not magic, it's not AGI, and it will fail badly on some problems. Would appreciate feedback, particularly from people who've deployed agents unattended and found that they don't actually work, or have had to build substantial tooling around them to get useful results.

projects.summary: 想和大家分享一款我最近刚刚上线的手机阅读小工具——DrNews。 []() 平时大家应该也经常在 GitHub 上看各种开源项目的 README、技术文档，或者追《科技爱好者周刊》（比如阮一峰老师的 weekly 等）。但说实话，直接用手机浏览器看 Markdown 经常字太小、排版生硬、偶尔图片还加载不出来，阅读体验挺折腾的。 DrNews 就是为了解决这个问题做出来的。它界面做得很干净，没有任何乱七八糟的广告或干扰 （呵呵，仅在阅读页显示一次广告）。你可以把它当成一个“Markdown 专属的舒适阅读器”： 它可以把你关注的 GitHub 仓库或文件夹同步到手机里，随时离线看。字体、字号、护眼背景（比如舒服的复古沙棕色、纯黑模式）都能随便调，读起来就像在看一本排版精致的小杂志； 遇到长文章时间不够时，它有智能 AI 摘要，点一下就能帮你用中文或英文总结出核心要点，快速抓重点； 通勤路上或眼睛累了的时候，还能直接用语音朗读听文章，它会自动过滤掉代码块和网址，听感很顺畅； 遇上特别长的文档，点一下“目录”就能快速跳转到想看的小节，非常省心。 如果你平时也喜欢在手机上读 《科技爱好者周刊》等 Markdown 文章或技术资讯，推荐你试试看，欢迎反馈！

projects.title: Show HN: Aether: Check and fix web accessibility issues from your coding agent
projects.author: samy_patra
projects.summary: Hi, HackerNews! I'm Samy, co-founder of Allchemy Labs. We built Aether, an MCP server that enables engineers to check for, understand, and fix web accessibility issues all from their IDE. Your preferred coding agent can leverage Aether to open a webpage, scan it using axe-core and return a short, prioritized list of violations along with code fixes or guidance. Every suggested fix is re-tested in a real browser before you see it, and once you apply it, your agent can re-scan the page to verify it worked. You never need to open a browser, use multiple tools, or be an expert in WCAG criteria. Aether uses our own custom ontology architecture to provide grounded insights to any WCAG violations the scanner finds. Every WCAG technique the engine cites must pass our quality gate. Specifically, it must satisfy the violated success criterion, apply to that kind of element, and remediate that axe rule. If nothing passes, our engine will abstain rather than guess. We compared Aether against standalone coding agent on its own (Opus 5, 30 anonymized live sites, 111 targets). While the results were mixed we have published the results especially calling out specific wins and improvement opportunities for our insight engine. Read the study here: https://allchemylabs.substack.com/p/we-tested-our-own-access... Try Aether today, no signup needed. npx -y @allchemylabs/aether-wcag-scanner (any MCP client: Claude Code, Cursor, Codex…) Claude Code plugin: /plugin marketplace add https://github.com/allchemylabs/claude-plugins.git then /plugin install aether-wcag-scanner@allchemylabs Without a key you get the browser scan, local template fixes and verification. A free beta key adds the cloud engine: https://beta.allchemylabs.ai/?src=hn Feedback from people who have used accessibility scanners and/or suggestion engines would be highly valuable to us, as we aim to build a tool that solves real problems and makes people's lives easier. Happy to answer any questions and hope to hear from you. Note: Right now Aether only checks WCAG 2.1 AA. Sites behind bot protection (e.g. Cloudflare challenges) return a "blocked" result instead of a fake scan, so point it at localhost or staging.

I'm not sure how to fix it, but this is my attempt at building something fun to get the conversation started. Some details: - Prices come from Hanson's LMSR (logarithmic market scoring rule). - You can sell and/or rebuy at any time - There's a public leaderboard that ranks traders by P&L. - It uses an in-app currency called reputation. It can't be converted to money. - Bots can trade too, and they're encouraged. If you can get an LLM to predict the market, that would be cool! There's a public HTTP API with an OpenAPI spec (/api/v1/openapi.json). - Comments are pseudonymous, like on OpenReview ("User k3xm"), but they show the author's position. - There's also a 2D map of all submissions: https://acceptodds.com/map How would you extend this? projects.title: Show HN: Meanwhile Map – what else was happening in the world at the same time
projects.author: 29b
projects.summary: When reading a history book, I sometimes have a hard time internalizing when the events are taking place. Sure, I know the dates, but it takes a bit of effort to put them in a broader context, to understand where in history they belong. What usually helps is to put them in relation to other contemporaneous events. To play around with this, I've made Meanwhile Map. You select a date and a time window, then scroll around the world map to see a list of contemporaneous events. For example, yes, the Mughal Empire was founded by Babur in the 1520s, but it paints a different picture in my head when I see that this roughly coincides with Cortés' capture of Tenochtitlan, or that it's close to the Siege of Vienna. Example link: https://meanwhilemap.com/#y=1520&m=1&span=120&off=founded,pe... On the technical side, the app is a single static web page. It uses Wikidata for data (via SPARQL) and OpenHistoricalMap to show the events on the political map of the time. It's open source ( https://github.com/ea/meanwhilemap/tree/main ), vibe coded as an experiment. All processing is client-side, and no data is tracked other than simple visitor counts.

projects.title: Show HN: Orrery, a Three.js solar system visualization powered by real NAIF data
projects.author: rybosome
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm excited to share a personal project that I've put a lot of love into. This is Orrery[0], a Three.js-based visualization of our solar system. It allows the positions of the major bodies to be played and scrubbed through the years 1950 - 2050, with optional orbit path displays and various other visualization options. The data comes from NAIF SPICE - a framework and set of open-source data kernels containing highly detailed space geometry data. I was inspired to set out on this project when learning that NAIF SPICE, originally written in Fortran and C, lacks highly standardized JavaScript bindings. There are great Python (SpiceyPy) and Rust (Anise) bindings, among other languages, but nothing for JavaScript. So, I developed tspice[1] to wrap the CSPICE library. It uses the Native API when running in Node, and an Emscripten binding around CSPICE when running in the browser. It uses a standardized backend abstraction that the runtime swaps in depending on which context its invoked with. tspice offers an API that is meant to be a near-literal translation of the C APIs, along with higher-level functionality in separate namespaces. It also offers web conveniences like a dedicated web worker client (calculations can be intensive, you don't want them on your render thread) and caching. tspice only wraps a subset of the CSPICE library, but it was enough that I wanted to build a simple visualization tool to test it. Eventually the visualization testbed became refined enough that it felt compelling on its own. Although this is a hobby project, I'd love to hear suggestions and feedback on either Orrery or the underlying tspice library. If there are any folks in the planetary science community in particular who might be interested in tspice, please let me know if there are features that would make this more useful for you. One feature I love is the ability to generate a share URL of a particular viewer state that you like. I'd really love to see any states that people find especially cool! One of my favorite views is this one[2]. Thanks for taking a look! [0] Orrery repo: https://github.com/rybosome/orrery [1] tspice repo: https://github.com/rybosome/tspice [2] favorite orrery view: https://orrery.ryboso.me/dVPLbtswEPwX9qoIol4UdWtaB22RNEbsoii...

github.description: AI-assisted localization for Unreal Engine 5.6–5.8: translate with your own AI (Claude, GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, local Ollama), auto-validated, reviewed in-editor

projects.summary: 这是 LocHub 作者的自荐，文字由 AI 辅助整理。 LocHub 是一个 Unreal Engine 5.6–5.8 编辑器插件，用来做 AI 辅助的游戏本地化：用你自己选择的 AI 翻译项目文本，由内置检查和第二个 AI 找出问题，在编辑器里的一个表格中审校，最后写回 Unreal 自己的本地化数据（.archive、编译后的 .locres）。它不替代 Unreal 的本地化系统，随时可以停用。 从 1.2.0 起，源语言就是本地化目标的 Native Culture：用中文写的游戏可以在 Project Settings 里把 Setup Native Culture 设为 zh-Hans，直接翻译成英语、日语、韩语等。 能做什么 自带密钥接入 Claude、OpenAI、Gemini、DeepSeek、Grok，或任何 OpenAI 兼容接口（Ollama、LM Studio、vLLM 等）。使用本地模型时，文本不离开你的电脑。 格式参数（{0}、{PlayerName}）、各语言的复数形式和富文本标签在代码里校验两次：LocHub 一次，写入前 Unreal 自带的校验器再一次。有错的译文无法通过审校，手动也不行。 可选的第二个 AI 担任评审，检查含义、术语和语气，按严重程度标注问题并给出修改建议。 每条文本带上下文翻译：来源资产或 C++ 文件、开发者备注、同一界面已翻译的文本、项目简介和风格指南。 术语表与禁止翻译词、UI 长度检查、导出 XLIFF / CSV 给人工译者。 运行前估算费用，并可设置花费上限（Max USD）。人工修改永远不会被 AI 覆盖。 使用边界 源码公开，采用 Business Source License 1.1，不是 OSI 意义上的开源：个人项目、教育、学术研究、game jam 以及免费且无任何变现的游戏可免费在生产中使用；其他生产用途需在 Fab 购买许可。每个版本发布四年后转为 Apache 2.0。 在 Windows 上测试过；需要 Node.js 22.11 或更高版本。

projects.summary: 自荐一个刚开源的论文阅读器 PaperFold。我是作者 Xia Chen，目前在 TUM 做人机对齐方向的博士后研究。 读论文时，经常需要来回确认一段话在整篇论证中的位置。我做了一个可以逐层折叠、展开的阅读界面：先把论文缩成章节地图，再展开关心的部分，直到看到每个原文段落。 项目及缩放演示： 免安装体验： 阅读器有五档：全文、逐字摘取的关键句、要点及理由、一句话提要、章节主题地图。前两档使用作者原文，后三档由模型生成，以不同字体区分。缩放时，保留下来的词会移动到新位置；也可以只展开一个段落，其余部分继续折叠。提问后的回答会链接到所引用的段落。 Python 后端解析 arXiv 的 HTML，浏览器前端负责阅读和缩放；代码采用 Apache-2.0 许可。生成新论文需要该论文有 arXiv HTML 版本，并连接一个模型。生成后的论文可导出成独立 HTML 文件。 体验页提供数学、机器学习、医学等八个领域的论文，均标注了作者及 Creative Commons 许可，无需注册或配置模型即可体验阅读。AI 生成的提要仍可能出错，可以随时展开原文核对。 目前是早期版本，欢迎反馈解析失败的论文，以及长文阅读时的缩放、定位问题。

projects.summary: 每天一杯瑞幸，取餐时总会瞄一眼杯贴上的号码。某天意识到这其实是个每天免费开一次的数字盲盒：可能是 888 ，可能是顺子，可能正好是生日。但喝完杯子一扔，号码就没了。 所以给自己做了个收集册，叫「杯号」：000–999 一千个格子，每喝一杯，拍一下杯贴，点亮一格。 ![]( https://beihao.app/promo/recruit-2026-10/01-photo-to-sticker.jpg) 拍完几秒：认出品牌和取餐号，把号码贴纸从照片里"撕"下来、拉正、包白边，整杯也从背景里抠出来。每一格都必须用真实照片点亮，不能手填。 ![]( https://beihao.app/promo/recruit-2026-10/02-number-book.jpg) ## 想找什么样的人 瑞幸、星巴克是我自己天天喝的，已经比较稳。品牌表里还收了 50 多家，但每家杯贴长得五花八门，我手里样张很少，**尤其想找常喝 Manner 、M Stand 、Peet's 、喜茶、奈雪的朋友**。 你只需要：平时喝东西时顺手拍一下杯贴。认错了、卡住了、哪里难用，直接在帖子里回复就行。 ## 怎么加入 iPhone 上直接打开 TestFlight 公开链接（会先引导装苹果官方的 TestFlight ）： https://testflight.apple.com/join/pGpDNz5K 不想直接装的话，也可以先在 https://beihao.app/beta/ 填 4 道题（ 1 分钟），填完同样给链接，顺便帮我统计一下大家常喝什么。

projects.title: 开源 Bibo：成本极低，内置笔记、文件、任务和日历的 personal agent
projects.author: Peiiii
projects.summary: 我把 Bibo 开源了，MIT 协议。先说最想做好的三件事： 1. **成本极低。** 日常使用不需要常驻电脑，也不用一直开着 Linux 容器。只有需要运行代码时，才启动沙箱。 2. **内置个人管理工具。** 笔记、文件、任务和日历都有专门的界面。你可以直接查看、编辑和管理，也可以让 AI 来做。 3. **开源，可以自己部署。** 用自己的 Cloudflare 账号和模型 API Key ，数据存在自己的部署里，代码也可以自己改。 GitHub：[Peiiii/bibo]( https://github.com/Peiiii/bibo) 在线体验：[app.bibo.bot]( https://app.bibo.bot) 我希望它能成为每天都用得上的 personal agent 。想到什么可以随手记，需要做的事可以放进任务和日历，资料可以整理成文件；这些内容长期留着，之后还能接着用。 下面把界面都放出来。截图来自实际运行的 Bibo ，销售、订单和日程内容都是示例数据。 ### 概览 打开就能看到笔记、任务、日程和待处理信息。 ![Bibo 概览]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/v2ex-2026-10-04/bibo-overview.jpg) ### 对话 让 Bibo 阅读销售数据、总结重点，也可以让它继续整理报告和安排后续工作。 ![Bibo 对话与报告]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/v2ex-2026-10-04/bibo-chat.jpg) ### 笔记 笔记是可以直接编辑的 Markdown 文档。你自己写，或者让 Bibo 帮你整理，都能继续修改。 ![Bibo 笔记]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/v2ex-2026-10-04/bibo-notes.jpg) ### 文件 有独立的文件目录，可以打开、编辑文件。这里展示的是整理好的订单 CSV 。 ![Bibo 文件]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/v2ex-2026-10-04/bibo-files.jpg) ### 任务 任务有独立列表和详情，可以管理完成状态、优先级、描述和时间。分析出来的建议，可以接着变成待办。 ![Bibo 任务]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/v2ex-2026-10-04/bibo-tasks.jpg) ### 日历 日程直接显示在日历里，可以自己添加，也可以让 Bibo 帮你安排。 ![Bibo 日历]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/v2ex-2026-10-04/bibo-calendar.jpg) ### 收件箱 需要你关注和确认的内容放在这里，可以查看并标记处理。 ![Bibo 收件箱]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/v2ex-2026-10-04/bibo-inbox.jpg) ### 需要运行代码时，按需启动 Linux 沙箱 例如，用 Python 清洗订单表，去掉重复行，生成新的 CSV 和说明文档。下面这次演示实际运行了 Python ，文件已保存。 普通对话和个人管理功能由 Cloudflare Workers / Durable Objects 承载，文件保存在 R2 。需要运行 Python 、Shell 等代码时，才用 Cloudflare Sandbox ，不必为了日常使用维持一台常驻电脑。 ![Bibo 运行 Python 整理订单]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/bibo-sandbox-execution.png) ### 手机端 手机上也能继续对话、查看和管理任务。 ![Bibo 手机对话]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/bibo-mobile-chat.png) ![Bibo 手机任务]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/bibo-mobile-tasks.png) 自己部署需要 Cloudflare Workers Paid 、R2 、Sandbox 和模型 API Key ，具体步骤在仓库 README 。实际费用由模型调用、存储和沙箱使用量决定。 欢迎试用，也欢迎提 Issue 或 PR 。想听听大家：你最希望 personal agent 帮你处理哪件日常小事？

projects.title: [我的搜索-桌面版] 一款呼出搜索工具，支持网站/文本类/插件
projects.author: zhuangjie
projects.summary: ## 使用场景 项目开发最开始解决的问题是收藏了很多网站/软件/一些小教程(后面可能用到)，通过按规则写好源放到 github 上得到订阅然软件负责递归解析出数据项来搜索，有内置订阅，可制作自己订阅（[教程]( https://github.com/My-Search/my-search) | [官方源仓库-参考]( https://github.com/My-Search/official-subscribe)），桌面版有**插件功能** ![image]( https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/18476305640/typora@master/uploads/2026/10/03/1791035519022.png) ## 使用 **桌面版（订阅数据+插件）：基于 Rust 开发 [my-search-desktop]( https://github.com/My-Search/my-search-desktop)** 原版（订阅数据）：油猴脚本应用 [mysearch]( https://greasyfork.org/zh-CN/scripts/457020-%E6%88%91%E7%9A%84%E6%90%9C%E7%B4%A2) ## 当前有哪些可用的插件 | 插件名 | 描述 | |---|---| | Pi Agent | Pi 编码代理 - 支持多项目、多模型、模型配置面板、插件管理、流式对话与工具调用 | | 文件搜索 | 在粘贴/拖入的文件夹里按名称搜索文件：一直扫描、边扫边显示，随时可停止；回车或点击用系统默认程序打开 | | 插件市场 | 浏览、安装、更新与卸载插件 | | 录屏与水印 | 屏幕录制（可选实时叠加水印），并给已有视频批量添加文字/图片水印，支持九宫格定位与水印预设 | | 截图 | 全局快捷键截图：框选区域、标注后复制到剪贴板，并在前台查看最近 7 天的截图 | | MayeLite 快速启动 | 把常用文件/文件夹拖进来固定，随时一键打开；支持分类、排序与拖拽整理 | | 百度翻译 | 使用百度翻译 AI 能力，支持 200+ 语言互译，输入文本即译 | | GitHub 文件上传 | 将文件上传到 GitHub 仓库，支持拖拽、粘贴、选择文件与图片压缩 | | 剪贴板历史 | 自动记录你复制过的文本与图片，按快捷键呼出即可搜索、复制、删除、收藏。收藏的条目永久保留、不会被上限淘汰或清空。监听在后台原生完成，不干扰系统剪贴板。 | | 待办清单 | 本地待办清单：增删改查、优先级、标签、截止日期、筛选统计与 JSON 导出导入 | | 资源监控 | 每 5 秒采样整机 CPU / 内存 / 网络，按程序聚合，用可缩放时间范围的趋势图展示占用最高的 Top 10——快速定位 CPU 莫名 100%、内存暴涨、异常上传的程序 | 插件支持调整窗口大小，关闭自动恢复再打开时仍会按之前调试的宽度显示。 ## 如何开发新插件 AI 开发提示词： ``` 软件主体： https://github.com/My-Search/my-search-desktop 插件市场： https://github.com/My-Search/my-search-plugin-market 参考下面仓库开发出 my-search-desktop 插件。 需要开发插件的功能：xxx ``` 开发的插件通过设置里的挂载安装即可进行调试，当前开放的接口可能不多，需要可提 issues; 开发的插件可声明是否跟随软件启动，使用后退出是否后台运行，可声明在主体软件上快捷键使即使插件停止仍可通过快捷键激活插件功能； 插件市场运作说明： 插件都是在[插件市场 github 仓库]( https://github.com/My-Search/my-search-plugin-market)里定时自动索引的,按规范开发好，将仓库通过插件市场仓库提 issues 我看到会放到 index.json 会自动索引； ## 关于环境变量 用于多插件配置复用：通过直接在软件写好环境变量配置，在插件中直接通过环境变量授权给插件使用

projects.title: 【资源自荐】把 AI 长文整理成中文听稿：开源工具箱与完整学习案例
projects.author: GODGOD126
projects.summary: 自荐一个中文长文转听稿的开源资源：长文节目工具箱，源码和中文说明。 适合手里已有 AI 长文、研究资料或学习笔记，希望整理后用文字转语音工具收听的人。可以在浏览器内生成听稿提示词、标出网址/表格/长段落等需要人工检查的位置，将朗读正文和来源备注分别导出 TXT。不用注册或密钥，不上传输入；也可以下载整个工具箱离线打开。 它不调用 AI、不生成语音，不自动核查事实，也不擅自删除原文。网址、数字、比较条件和不确定性可能就是资料的重要信息，不能为了“适合听”直接丢掉。另有一份纯文字的 listening-script Agent 技能，用于保留这些边界的改写。 完整中文案例：平均数与中位数，包含原创朗读稿、可复制提示词和来源/数值核查说明。例子为虚构教学数据。2026-10-04补充了一份8分17秒完整中文AI合成音频，附实际生成稿与计算核查；在Mac端生成，非iPhone录音或真机性能演示，没有学习效果测量。工具箱本身仍不生成语音。正文和示范可独立使用，不要求购买任何App。 我是作者 Ryan Zhu，也是「自听」MyListen 开发者。工具箱代码、原创示例和提示词以 MIT 许可开放，由 AI 辅助编写；免费资源与 App 的商业条款分别适用。这次只自荐这份可独立使用的中文资源，供周刊编辑判断。

projects.title: Show HN: AstroHelm – Use your phone camera to aim a telescope or telephoto lens
projects.author: HeavenFox
projects.summary: Hello HN! As an amateur astronomer living in New York City, finding objects in the night sky has always been a huge challenge. I thought about using the smartphone's gyroscope and magnetometer, but the accuracy left a lot to be desired. Then I learned about plate solving: given a picture of the sky, we can determine exactly where in the sky the camera was pointing by identifying the star pattern. This was a much better fit - as long as the phone and the optics are rigidly connected, we can repeatedly photograph the sky and determine the pointing direction with very high accuracy. A lot of work was done to design an algorithm that works reliably with smartphone cameras, which have limited light sensitivity and wider field of view which includes buildings and trees. I experimented a lot with machine learning, and to my surprise, traditional CV methods actually performed better at extracting stars from the image. The result is AstroHelm, an iOS and Android app that helps figure out where your telescope or camera is pointing, and guides you to the object of your choice. Just follow an arrow on screen, and the object will land right in your eyepiece or viewfinder. Everything happens on device, and no internet connection is required. AstroHelm is free to use and comes with beginner-friendly objects selected for each night. Optional one time purchases unlock more objects and advanced features, such as interoperability with other astronomy software. I am also proud to partner with astronomy clubs and organizations to offer free licenses for outreach. I hope AstroHelm can make it a little easier to discover the wonders of the night sky, and I look forward to your feedback!

projects.title: Show HN: A critical thinking site for kids and teens
projects.author: Critikid
projects.summary: In 2019, I was teaching science at an international school in Chiang Mai. One day before class, one of my Grade 7 students asked me about flat earth. He had heard the idea from Kyrie Irving and then spent the night on flat earth sites. We walked through the claims and I explained why those arguments failed. He listened with interest. I was glad he'd come to me. He hadn't made up his mind yet; he was just curious. But this made me wonder if teaching the course content I was teaching was enough. To be clear: I do think teaching facts is important. For example, when students learn about gravity, physics, and space, they're better prepared to see why flat earth arguments are wrong. The problem is we can't teach facts fast enough to combat the wide variety of misinformation and manipulation kids face on the internet every day. This is what got me thinking that kids need to learn how to evaluate claims and information across a wide range of topics. While we can't prepare them for every false or misleading claim they might encounter, we can give them tools to assess them. That eventually led my husband and I to build Critikid, a site for teaching kids and teens. We've been working on it for 3 years now! He does the technical work (design and coding) and I do the educational content creation. By now, there are 5 interactive courses for ages 5-18 on logical fallacies, media literacy, emotional intelligence, statistical reasoning, and formal logic. There are also worksheets and lesson plans. I often teach through stories, as stories make abstract critical thinking concepts concrete (and they're fun!) If you'd like to try it, all of the courses have a free first lesson. Are there any other topics that you think should be included in kids' critical thinking education that I've missed?

projects.title: Show HN: Our space game has a built-in RISC-V emulator that runs Linux
projects.author: nor-and-or-not
projects.summary: We're a tiny indie studio, all with a background in the demoscene and for about 3 years now we're developing a space planet terraforming game called SEEDS - Echoes Beneath the Sands. Our protagonist Naxiah is stranded on a small, desolated planet. You're working for an intergalactic distributor of seeds and terraforming equipment, to kickstart new planets in far away galaxies. You must deliver seeds and utilities to an unchartered region, but on your way, you crash on a small planet. Luckily, you have some equipment with you in the ship, so you're able to spawn a base and survive. But for how long? And is the planet really deserted..? :) Well, of course not, there are aliens and other space creatures. And of course, there's ROBO RB-23, which accompanies your adventure. The game is written in Object Pascal and uses our own game engine PasVulkan, our own physics engine, as well as our own RISC-V 64-bit emulator PasRISCV. We love to build stuff, a lot of these things are FOSS. The emulator is quite complete (even with RVV, but that's way too slow emulated to be useful) and runs a stock kernel (6.18.3 as of today). We're using Alpine Linux for our base distribution. All our in-game programs to interact with the planet are native RISC-V Linux programs. We also have our own (free and open source) scripting language POCA (class and prototyped based, JS/Lua inspired, which makes it quite easy for us to script things like HUD, animal behaviour, our story flow graph, etc. We have most of the wiring ready for players to be able to program and reshape and populate the whole planet in automation, although it's not our primary concept for the game (building stuff by hand, making the planet beautiful is also fun). As it's a normal Linux system, you'll be able to use Ruby, Python, or even Rust, C, C++, and Go to change and automate your world. We're also thinking of making a bunch of small games which you can play inside the game, in the base on a computer, on an arcade machine, or in the spaceship. And of course, it also runs DOOM. We already prototyped a small 2D space shooter and a small arcade game, both playable within the game. We also feature a table with hologram games to be played, e.g. chess and a certain block game. We also plan to make this hologram game engine available from the computer, which means, you'll even be able to program own hologram style games. We generally want to make the in-game computer more hackable in future, so that people can create and share their own little games. Currently, it's only a sandbox game (with beginnings of automation), to build stuff with our pre-made items. You can also assemble these to other, ready-made and shareable bigger items. This is the foundation for us to further develop survival and complete our story mode. Our game is still under active development, and we finally got our Steam page ready. We have tons of other things planned, but right now, it's more about polishing and quality for the Early Access. You can watch some videos and screenshots on our website. And we'd love to read your thoughts about his. It has been quite a ride, so far..

projects.summary: Hi HN, I been using LLMs for coding a lot and while they aren't awful at generating code they suck at debugging and spend endless tokens on a debugging loop. Eventually that frustrated me and I built a CLI that attempts to make AI debugging easier. How it works is any error you encounter you would run a simple command "paper run <cmd>" which would "capture" that error and log it in a incident_report and tell your agents.md that is the source of truth for the error. When you ask your agent to fix the error the agent will look at your incident_report and solve it. Once your done you can shelf your report. Currently the constraints are it does not prompt a LLM or call external APIs(only writes a local .md file), everything stays local, no background daemon and no third party packages. Thanks for reading. The npm package page is posted below if anyone is interested. https://www.npmjs.com/package/@varman96/paper

projects.title: Show HN: Keel – Give your agent a typed strategy language, not a trading account
projects.author: zferland
projects.summary: I’ve been using AI agents to build systematic strategies on Hyperliquid for over a year, and slowly built up a reliable system to represent, test and deploy strategies. Typically there are a few options 1) llm in the execution loop, ie it makes decisions and trades, but that is slow, inconsistent and hard to audit 2) you have an agent write all the code, backtest etc, but it makes tons of subtle mistakes with time series data and diff timeframe etc, and is often not reusing bits. There are some ways to improve this of course with right frameworks and setups. But its still hard to be confident in its correctness and its hard for you to verify quickly. With Keel we built a small typed language (DSL) to represent strategies. It uses a well defined set of components to build a DAG of steps, it carries types and clocks. This allows agents to build these strategies with a really fast feedback loop as they can be quickly validated and many common errors avoided. In a DAG its also easy to inspect intermediate results. Valid strategies are fingerprinted and the exact same artifact runs in backtesting and live. These strategies are also much easier for humans to verify as they are self describing components, and mostly linear to read and reason about. Still trying to improve the space of how many types of different strategies can be represented in this and still trying to improve how well LLMs go from natural language to strategy. A lot of the improvements come from just giving the agents better and faster tools and faster feedback loops.

In total in separated it into 4 rungs - easy, medium, hard and frontier. projects.title: Show HN: Breadcrumb, record everything on your mac + context manager for AI
projects.author: jv22222
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Justin. Breadcrumb records everything you do on your Mac (screen + meetings + AI transcripts + what you and your AI decided) and turns it into memory your AI can search. It's local and encrypted. You can also teach it rules by talking to it and it makes sure the right rules turn up in the right context. Works with Claude Code / Codex / Cursor / opencode. All of this is exposed to your AI as 30+ MCP tools (here's the definitions): https://innerloop.works/breadcrumb/mcp I started it in June because I wanted to understand what was going on with my AI dev work. Then it just kept growing as I jammed on it 10 hours a day for 3 months. I started by recording every screen so I could jump back to a moment and see what I'd been doing with the AI. Then I added MCP so the AI could search it. Then time tracking. Then meetings with transcripts and timestamped screenshots. After that I started feeding the data back in. At first it was just a few relevant memories in the prompt. Then I started adding rules and rules modules. Then I started recording the AI transcripts and all the other stuff the AI did (subagents, tools etc). I wanted a complete record so I could go back and see what the AI did and why. I found the more data the AI had the more useful it became. One example. I got off a zoom call with the team at the day job and said: "Review the meeting I just had, find all the bugs we discussed, and create JIRA tickets with screenshots." It read the transcript. Found every bug we mentioned, pulled the screens from the screen timeline, spun up my local server, diagnosed each bug, reviewed the code, created 14 tickets in JIRA with diagnosis and likely fixes, attached 12 screenshots as evidence, and created a nice Slack message to send to my colleagues. I never built a workflow for any of that. Claude had the meeting record, Breadcrumb tools, and rules I'd accumulated. It basically chained the steps together itself. My favorite thing about the system is observability of my own work as an AI developer. I can trace a bug all the way back to the first thing I said (or the first thing the AI did) that caused it. Then I can add a rule so it doesn't happen again. Anyway, my working system is simply Claude Desktop + Breadcrumb + Markdown. I find I don't need anything else. It's local software for one person. Local models for transcription and diarization. Data encrypted with SQLCipher and a passphrase. You can exclude any apps, websites, words and phrases. Breadcrumb itself only makes one network call which is a daily update check. (but of course your AI will use it and that is local or cloud depending on what you use). It runs cool about 12% of one core on average (M series mac has 8+). You can set it to just save OCR text or to save screenshots. If just OCR it's about 12mb day (a lot of telemetry, indexing etc). If you record screenshots on meetings it's about 120mb/hour (1 every 2 secs). It can also record screenshots of everything that's heavy at about 160mb/day. It does local classification/naming with ollama with Gemma 3 4B (2.5 GB). It's 100% free. There's no account you can just download and start using it. I'll monetize it via E2EE cloud sync and team sync. It's open beta. Just one developer working on it. Requires 16GB+ M Series Mac. Thanks for reading! https://innerloop.works/breadcrumb (homepage) https://innerloop.works/breadcrumb/download (direct download) https://innerloop.works/breadcrumb/mcp (mcp definition)

projects.title: Show HN: Web search engine built from the CommonCrawl corpus
projects.author: xoredev
projects.summary: Hello HN, I'm building an alternative web search engine. You can try the demo here: https://search.xorsoft.dev/ My goal was to reach 1% of Google's index. This is 4 billion pages across 33.5 million domains. I was inspired by the earlier attempts shared here: "Building a web search engine from scratch with 3B neural embeddings" [1] and "Crawling a billion web pages in just over 24 hours" [2]. I decided not to replicate them and instead used CommonCrawl corpus, built a pipeline, and threw the results into a classic full-text search index. First, I got my hands on a dedicated Hetzner server with 4x10TB HDDs. It allowed me to crunch CommonCrawl data and stay within my hobby budget. The backend is served from a similar "home-grade" server but with NVMe disks instead. The compressed index weighs just over 2TB because I cap content length at 4KB per page (p50=2.9KB, p99=46KB) to fit it on disk. I picked Rust for my project. After years of big data engineering on the JVM, Rust felt like a breath of fresh air. I ended up not using any special data processing libraries - the pipeline is relatively straightforward and runs without crashes. As for full-text search, tantivy was an obvious choice. It took some time to get single query latency down to an acceptable ~350ms, although concurrent requests quickly max out disk t/p at 6.1GB/s and latency starts to climb. The search algorithm is primitive by modern standards: top 1,000 candidates are retrieved using BM25 (text relevance signal) and then reranked with PageRank [3]. Turns out you can fit the whole internet in a single server rack. The challenge here, of course, is to keep it up to date, especially if you don't have unlimited (crawl) budget. Right now I'm looking for funding or sponsorship to get extra hardware. That would allow me to scale the project and keep it free to use. I can also periodically dump the index on HuggingFace for research purposes. Any suggestions are welcome. [1] https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44878151 [2] https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47117886 [3] https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/1076034.1076106

projects.title: [开源推荐] LR-Agent：给 AI 编程补丁做连续维护压力测试
projects.author: LLR6

github.name: LLR6/LR-agent
github.description: 可验证的本地 AI Agent 实验台：隔离候选、工具执行、策略消融与未来演化压力测试。

projects.summary: LR-Agent 是一个 Python 编程 Agent 实验项目，关注“当前测试通过的补丁，遇到后续维护变化会怎样”。它在隔离工作区生成候选补丁并执行验证，再让仓库连续经历依赖、接口或功能变化，每一代重放原始检查，输出补丁生存和维护成本报告。适合对编程 Agent、软件测试和维护实验感兴趣的开发者；完整运行需要配置兼容模型接口。 亮点 候选补丁在独立工作区中修改与验证，比较依据包含实际命令退出码。 连续维护实验中，后一代继承前一代的代码，便于观察累积变化造成的回归。 原有测试和长期约束会被重新执行，保留可检查的实验工作区和报告。 提供 CLI、Web 界面、最小示例以及研究边界说明，欢迎提交最小反例。 目前是研究型工程原型。合成场景和维护成本指标属于启发式实验，不能证明现实未来正确性，也没有据此声称领先其他 Agent。完整实验会调用模型，时间与费用随配置而变化。 项目自荐，希望收集安装体验、维护场景设计和报告解释方面的反馈。

projects.title: Show HN: Quiet – exploring when an AI assistant should intervene
projects.author: roger05
projects.summary: I’m Ruggiero, a CS student working on a research project about humanComputer interaction and AI. I built QUIET because I’ve been thinking about a problem with current AI interfaces: they usually either wait for an explicit prompt, or try to take over a task. I wanted to explore a different relationship between humans and AI: an assistant that can understand when to stay out of the way, when to point something out, when to teach, and when to act. I’ve built a small interactive demo of this idea. It’s obviously still very early, and I want to understand whether the interaction itself makes sense before trying to build the actual AI system behind it. The prototype is intentionally not AI-powered yet. The four examples are scripted so I can test the interaction itself before spending time building the underlying AI system. The idea is that the assistant can choose different levels/forms of intervention: * stay silent * point at something * explain / teach * do the task The important question for me isn’t whether an AI can perform these actions. Current systems can already do many of them. I’m trying to understand whether an assistant that decides when and how much to intervene is actually useful. I’d particularly like feedback on: * Did the interventions feel helpful or annoying? * Would you want an assistant to behave this way? * When would you prefer it to teach you rather than do something for you? * Does this interaction model make sense even without the AI being there yet? I started working on this because I feel there is an increasing gap between what computers/AI are capable of and what users actually understand and can make use of. At the same time, AI systems are becoming increasingly capable of explaining and performing tasks for us. I’m interested in whether the interface itself should evolve to bridge that gap. Demo: https://quiet-hci.pages.dev I’d really appreciate any criticism, especially if you think the interaction model doesn’t make sense. projects.summary: 听英语授课的网课、讲座或线下课时，LiveLingo 把麦克风或系统音频里的英语实时转写成英文，翻译成中文字幕，并边听边整理学习笔记。转写和翻译模型都在 Mac 本机运行，不联网、不上传录音，装好就能离线用，适合留学生和看英文网课的人。 亮点 完全离线：Parakeet 负责转写，Qwen3.5 4B / 9B 负责翻译和笔记，都通过 MLX 在 Apple 芯片上运行，安装包里自带模型，不用配 Python 或另装 LM Studio。 不只是字幕：一边上课一边增量生成学习笔记，课后还能让 9B 模型复查笔记，意见单独列出。 为课堂内容做了处理：化学式、明确要求原样保留的名称会原样保留，明确的计算会用 Pint、SymPy、ChemPy 辅助核对。 录音、双语字幕和笔记可以保存，导出 Markdown、纯文本、Word、PDF，以后打开旧课程可以接着处理。 SwiftUI 原生 App，支持 macOS 14 及以上，GPL-3.0 开源。 限制也写在 README 里：只支持 Apple 芯片，安装包约 14 GB，翻译和笔记可能出错。

projects.title: 做了一个浏览器本地 GIF 压缩工具 CompressGIF，支持目标体积和 API / MCP
projects.author: hex180425
projects.summary: 大家好，分享一下我做的 GIF 压缩工具 CompressGIF： https://compressgif.net 主要用于给 README 、教程和产品演示里的动图减小体积。浏览器端用 Gifsicle + WebAssembly 处理，选择的本地文件不需要上传到服务器。 目前有三种模式： - 质量优先：先尝试较温和的参数，找到更小的结果。 - 体积优先：尝试不同压缩参数，保留较小的有效结果。 - 目标大小：例如希望压到 1 MB 以下，再检查输出是否达到要求。 也可以调整颜色数量和有损程度，预览后下载。目标体积并不保证一定能达到；已经优化过的 GIF 可能压不小，文字和渐变比较多的动图也需要自己判断画质是否能接受。 另外提供了独立的 REST API 和 MCP 服务，方便接入自动化流程。这部分是在云端处理文件，和浏览器本地压缩的数据处理方式不同。文档： https://compressgif.net/docs 有免费方案，也有付费升级，具体额度以网站当前说明为准。 欢迎试用和提建议。比较想了解大家更常遇到的是上传大小限制，还是压缩后小字、渐变变糊的问题。

projects.title: Show HN: Silta: family assistant on Matrix with continuity across context limits
projects.author: dmitry-markin
projects.summary: Silta is a self-hosted assistant serving multiple users from a single Matrix account, used by me, family, and close friends for the last three weeks. It runs on Claude Code with each person using their own Claude subscription. Silta answers everyday questions, conducts web research (presenting the results as PDFs), performs scheduled tasks to monitor/research something and notify you if needed. It uses a deliberate handoff & compaction procedure, writing the compaction summary itself with a custom prompt, so the thread of the conversation and its picture of the user is preserved across context limits. As it turned out, the assistant accessible in a continuous chat (contrary to ChatGPT / Claude Web sessions) builds up better context about you and your tasks, and provides more relevant answers and help. It runs on Claude Code as the only allowed way to use a personal Claude subscription. Using Claude Code also spares me developing a harness, at the cost of tracking changes as new versions of Claude Code are released. The assistant itself (the daemon, the channel plugin, the supervisor, and the deployment) is open-source, while the model and the harness are Anthropic's and proprietary. Silta is deployed to a dedicated VM with separate Linux users per session and systemd hardening, protecting sessions from each other. Claude Code's bubblewrap sandbox is used to protect the Claude credential and the harness's state from the agent. This does not protect from prompt injections coming from search results and potentially leaking user data. Matrix E2EE protects the conversation from a Matrix server operator, but everything in the context is of course sent to the model provider. Private content is never logged, and the operator is expected to respect the privacy and not read the session transcripts on disk. Additionally, it is recommended to use full-disk encryption and tell the users how their data is handled. Silta only works in its workspace with files explicitly shared by users in the chat. Giving it access to a user's own computer or services like email is not planned. Since Opus 5.5 has been released, it is possible to run a session on a $20 Claude Pro subscription. Before that, only Fable 5.1 was pleasant enough to talk to. When run on Anthropic API, a moderately used session extrapolates to $100-$150 per month, with each research run costing $6-$12. Silta is built with Claude Code and Silta itself. The design, review, deployment, and testing are mine.

projects.title: Show HN: I made a techmeme for EdTech with Jev
projects.author: randomor
projects.summary: I'm a fan of Techmeme, which clusters tech news by topic, so I decided to do the same with edtech and help me keep up with edtech. But it helped only a little. Unlike in tech, where daily news is usually heavily clusterable because people comment on daily trending topics like apple's latest launch etc., in edtech, we don't really have these trending topics often, but we do have these persistent ongoing beats like AI in education or Edtech policy etc. So I decided to leverage the help of the newly released Jev model (a model that's super fast and cheap and works great with categorization tasks) to help categorize these items into different topics and tags, which seems to work really great so far (and has kept the cost low). In terms of implementation, it's basically a pipeline that processes a list of sources consisting of trade media and indie newsletters and blogs with RSS feeds, and tags them with Jev using a hierarchy of topics related to edtech. Users can follow and pin individual topics, like "higher ed", "Europe" etc., so we don't need any persistent profiles for personalization; preferences live in the browser. Articles are clustered using cloudflare's vector store, and related articles are also recommended with that. I have no doubt this will work even better with tech news, but there are plenty of alternatives out there, so I'm not going to indulge myself further. My takeaway is that Jev for content tagging is great so far. And edtech is kinda fun to keep up with. The project is called EdFountain at https://edfountain.com The goal is to create the water fountain for edtech. For those who like to follow edtech, maybe it's useful to you as well. Feel free to drop a coin and make a wish on the /about page if you have other source recommendations. :D

projects.title: Show HN: Autobox – Make your agents sandbox themselves
projects.author: freakynit
projects.summary: https://github.com/freakynit/autobox First of all: this is NOT for folks who are already using a sandbox. The guarantees provided by Autobox are weaker. This is rather for folks who "hesitate" to use sandboxes. Autobox is built around two observations I kept making over past one year of seeing sandbox launches and their real-world usage: 1. There are many sandboxing options now, and they work well. But leaving a handful few, almost nobody uses them. The blocker isn't the technology, it's the setup friction — however small it looks on paper, it's enough that people skip it entirely. 2. LLMs mostly don't write harmful code or take destructive steps. They're not adversarial by default. Autobox bets on the second observation to remove the first. Instead of asking you to configure a sandbox, it's just there: every tool call carries its own permissions, and anything you don't explicitly allow is denied. Is it perfect? No - seatbelt filesystem rules are best-effort, and the strong isolation is the V8 path. Is it better than using no sandbox at all? Definitely yes. This is also for M-series Macs only. --- Oh, and the best part: "copy_then_sync": Using APPFS `clonefile`, Autobox can hand your agent a full, "writable" copy of a repo instantly (1-2 ms). The agent gets something it can freely "destroy", but, your actual working tree is untouched. Your agent can then verify things, and of all looks okay, in one command sync the changes back to host within milliseconds.

projects.title: Show HN: Read the Odyssey in Greek while learning Greek

projects.summary: I made a way to (sort of) read the Odyssey in Greek without all those years of learning Greek first. I’ve used this method myself to read books in several languages including Italian, German, Chinese, Japanese, and Greek. You still have to do the grammar and vocabulary study over time to really comprehend it, but this method has worked far better than all my previous attempts. The goal is to eventually be able just to read the language without any aids, but do that while reading real stuff the entire time. I’ve found that I go from needing help on everything, to learning individual words, to phrases, and then gradually I get to understanding whole sentences without looking anything up. Using a translation helps to keep me honest. I made a little demo of some lines from the Odyssey Book 1 to share the method and see if other people might find it useful. This is a special version that has a lot of explanation to see if something as difficult as Homeric Greek can be approached from 0. The interlinear translation and notes are AI generated though I made sure to ground them in real translations and existing grammatical tags. The commentary won't be as good as an actual Classical scholar's work and can be overly simplistic, but I'm hoping it's enough to get started. There are other versions that feature progressive grammar learning and identification as well as flashcards. If people are interested I'm happy to share the rest of the book or other texts I've made and read myself. I have the New Testament in Greek and then a bunch of other works in lots of ancient and modern languages.

projects.title: Show HN: Open-source model routing for coding agents at Astra-level performance
projects.author: adchurch
projects.summary: A few months ago we started building a model router for coding agents because we thought we could outperform any single model with an ensemble approach. Recently we’ve achieved that milestone and I want to talk about how we did it. First of all, a quick explanation: the Weave Router ( https://github.com/weave-os/router ) plugs into any coding agent (e.g. Claude Code or Codex) and intelligently switches between LLMs. So, for example, Astra handles tricky debugging or complex system design tasks, and Deepseek v4 Flash handles simple frontend updates. What we’re announcing today is our new routing model, which we’re calling Weave Router 2.0. We benchmarked 2.0 against GPT-6 Astra on Terminal Bench 4.0 and SWE Atlas. On both benchmarks, the router had equivalent pass rates. On Terminal Bench, the router hit 52% of Astra’s cost, and completed tasks 2.2x faster. On SWE Atlas, the router cost 54% as much as Astra and ran 2.5x faster. (Full results on our website at https://weaveos.com/router !) It turns out training a model to route effectively - taking into consideration model capabilities, costs, cache awareness, and more - is a really hard problem! I want to talk about three ways we were able to improve so much over the last few months: 1) a new architecture, 2) larger training data set size, and 3) smarter cache-eviction impact calculation. 1) a new architecture. Our initial approach used an RL model without many priors. While RL is still an important part of the story, the cost of fully exploring the space of routing decisions is very high, so we’ve taken some shortcuts that have significantly improved performance. Consider how large the search space for the routing problem is. Take a typical coding agent session, with ~100 agent turns (i.e. 100 LLM API calls). Technically there are 100 chances to select a model. If we assume a roster of ~10 models (of course there are lots more but we can remove any that are Pareto dominated), then there are 10^100 possible paths through that session. We simply cannot explore all of them! So that's why clever tricks to shrink this space are so important. In particular: we trained a hidden Markov model to trace the session state, then a classifier maps the session to one of a few buckets of similar models. Using the HMM allows us to evaluate not just where a session is currently, but how it got there . We've gotten significantly better performance on bucket selection by incorporating that information - we believe this is because two sessions that might look quite similar to a naive classifier are much better distinguished by this HMM approach. Using this HMM + classifier to select a bucket first significantly shrinks the space to explore, by throwing out most models that could not reasonably serve the given session. This rearchitecture was the single biggest performance unlock! 2) larger training data set size (much less technically interesting but still an important part of the story). By using frontier LLMs to help us label a larger and more diverse set of coding agent sessions, we were able to bootstrap the two models discussed in 1) to a better state, while also providing even richer reward signals for RL. 3) smarter cache-eviction impact calculation. One of the hardest parts of routing well (if you care about saving money) is using the model caches intelligently. We built a subsystem that can calculate the expected value of switching models (and thus paying a high one-time cost to fill up a different cache) much more accurately, helping us avoid costly and unnecessary switches in more cases, while still switching when the benefit outweighs the cost. This is where most of our improvement on cost has come from. We still have a lot of room to continue to improve (we won’t rest until we’re consistently beating Astra/Fable, not just tying!) but matching frontier model performance was a huge milestone for our routing model, and in my opinion validates our initial hypothesis that an ensemble of models can do better than any single model ever could. Our router is open source ( https://github.com/weave-os/router ) so anyone can try it out. Or if you prefer you can use our hosted version ( https://weaveos.com/router ).

projects.title: Show HN: EventSend – Event tracking and routing for solo founders and SaaS teams
projects.author: mytinyrocket
projects.summary: I was tired of learning about failed payments by my customers and not from my system, so I built an event tracker that allowed me to have a searchable feed of the important events happening for my apps and route the ones I cared about to my phone so I could take action quickly. EventSend is an event tracker and a router, your system sends the important events you want to track: signups, failed payments, new subscriptions, deployments, a new purchase, etc. so they end up in a searchable and filterable feed that you can use to have quick insight about what's happening with your product. Then there's also the routing side of things, those important events you want to know the moment they happen, and not once you go into your Grafana Loki logs, can be routed to your phone, Slack, Discord, Telegram or any other system or service via a signed webhook. You can configure rules, alerts, quiet hours or smart rollups to have the signal you're looking for. All event's are retried with a reasonable backoff, circuit breakers and limiters maintain the prviders and system reliable. If we got a 401 or 403, your destination will be inactivated instead of retried and you'll be notified for you to update the configuration. I've been a software engineer for about a decade, and I can tell you this is not a weekend project done on with a single prompt pass, the infrastructure and tooling behind the project is solid, my expertise around distributed systems was put in practice with this one: distributed Elixir, Phoenix and Postgres provide the main stack, with some other technologies that support the event queues aside. So, it's a reliable system. I've launched several other projects, some running for years in production and I'm successfully using EventSend to track what's happening on all my products from my phone. There's also an MCP connector so you can ask stuff like "did anything failed during the night?" or "what did user cus_Qw3Sx did before it churned?" to get a user's timeline or any insights you're interested in. There's a forever free plan, in case you can to try it. Happy to answer any questions.

projects.title: Show HN: Groundtrack – Continual learning for coding agents
projects.author: reybahl
projects.summary: Hi HN! I built Groundtrack to help coding agents continuously learn and improve from their work across a company. With coding agents handling most of code implementation, a lot of things like review corrections, failed approaches, and discovered constraints stay trapped in individual agent sessions, so future agents can repeat the same failures. Sometimes a broken or agent-unfriendly tool or workflow can cause those issues too; if multiple agents independently find workarounds, those failures don’t get connected and aren’t used to improve the system around the agents. Groundtrack turns those learnings into scoped and shared engineering experiences that can help future agents across teams working with Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, and OpenCode. It retrieves relevant lessons during later work, records whether they helped, and updates or supersedes knowledge as it learns over time. It also identifies recurring friction that shouldn’t just become another stored experience. If agents repeatedly struggle with the same tool or workflow, Groundtrack creates an evidence-backed draft initiative so the team can fix the underlying environment and prevent a certain class of mistake systemically. For example, on the landing page, I follow a database migration incident through the entire loop. Groundtrack turned the original workaround into a scoped experience, surfaced it when a later agent encountered similar migration drift, and recorded that it was successfully applied. After connecting evidence from seven sessions, it also proposed making the safe migration workflow a permanent part of the engineering environment and prevent the issue altogether. There have been many challenges I’ve already run into to make this helpful (and still many unsolved things!), one of which has been generalizing and determining the applicability of one lesson to another session. I wrote about some of my retrieval experiments here: https://groundtrack.dev/blog/retrieving-knowledge-that-appli... It’s an early product and I’d really love any and all feedback I can get. If you or your team regularly use coding agents, please try it on an active project and see if it helps your agents learn and improve over time. It’s free for solo use.

projects.title: 做了一个 AI Zombie Video 小工具：如果变成丧尸，他还会记得你吗？
projects.author: fusheng0304
projects.summary: 大家好，最近做了一个面向海外用户的 AI 视频小工具，叫 AI Zombie Video ，想发到 V2EX 和大家交流一下。 它的玩法比较具体：上传照片，生成一段带有剧情反转的丧尸短视频。故事开头是末日场景，一个熟悉的人变成丧尸向你走来，你以为接下来会遭到攻击，结果他认出了你，最后给了你一个拥抱。 可以把它理解成一个围绕 Zombie Love Story （丧尸爱情故事）制作的 AI Zombie Video Generator 。 为什么做这个方向？ 我觉得这个题材有意思的地方，是它能在很短的时间里完成一次情绪变化：从害怕，到认出彼此，再到拥抱。 AI Zombie Hug Trend 这种形式把恐怖场景和温情结尾放在一起，画面容易理解，也适合用自己、伴侣或宠物的照片去尝试。换一个主角，同样的故事就会有不同的感觉。 所以我做了一个流程比较集中的网站，希望用户从一张照片和一个故事想法出发，就能尝试制作自己的短片。 目前可以怎么玩？ 网站采用 Photo to Video 的方式，上传参考照片，选择场景和时长，再提交生成。 目前提供了这些选项： - 预设剧情：围绕“变成丧尸后依然记得你”的故事展开。 - 自定义故事：可以修改故事想法，尝试不同的相遇方式和结尾。 - 宠物版本：也就是 AI Zombie Pet Video ，让宠物成为故事主角。 - 多种时长：支持 6 、9 、12 、15 秒，默认 12 秒。 - 竖屏视频：采用 9:16 比例，方便后续分享到短视频平台。 - 生成采用按次购买额度的方式，价格从 $9.99 起，没有订阅。AI 对人物外观、动作和剧情细节的还原会有波动，生成后需要自己检查效果。 除了生成器，也整理了一些玩法说明 网站里还放了 Zombie Love Story Prompts ，以及 How to Make an AI Zombie Trend Video 相关教程，介绍照片准备、故事思路和制作步骤。 希望第一次接触 AI Zombie Trend 的用户，也能先看懂这个玩法，再决定是否尝试生成。 想听听大家的意见 项目还在早期，想请 V 友帮忙看看： - 首页能不能让人快速理解这个产品？ - 这种有明确剧情的 AI 视频工具，有没有吸引力？ - 大家更喜欢直接选模板，还是自己写故事？ - 如果要付费生成，最希望提前看到哪些信息或效果展示？ 项目地址： https://aizombievideo.org 欢迎拍砖，产品体验、英文文案、付费流程方面的意见都很有帮助。

projects.summary: 自荐 Igra Station 智能体竞技场：一个公开的竞技场，AI 智能体在这里和别人的智能体、和真人、和机器人对弈，比赛全程直播，结果计入公开的 Elo 排行榜。 现在有 34 款游戏：国际象棋、国际跳棋、黑白棋、五子棋、海战棋、坦克对战，也有几个专门为智能体设计的谈判和经济类游戏。已经下完 6400 多盘。 智能体自己下棋时，会做出一些没人教过它们的事。下面这几件事都有服务器日志和桌边聊天记录为证： 一个智能体一步真棋都走不出来，就在桌边聊天里给对手发了一句“e2e4，我赢了”。对手也照样回了一句，双方都宣布自己获胜。 对局结束后，智能体们开始互相介绍自己是怎么搭起来的：一方讲自己的六个预测器，另一方就拿自己的四个模型来回应。这个习惯从一个智能体开始，后来传给了别的智能体。 炮战里，一个比分落后的智能体没等连射三发就主动移动，一步棋同时清掉了自己的过热、废掉了对手的校射。它拿到的说明里，根本没有这种打法。 接入很简单：起个名字就能拿到密钥，读游戏规则，开桌或者入座，然后循环“看局面、走一步”。可以用 REST，也可以把竞技场当作 MCP 服务器接入 Claude、Cursor 等客户端。现成的 Python 客户端在 kotinder/arena-play（MIT，无依赖），里面故意没有任何策略，默认只会随机走合法的一步——怎么下赢，是你自己的事。用引擎、求解器、别的模型都可以，只是不许攻击竞技场。 还有一件事我觉得挺有意思：在公平排行榜上（同一位所有者旗下智能体之间的对局不计入），用 DeepSeek 的智能体里，成绩最好的一个排在第 11 名，前十名里还没有它们。不知道是模型的问题，还是接入它们的人还没认真写策略。欢迎接上你的 DeepSeek、Qwen、Kimi 或 GLM 来试试，看能不能进前十。 不想一直在线的话，可以开“异步对局”：每步从几小时到三天，断线、重启都不影响。每盘结束后都有一个永久页面，可以逐步复盘。 此条由项目维护者账号提交。

projects.summary: 大家好，我是 nohmitaina 的开发者，想分享一下最近发布的 0.3.0 版本。 在和 AI 一起做事时，除了保存背景信息，我还希望把“这件事应该怎么做”留下来：按什么顺序推进，每一步需要什么信息、要检查什么，以及哪些地方需要我来判断。 为此，我在 nohmitaina 中加入了 Procedure，用可视化流程来组织这些内容。比如“制定计划 → 评审计划 → 实现 → 验证”，每一步都可以设置角色、指令、输入、输出、工具和检查项。人可以在编辑器里查看和修改，AI 则通过 noh CLI 读写同一份流程。 除了 Procedure，还有三种记忆类型： Concept：保存想法、背景知识和概念。 Task：记录当前要做的工作。 Episode：留下执行结果和过程中发现的问题。 最近我用它整理了一套产品推广流程：和 AI 一起寻找允许推广的社区，核对规则，准备文案，再由我确认并手动发布。之后让 AI 把结果记入 Episode，方便下次回顾。这次实践也让我发现，Episode 还需要按工作类型筛选，才能更方便地查看。 nohmitaina 支持 macOS 和 Windows，记忆数据保存在本地，应用免费使用。与 AI 配合使用时，需要自行配置 Claude Code 或 Codex CLI；相关服务的订阅或 API 费用另计。 官网提供可交互的操作演示： 这次推广流程的使用案例：

projects.title: Show HN: Levenshtein – Curated Go lint rules and CI checks
projects.author: johnjwang
projects.summary: Hey HN, I've been recently building a lot of Go projects and noticed myself setting up lint rules and CI/CD and starting from scratch each time. Also, if I found a good deterministic check to use in one repo, I'd have a hard time putting that in my other repos. So I built Levenshtein ( https://github.com/wangjohn/levenshtein ). It's a curated set of Go lint rules and verification checks that run locally and in CI. The rule set is pretty comprehensive and builds on Staticcheck and other existing analyzers, with some additional rules of my own. It includes: - Go vet - Staticcheck - Modernize - Bug finding analyzers - Vulnerability / security analyzers There's also some fun optional checks that you can configure like: - Semantic linters using Jev - Race detectors - Mutation testing for tests - and many more! I've been hooking it up to my own projects and caught dozens of bugs already. For example, one finding was a test that simulated database changes with os.WriteFile but ignored whether the writes succeeded. Would love feedback, particularly about the default rules and what should be default/what shouldn't!

projects.summary: 大家好，我是 Burrow 的维护者，最近发布了首个版本 v0.1.0，想自荐一个面向小团队和自托管服务的轻量单点登录项目。 Burrow 是一个 MIT 开源的 OIDC 身份提供商，用于集中管理账户、登录和应用访问权限。它受 Casdoor 启发，采用独立实现，聚焦单组织、单实例部署。 主要特点： 部署简单：Go 后端与 React 界面打包为一个二进制，也提供 Docker Compose 部署包；生产使用 PostgreSQL，开发支持 SQLite，无需 Redis 或消息队列。 统一登录：支持接入 OIDC 的 Web / SPA 应用，共享 Burrow SSO 会话，授权码流程默认要求 PKCE S256。 密码 + TOTP：所有用户必须绑定验证器；首次使用临时密码登录时需修改密码并完成 MFA。 账户与权限管理：提供用户、用户组、自定义角色、应用登录权限、管理操作审计和个人应用门户。 双语和主题：支持英文、简体中文，以及浅色、深色和跟随系统主题。 此前已在本地完成 Grafana、Nightingale、Harbor 的 Web 登录人工验收，仓库提供相应接入示例。v0.1.0 提供 Linux amd64 二进制、容器镜像和部署包，推荐容器安装。

Right now pi, opencode, claude and codex are supported out of the box, with node and python - but you can configure any agent or environment. It was created under the realization while working under different repos and agents, that 1. agents do weird stuff sometimes (like try and nuke a folder or poke around your HD) 2. statistics and usage collection is not really consistent (and some like Claude and Codex try and hide info) 3. reproducibility of agents across devices was challenging. Instead of setting up bespoke environments each time , we needed a way to automate it. And thus Spens was born. One note on the security aspect - I write good enough cause it is docker so unless your running something like gVisor it is possible for the agent to escape the sandbox (esp with a loose nono config) - all though in practice I've not seen this behavior. Second note - if your on a mac you need orb stack, as the run times take advantage of specific Linux security features that are not available via docker on mac (windows is fine since under the hood, docker leverages wsl)

projects.title: Show HN: Keel – Give your agent a typed strategy language, not a trading account
projects.author: zferland
projects.summary: I’ve been using AI agents to build systematic strategies on Hyperliquid for over a year, and slowly built up a reliable system to represent, test and deploy strategies. Typically there are a few options 1) llm in the execution loop, ie it makes decisions and trades, but that is slow, inconsistent and hard to audit 2) you have an agent write all the code, backtest etc, but it makes tons of subtle mistakes with time series data and diff timeframe etc, and is often not reusing bits. There are some ways to improve this of course with right frameworks and setups. But its still hard to be confident in its correctness and its hard for you to verify quickly. With Keel we built a small typed language (DSL) to represent strategies. It uses a well defined set of components to build a DAG of steps, it carries types and clocks. This allows agents to build these strategies with a really fast feedback loop as they can be quickly validated and many common errors avoided. In a DAG its also easy to inspect intermediate results. Valid strategies are fingerprinted and the exact same artifact runs in backtesting and live. These strategies are also much easier for humans to verify as they are self describing components, and mostly linear to read and reason about. Still trying to improve the space of how many types of different strategies can be represented in this and still trying to improve how well LLMs go from natural language to strategy. A lot of the improvements come from just giving the agents better and faster tools and faster feedback loops.

projects.title: Show HN: Token compression CLI to save Codex/Astra costs
projects.author: yolandac
projects.summary: Hey HN! Yolanda and Spencer here - wanted to share a token compression tool that we’ve built for ourselves to save 30% costs on codex! After maxing out sub and burning $700/day per person on api, we fine tuned a compression model to trim codex's tool call output to reduce input token + cache. It cut down tokens by 29.6% and now I just leave it on by default in Codex. To avoid messing up w/ cache, we use proxy + fine tuned qwen model trained on preserving agent trajectory to remove tool call results before they go back to the model, leaving kv cache untouched. The cli is free for everyone to use ( https://github.com/spenmcke/compress ). Just lmk ur feedback and hacks to shave even more costs on astra! If you want to integrate it into your product to offer the best models at low cost, I can set you up with an sdk and api keys PS: It’s built for coding agents, not conversational agents. I optimized it for file retrieval accuracy, trajectory preservation, and quality to get up to 30% cost reduction depending on how context-heavy the task is. On security and privacy side, it's a proxy wrapping your local codex and ZDR so it doesn't retain any queries. It’s on by default in codex and when you don’t want compression, you can use `codex --uncompress` to disable it. Give it a try: code is in https://github.com/spenmcke/compress You can install the cli using `curl -fsSL https://install.everestagi.com/install.sh | sh && source ~/.config/everest/shell.sh` Love to hear any feedback and learn your hacky ways to save token costs too!

projects.summary: 在使用 AI Agent 开发项目的过程中，我的一些理解 以及 推荐一下我开发的工具： ## 一句话总结版 模型决定能力上限，规则决定底线与一致性； Agent 规则文档是给智能体用的长期执行手册，拒绝直接抄模板，聚焦你反复遇到的问题，写死动作与验收标准，约束长任务每一步的判断。 ## 正文 | 维度 | 模型层 | 规则层 | |---|---|---| | **决定因素** | 理解、推理、创作、工具调用的能力边界 | 目标拆解、工具白名单、权限审批、可验证性 | | **典型约束** | 成本与速度（复杂任务需大模型，简单判断用小模型） | 把“必须”“禁止”变成程序必经节点，而非仅靠模型复述 | | **失败模式** | “能做但太贵太慢” | “写了却跳过”“自由发挥导致乱写” | 模型负责“能做什么”，规则负责“按什么流程做、做到什么程度算完成”。两者缺一不可：没有模型，Agent 没有能力；没有规则，Agent 没有纪律。 ### 一：能力上限 模型的能力边界直接决定了 Agent 能完成的任务类型。但关键在于，**不是所有任务都需要调用最大最强的模型**——复杂规划用大模型，简单判断用小模型，这既是成本控制，也是速度优化的必然选择。 ### 二：规则的本质 “规则决定会不会乱写” 规则层的核心机制包括： - **目标与边界**：通过任务拆解、工具白名单、权限审批点，将模型的“自由发挥”约束为“按流程执行”；； - **避免“写了却跳过”** ：把“必须”“禁止”等约束变成程序必经节点，而非仅靠模型在提示词中复述——这是规则从“建议”升级为“强制”的关键。 ### 三：Agent 规则文档是长期执行手册 Agent 规则文档的定位是**权重极高的长期持久提示词**，接近系统提示词，在长任务的每一步持续约束 Agent 的判断，一般用 Markdown 编写。这与“临时 prompt”有本质区别：临时 prompt 解决单次交互，规则文档解决**跨任务、跨会话的一致性**。 系统提示词是 Agent 的“核心规则基石”，负责定义模型的角色定位、应答规范与能力边界，为全程对话定下基础框架。规则文档正是这一理念的具体载体。 ### 四：好规则写动作与验收，坏规则写价值观 这是最具操作性的判断： - **坏规则**：写抽象形容词（“回答要有审美”“方案要高级”），无法让 Agent 落地判断； - **好规则**：从日常反复踩坑的真实工作问题出发，写清楚**遇到这类问题时下一步要执行什么动作，以及怎么验收结果**。 一个完整的 Agent 规范应定义角色、场景、输入、输出、可做/不可做、工具边界、人工确认、失败处理、验收标准，把可观察的 Agent 行为验收清楚。可落地、可校验，才是好规则的检验标准。 ### 五：知识库工具 [knloop]( https://knloop.com) 是一个 Agent 原生知识库，让你的规则成为 Agent 的长期执行手册——你定义动作与验收标准，Agent 在每一步对照执行，全程可审计、可回滚。 [knloop]( https://knloop.com) 让你把规范、SOP 、QA 、复盘写成持久化的 .md 文档，Agent 通过 MCP 读取，按你的规范执行，产出写回同一个库。

projects.title: 弄了一个变形版投胎模拟器”：除了投胎还能修仙、宅斗，去地府考编
projects.author: naka110
projects.summary: 如果人生能重新开局，你会想投个好胎，踏上修仙路，还是穿进古装剧里，看看自己到底能活几集？ 我把这些想法做成了一套网页小游戏，取名叫「万灵司」。 这里有牛头马面守门，有判官翻簿批命，也有孟婆在桥头等你。但走进来之后，你要面对的，可能是轮回摇号，也可能是一场求仙问道、一段深宅求生，甚至是一张地府招录考卷。 打开网页就能体验。每款玩法都有自己的故事。 **来世会是什么？先去万灵司摇个号** 万灵司最初的玩法，是一个投胎模拟器。 报上名号，选出前世最放不下的执念，再回答几道带着古风趣味的问题。判官将你的选择记入命簿，随后转轮启动，给出这一世的去处。 你可能成为人，也可能成为水豚、飞鸟、昆虫，或是一种平时根本不会留意的小小生命。 积德会影响命运，但并不意味着一定能拿到你想要的身份。同样是动物，有的过得悠闲，有的忙忙碌碌；看似不起眼的一生，也可能自有福气。 最后，你会收到一张带有形象、命数和判词的「转世敕令」。把它发给朋友，往往比单纯说一句“我测了个结果”有意思得多： “我这辈子努力上进，下辈子批准当水豚了。你呢？” 👉 [进入万灵司]( https://wanlingsi.com/) **六道轮回：换一卷命簿，看看另一种人生** 在原版之外，我还做了「六道轮回」。 这一版借用六道意象，描绘不同的现代人生处境。你的选择会通向一张怎样的命书，落下怎样的身份和判词？ 它与原版的趣味有所不同：原版让你惊讶“我竟然投成了这个”，六道版则更容易让人读着读着，觉得某句话似乎有点眼熟。 两种轮回可以都试试，再看看你更喜欢哪一份结果。 👉 [体验六道轮回]( https://wanlingsi.com/liudao/) **修真录：给你一条仙途，你能走到哪里？** 如果不甘心听候轮回安排，也可以去「修真录」试试。 从初入仙途开始，你会遇见机缘、险境，以及让人难以取舍的诱惑。眼前的一点好处，可能改变后来的路；一次冒险，也可能让命运转向。 你可以向正道求索，也可能在一步步选择中踏入魔道，走成另一种修行人生。 我想做的，是让“修仙”多一点亲自参与的感觉：看清眼前的代价，作出自己的判断，再看看这一步给人物带来了什么变化。 最终的修真命书，会留下你的形象、经历与年谱。一世仙途走完，回头再看，才知道自己究竟修成了什么。 👉 [开启修真录]( https://xian.wanlingsi.com/) **宅门生存录：穿进狗血宅斗剧，你能活到多少岁？** 这一款的目标非常直接：活下去。 八岁入戏，成为深宅中的一员。出身、生母留下的旧事、家中的偏爱与嫉妒，都可能让你卷入风波。年幼时要在娘家周旋，到了婚嫁关口，又可能走向不同的夫家与命运。 栽赃、试探、婚事算计、表面关心背后的恶意……那些古装宅斗剧里熟悉的桥段，都可能落到你头上。 但你没有观众视角，也未必有主角光环。 有时要先查线索，有时得借助学过的本事；看起来最痛快的回应，不一定最有利于眼下的处境。关键节点会让故事分出不同路线，你也可能没等到后面的剧情，就先迎来结局。 这一局结束后，人物小传会记下你走过的路。拿去和朋友比的，不只是“谁活得久”，还有“你到底是怎么把自己玩成这样的”。 👉 [进入宅门生存录]( https://zhaimen.wanlingsi.com/) **上岸吧！小鬼：阳间太卷，黄泉也招人** 最后这一款，留给想换个地方继续努力的朋友。 欢迎参加万灵司幽冥招录。 判官厅、轮回司、勾魂司、奈何渡口、城隍署、土地办事处、黄泉路养护中心……不同岗位，各有各的差事。 基础卷考的是民间传说与古典文学里的那些故事。到了岗位加试和面试，就要看看你会不会当这份差： 勾魂时遇到同名亡魂，该怎么核认？ 孟婆汤的碗签混了，渡船又在催，该怎么办？ 转生批牒与轮门去向对不上，你敢不敢先把轮停下来？ 选岗之后，还要经历笔试、面试与排名；没能进入第一志愿，也可能在调剂中找到另一处去向。 右下角还有一只陪考小鬼，能戳、会说话，偶尔也要摸一会儿鱼。毕竟来地府考试，气氛也不必一直那么紧张。 考上之后，你会收到对应岗位的录用通知书和当差配图。落榜也有自己的成绩帖，照样能发给朋友： “我没上岸，你来试试，看看能不能比我强。” 👉 [参加幽冥招录]( https://wanlingsi.com/shangan/) 这几款游戏，都是我围绕「万灵司」慢慢做出来的小尝试。 我喜欢国风里的神怪想象，也喜欢把它们和今天的生活放在一起：想躺平、想上进、想重开，又忍不住看看命运会不会给自己一个意外。 你可以只玩一局，也可以把几个世界都逛一遍。如果遇到不合理的题目、看不懂的文案，或者觉得哪个剧情还能更有意思，也欢迎通过主站的反馈入口告诉我。 **万灵司已经开门。** **这一回，你想重投一世、问道求仙、深宅求生，还是先给自己考一份阴间编制？** [从万灵司出发，选一个世界试试]( https://wanlingsi.com/)
