projects.title: Show HN: Tracelane.dev- OSS Rust LLM Gateway with a tamper-evident ledger
projects.author: NovStar
projects.summary: Hi everyone, Sanjeev here- founder. My journey in AI started with wanting to break into emerging AI companies, but without deep hands-on experience, it was hard to even get noticed. I started with scope focused minor projects but then curiosity got expanded to understand what happens under the hood of LLM calls, what goes in & how reliable AI agents works and gets built by world's top companies and how future of agents would evolve in next 10 years when agents will have more controls. For the last 6+ months, I’ve spent every minute of weekends, nights researching, learning deeper with coding agents and newer models, while managing my day job and family, gained 5 KGs weight along the way. I wanted to find my Ikigai of what I am good at, what I can sustain working on without loosing my head and effectively also use my 15 years of real work experience from BFSI where serious SOC 2 auditors ask for tamper evident evidences and not just logfile as proof. That became Tracelane. With Tracelane, you can host your own neutral model agnostic gateway to put controls, add guardrails, observe everything happening in production environment and proof what your agents did and why. Though I built everything as solo, I have put every due diligences to ensure the product is secure, fast, ready to use in actual live env by serious adopters. I would genuinely appreciate your feedback —especially the audit ledger design and what evidence you’d want from an agent recorder before trusting it.

projects.author: huangy7

github.name: huangy7/lokii
github.description: Blazingly fast, native macOS file search powered by Rust and AppKit — like Everything for Mac

projects.summary: Lokii 是一款极致轻量、亚毫秒级响应的 macOS 原生即时文件搜索工具，致力于在 Mac 上带来类似 Windows 下 Everything 般的轻巧、瞬时文件名检索体验。 在 macOS 上，Spotlight 或访达搜索在定位文件时有时不够快速直接，或者在海量文件中难以做到纯文件名的“键入即出结果”。Lokii 采用 Rust 内存倒排索引核心（lokii-core）+ 纯原生 Swift/AppKit 前端的架构，在数十万文件规模下依然提供亚毫秒级延迟与极低的资源消耗。 核心特性 1. 亚毫秒级即时检索：输入字符的同时结果瞬时呈现在屏幕上，50 万级文件检索延迟 < 10ms，常驻内存占用极低（< 100MB）。 2. 多模式智能识别：支持纯子串匹配、通配符（, ?）、正则表达式（^...$）以及模糊拼写容错（Fuzzy）。 3. FSEvents 实时无感监听：基于 macOS 多路 FSEvents 增量事件流与防抖队列，文件增删改移与重命名实时自动同步，日常待机 CPU 开销接近为零。 4. 全键盘极速流交互： 全局快捷键呼出（⌘⇧Space） 方向键平滑导航，Enter 访达中直达定位 ⌘C 一键复制完整文件路径，Esc 瞬间隐藏退出 5. 纯原生 AppKit 视觉质感：高信息密度原生虚拟列表、自适应斑马纹、系统原生文件图标渲染与轻量视窗动效。 6. 持久化紧凑缓存：基于 bitcode 紧凑二进制格式序列化存储索引，启动瞬间热加载恢复就绪状态。 7. 100% 离线与隐私优先：纯本地运行，没有任何账号系统，零网络请求、零遥测与追踪埋点，文件名与目录结构绝不离开您的 Mac。

projects.title: 做了个开源的 plist 在线编辑器，不装 Xcode 也能打开二进制 plist
projects.author: poppub
projects.summary: 各位 V 友好，分享一个自己做的小工具：**OpenPlist**，可以直接在浏览器里查看、编辑和转换 Apple 的 plist 文件。 它想解决的需求很简单：有时候只是想看一眼配置、改几个字段，或者把二进制 plist 转成能读的 XML ，希望打开网页就能处理。在 Windows 、Linux 上也能用，不依赖 Mac 或 Xcode 。 在线使用：[OpenPlist]( https://openplist.com/zh) 源码：[GitHub]( https://github.com/chenz24/openplist) 目前主要支持： - **查看和编辑**：打开 XML 、二进制（`bplist00`）和 OpenStep 格式的 plist ，在树形视图里修改键、值和类型，也可以切到 XML / JSON 源码编辑。 - **格式转换**：XML 与二进制 plist 互转，以及 plist 和 JSON 互转。 - **日常操作**：搜索键和值、新增和复制条目、撤销重做、未保存提醒。 另外也做了一些 Apple 开发相关的小工具，比如查看 `.mobileprovision` 的有效期、团队和设备信息，编辑 `.mobileconfig`、`.entitlements`、`.strings`、`.stringsdict` 和 `.xcconfig`，以及对 OpenCore 配置做一些基础检查。 **核心查看、编辑和转换都在浏览器本地完成，不上传文件内容。** 配置描述文件另外有可选的 AI 分析，只有主动使用时才会向配置的服务商发送经过部分字段脱敏的内容。 项目采用 MIT 协议开源，可以自行部署；界面支持中文、英文和日文。 两个使用时需要留意的地方：plist 导出会重新生成排版，不保留原注释； JSON 无法完整保留 plist 的日期、二进制数据等类型。内置的配置检查也只覆盖部分规则。

projects.author: huangy7

github.name: huangy7/MeowOut
github.description: A native macOS menu bar toolkit with a pixel pet that keeps you healthy. Clipboard, 2FA, dropzone, memos, snippets and a live system monitor — in one app. 原生 macOS 菜单栏工具箱，附带守护健康的像素宠物。

projects.summary: MeowOut 是一款采用 Swift 原生构建的 macOS 菜单栏多合一效率工具箱。 很多开发者平时电脑菜单栏上会挂着许多单一功能的小工具（剪贴板、2FA、系统监控、便签备忘、防休眠等），不仅占用内存和屏幕空间，切换也很繁琐。同时长时间伏案编码容易忘记喝水和休息。 MeowOut 将高频开发者日常工具深度整合进同一个原生菜单栏应用，并引入了一只可爱的像素小宠物（猫咪、熊猫、皮卡），在菜单栏陪你工作的同时提醒定时喝水、防沉迷与正念呼吸。 核心功能 1. 像素伴侣与健康守护：猫咪/熊猫/皮卡在菜单栏常驻奔跑与互动，定时提醒喝水、久坐休息，内置全屏沉浸式正念呼吸练习。 2. 剪贴板历史：完整记录纯文本、富文本与图片，支持模糊搜索、快捷粘贴、置顶收藏与历史清理。 3. 快速备忘（闪念胶囊）：原生 Markdown 备忘录，支持时间线与日历双视图，快捷键随手呼出速记窗口。 4. 文件中转站：轻量拖拽暂存区，随手拖入多格式文件、需要时随时拖出，支持内容快速预览。 5. 两步验证（TOTP 2FA）：支持主流 TOTP 算法，密钥经 macOS 原生钥匙串（Keychain）安全加密存储。 6. 实时系统与硬件监控：半透明面板实时展示 CPU、内存、网络、电池与磁盘状态，支持进程下钻与高能耗排行；支持合盖防休眠、电池保护模式与清洁锁屏模式（擦键盘防误触）。 7. 日常效率扩展： 环形快捷启动器：长按唤出光标直达的圆形多轮盘快捷启动器。 轻量基金看板：实时估值跟踪、隐私遮罩与持仓收益计算。

github.name: hAcKlyc/MyAgents
github.description: MyAgents - 优雅、易用的 Agent 桌面端 ，一站式 Agent 工作台与任务中心

projects.summary: 我是 MyAgents 的作者，自荐给周刊的软件栏目。 国庆这周，我把自己的几台电脑接成了一个 Agent 网络。现在坐在笔记本前，可以让 Windows 上的 Agent 用它当地的文件和环境干活，再把结果交回来。 MyAgents 是免费开源的桌面 Agent 工作台与任务系统，支持 macOS / Windows。刚发布的 0.5.0 新增 AgentNet：同一账号的设备加入网络、选择开放的 Agent，就能在对话中跨设备派活，不需要自己搭服务器。 我实际试了一件很小的事：问 Windows 下载文件夹里有几个日志文件。笔记本上的 Agent 找到远端设备，Windows 那边检查完，回传了 6 个文件及明细。这件事不复杂，但说明其他电脑上的文件和工具，也可以进入当前的工作。 单机也能使用：每个 Agent 有自己的工作区、模型、Skill 和工具，日常事务可以建成定时任务。支持 Claude Agent SDK、Codex、DeepSeek Harness 等运行环境。 客户端采用 AGPL-3.0-only；模型订阅或 API 按所选服务商计费。跨设备调用要求目标电脑在线、应用运行、相应 Agent 已开放，设备间任务与结果端到端加密。

projects.title: [送码] 给 Navidrome 写的安卓播放器 Mu3ic：现代 UI、智能歌单、混音、断网也能听，基础版免费
projects.author: aslehx
projects.summary: 我的歌放在家里服务器上的 Navidrome 里，五千多首，标签都是自己整理的，上个月还让 Agent 批量标准化一遍。电脑上听没问题，手机上一直没找到用着顺手的客户端，于是便有了[Mu3ic]( https://mu3ic.xyz)。 - 主页： https://mu3ic.xyz - 直接下载 APK： https://dl.robb3n.site/mu3ic/Mu3ic-stable.apk - GitHub 镜像： https://github.com/robb3n/mu3ic-releases/releases/latest ![Mu3ic]( https://i.imgur.com/BA2D4TN.jpeg) 先说明一下：Mu3ic 是播放器，连的是你自己搭的服务器，不提供任何音乐。Navidrome 之外，兼容 Subsonic / OpenSubsonic 的服务端也能连。原生 Kotlin + Jetpack Compose ，安卓 7.0 以上，安装包 8 MB 左右。 ## 为什么自己写 安卓上的 Subsonic 客户端其实不少，我前后装过好几个。 音流功能比较全，但界面不够现代，用起来不顺手。界面现代的是 Symfonium ，功能也全，可它同时要管本地文件、网盘、Plex 、Jellyfin ，对 Navidrome 的适配反而一般，缓存机制也不好用；设置项多到要专门花时间调，买它还得走 Google Play 。开源的那几个，要么界面停在好多年前，要么能做的事太少。 我要的其实就几样：界面好看、好用，天天要用的东西，光这一条就筛掉了大半播放器；打开要快；只管连服务器听歌，别的不管。所以 Mu3ic 从一开始就定成只做流播，不扫描手机里的本地文件。手机上存的缓存和下载，都只是为了断网的时候还能接着听。 写到现在，我觉得它和别的客户端最不一样的有三点： - **界面**：整套界面是自己设计的，不是 Material 默认那一套，滑动和转场都跟手，下面的截图都是真机上的样子 - **智能歌单**：在手机上就能建、能改，用的是一个“看得懂”的按钮式规则编辑器，不用去服务器上写 .nsp 文件 - **混音**：按你的播放记录、收藏和曲库标签自动组歌，每次点都重新采样 下面按我写它时想解决的事一件件说。 ## 曲库大了，翻起来要等 五千多首歌，每翻一页都要等服务器返回，滑快了就是一片空白。 Mu3ic 在手机上存一份曲库索引，整点和服务器同步一次。按单曲、专辑、歌手翻都是读本地，滑多快都不用等。搜索也是这三个维度一起出。 ![曲库和歌单]( https://i.imgur.com/UsP8zr8.jpeg) 打开 App 先看到的是首页，三排卡片： - 最近播放：记的是你从哪开始播的，歌单、专辑、混音、最爱都算 - 最近添加：单曲和专辑，同一天入库的同一张专辑会并成一张卡 - 最近喜爱：单曲、专辑、歌手 再往下是听歌统计：今天播了多少、连续听了几天、这周的曲线，按住曲线能看某一天和上周同一天的对比。 ![首页]( https://i.imgur.com/i6RLWKN.jpeg) ![首页下半]( https://i.imgur.com/QTraEsF.jpeg) ## 外语歌，想知道这句在唱什么 歌词逐行滚动，外语歌下面直接跟着中文翻译（服务器上的歌词带翻译就能显示）。 拖进度条的时候，手指停的那一句会浮出来：第几句、原文、译文。想回到某一句，看准了再松手就行，不用来回试。歌词这些都是基础版就有的。 ![拖动浮出歌词]( https://i.imgur.com/SaJe7rk.jpeg) ![歌词页]( https://i.imgur.com/0xiN72x.jpeg) ## 地铁里、电梯里，网一断就停 听过的歌边播边存，还会提前缓存下一首。连不上服务器的时候，接着播缓存里的；换到一首没缓存的，等 10 秒还连不上就跳到下一首有缓存的。 打开离线模式之后，App 一个网络请求都不发。没缓存的歌会变灰，能播哪些一眼就知道。 ![离线]( https://i.imgur.com/4Ffy5fU.jpeg) ![连接状态]( https://i.imgur.com/h0EgZ2l.jpeg) ## 专辑和歌单页，想好看一点 专辑、歌手、歌单页都把封面做成页头，名字和按钮收在一座浮岛里。歌单里如果整张专辑都在，会并成一张专辑卡，不用一首首往下翻。 ![详情页]( https://i.imgur.com/F4xnUQ3.jpeg) ## 播放页，想要安静一点，或者信息多一点 播放页分极简和详细两档，每档两款皮肤，一共四款： - 极简：滑封面（左右拖封面切歌）、衬底（封面铺满上半屏） - 详细：标准（操作台，均衡器、倍速、定时、输出都在手边）、数据（大号时间加格式、码率、播放次数） ![四款皮肤]( https://i.imgur.com/B9nrOrC.jpeg) 衬底和数据两款的进度条画的是这首歌的真实波形，副歌在哪一眼就看到。每首分析一次就存下来，下载过、缓存过的歌直接用本地音频算，不多费流量。这两款皮肤和波形属于 Pro ；滑封面和标准是基础版的，进度条是一根细线。 ![真实波形]( https://i.imgur.com/AIps421.jpeg) ## 智能歌单，不想去服务器上写文件 Navidrome 本来就支持智能歌单，但要在曲库目录里放一个写满 JSON 规则的 .nsp 文件。Mu3ic 里可以直接新建：选一个模板（年代 × 语言、歌手代表作、流派、最近 N 天、高分，或者照着一个现有的歌单改），再加减条件，「满足全部」还是「满足任一」点一下就切。编辑的时候底部实时显示预计有多少首，这个数用的是手机上的曲库索引，不用等服务器。 ![新建智能歌单]( https://i.imgur.com/AqsBz2Y.jpeg) 自己建的智能歌单，以后可以在「⋯」里接着改规则。来自 .nsp 文件的那些照样能听，只是规则改不了（改了也会被下次扫描覆盖）。 ![规则编辑]( https://i.imgur.com/wdtcSNc.jpeg) 浏览和播放智能歌单是基础版就有的，规则编辑器属于 Pro 。 ## 混音，每次听都不太一样 混音是 App 自己按打分采样出来的播放列表，点一次重新抽一次： - 为你：常听热曲、冷门佳作、最近混音、高分混音 - 最爱：最爱混音、最爱专辑混音、最爱歌手混音 - 按标签：单个歌手、流派、语言、年代（ 80s 、90s……）各自一个 - 长按任意一首歌，可以「以这首开混音」，找同歌手、同流派、同语言同年代的歌接着放 ![混音]( https://i.imgur.com/DUpnXAj.jpeg) ![按标签混音]( https://i.imgur.com/6vPMtSW.jpeg) 混音很吃**曲库标签**，标签整理得越好越好用，具体要哪些标签写在后面的「注意事项」里。混音属于 Pro 。 ## 免费和 Pro 基础版是完整的播放器：不限时，没有广告，不用注册。上面说的曲库、搜索、首页、歌词、缓存和离线模式、详情页、两款免费皮肤，都是基础版就有的。另外还有歌单、收藏、评分同步回服务器，听歌记录回传，播放键长按停止，应用内更新（下载后先校验签名再装）。 Pro 解锁这些： - 下载库：专辑、歌单、歌手、单曲整份下载，最爱自动下载，离线时封面和歌词也在 - 混音、智能歌单规则编辑器 - 波形进度条和衬底、数据两款播放页皮肤，均衡器 - 三种桌面小组件（播放条、播放来源、听歌统计），歌单和混音的桌面快捷方式 - 多服务器主备自动切换、切换应用图标 ![下载库]( https://i.imgur.com/ROZwE34.jpeg) App 里可以直接买，跳到手机浏览器用支付宝付。首发一个月推广价 ¥18 （原价 ¥38 ），到 11 月 5 日。一次买断，一码一机，每年可以自己换绑两次设备。 ## 注意事项 **Navidrome 版本**：大部分功能走的是 Subsonic 接口，老版本也能用。下面几项用到了 Navidrome 自己的接口，要 0.64.0 或以上： - 新建、编辑智能歌单 - 首页的听歌统计（读的是服务器上的播放记录，所以同一个账号在别的设备上听的也算） - 语言混音（语言只有 Navidrome 自己的接口里有） 版本不够时这几项用不了（建智能歌单会提示服务器不支持，语言那一节混音不出），别的照常用。 **混音要哪些标签**： - 流派：曲目的 GENRE ，多个流派也认 - 语言：LANGUAGE ，用 ISO 639-3 的三字母码（ eng 、cmn 、jpn 、kor 、yue……），这个是 Navidrome 内置识别的标签 - 年代：曲目的年份（ DATE / YEAR ） - 歌手：单个歌手混音只给「收藏了、而且曲库里不少于 50 首」的歌手出 流派和语言不足 20 首的不单独出卡。因为太依赖标签，底栏的「混音」 tab 默认是关的，在设置 → 底栏里打开；首页的四张混音卡不受这个开关影响。 ## 领码 先在 1 楼放 10 个 Pro 码，先到先得；用完了会在楼里再放一批。一码一机，激活后就绑在这台手机上了，所以一人拿一个就好。用掉了麻烦在评论里回一下用掉的码，后面的人就不用白试了。 激活：设置 → 关于 → Pro → 输入激活码。 ## 隐私 - 激活时只发激活码，和一个加盐哈希过的设备标识（由 Android ID 算出来，换不回原值） - 购买时，建单只发项目名，查单只发订单号；付款在支付宝完成，我拿不到付款人的任何信息 - 检查更新不带任何标识 - 除此之外什么都不收集：没有统计，没有广告，没有崩溃上报。曲库和播放记录只在你自己的服务器和手机上 ## 最后 ![基础版免费]( https://i.imgur.com/uEFlk3X.jpeg) 有问题、有想要的功能，直接在这里回我就行。如果您喜欢，可以 APP 内购买 Pro 会员解锁完整体验，首月仅需~~38~~18 买断，感谢支持。

projects.title: Show HN: Paganel – Data migration with a receipt you can verify later
projects.author: stan_stork
projects.summary: Paganel comes from an old work problem: I had a large schema migration with lots of transformations and several environments to check. One of the main requirements was to validate whether the data had moved correctly, and I was not allowed to use any SaaS tools because it was forbidden for data to leave our network. Since I couldn't find any air-gapped tool that could do both the transformation and the verification (basic row counts aren't enough for transformed data), I had to write custom scripts for the entire process. Ever since then, the idea of automating complex migrations has stuck in my head, which led me to start building Paganel a year and a half ago. In Paganel, a migration is just a single declarative file. You specify where the data comes from and where it's going, and the rest goes in the same file: joins, filters, computed fields, and validation rules. If you are missing a specific source, sink, transform, or filter, you can easily extend Paganel by writing your own WASM plugin in Rust or JS. These execute inside a strict sandbox, so they don't have any filesystem or network access unless you allow it in the migration config. I also wanted to make large migrations simple, so before running a real migration, you can run pag plan to review the output schema, the DDL, and the time and memory estimates. You can also use the plan to see a sample of real rows. They get processed through the whole pipeline, which gives you absolute clarity on what will actually be inserted. One of the biggest challenges isn't just doing the migration, but verifying that everything actually moved correctly. For that, there is the --integrity flag. Pass it, and Paganel hashes the rows on the fly as they migrate, storing those hashes on disk, keyed by primary key. After the run, it uses them to spit out a 32-byte root hash for the table. Together with the row hashes, this gives you a complete 'migration receipt.' Minutes or weeks later, you can run pag verify, and it re-reads the destination, recomputes the hashes and compares them with the receipt, without connecting to the source. When the root doesn't match, you know something changed, and then verify goes through the row hashes and tells you which rows it was. It tells you that the destination still contains what Paganel wrote, but it can't tell you whether the transformation itself was correct. Another huge factor is migration speed. I created a small benchmark to measure Paganel's speed and tested it on a 100M-row migration from MySQL to PostgreSQL (with the databases on separate servers). With the default config, which is a single stream, I got about 390k rows a second. Splitting the table into four parallel streams got it to almost 940k. The number of streams is configurable for tables with an integer primary key. Enabling the --integrity flag does add some overhead, dropping those numbers to 340k and 670k, respectively. Paganel is still pre-v1.0, so there are some rough edges to be aware of: - No CDC yet: Currently, it only handles batch processing. Continuous sync with verification is the ultimate goal, but nailing the batch engine comes first. - Limited databases: Right now, Paganel only natively supports MySQL and PostgreSQL. - API changes: The project is under heavy development, meaning the config syntax might change slightly from release to release. - One-man team: I'm developing this solo. You will likely run into edge cases I haven't caught yet. - Platform testing: The full integration suite and all my own manual testing run on Linux. macOS and Windows get pre-built binaries too, but they only go through a basic smoke test. If you want to try it out, the quickstart in the README will spin up some sample databases in Docker for you. How do you verify migrations today? I'd like to know whether a receipt like this would fit into how you work.

API 流量与 Token 检视：内置轻量反向代理，位于 CLI 与模型服务商端点之间，可直观查看请求/响应报文、延迟及 Token 用量，一键开启与还原。 4. projects.summary: snap-back 是一个开源命令行工具，给 Claude Code、Codex 等编程 Agent 加上撤销功能。它在 Agent 改动前后把项目快照存进一个独立的影子 git 仓库，不碰你自己的 .git、暂存区和 stash。Agent 删错文件、改坏代码时，snap-back undo 一条命令恢复，包括被删掉的文件。适合用 Agent 写代码、又怕它一次改坏一片的开发者。 亮点 任何 Agent 都能用：snap-back wrap -- codex 包住一次会话；Claude Code 可以直接装成插件，每次工具调用前后自动快照，再用 /snap-back:undo 回滚。 撤销前先列出要恢复和要删除的文件，确认后才动手；每次恢复前还会再拍一张安全快照，所以撤销本身也能撤销。 遵守 .gitignore，跳过 nodemodules 这类目录；2 万个文件的项目首次快照约 3 秒，占用约 6 MB。 不联网，只依赖两个包（cac、chokidar），核心代码约 2200 行，MIT 协议，macOS、Linux、Windows 上都有测试。 坦白说明做不到的事：Agent 在项目外的副作用（写数据库、发请求）无法撤销，被 .gitignore 忽略的文件也不在快照里。

projects.title: Show HN: Tofu – let your agent deploy full-stack apps
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm the founder of Tofu, a code deployment platform built for agents. Paste our setup prompt to any agent you're already using and Tofu enables your agent to take your project from code to production. Current features include frontend & backend hosting (created & managed by Tofu), Postgres database (created & managed by Tofu), domain management (one-click setup for Cloudflare managed domains, manual DNS record for others), authentication, Google login, and Analytics. We built Tofu out of our personal frustrations: we're engineers who know how to code, we've deployed live products and understand the process, and our AI agents have already finished writing the code that works locally, yet taking a product fully online still took 2-3 hours: - Setup hosting, backend, database - Copy-pasting a lot of apikeys/secrets from here to there - Setting up correct redirect urls from places to places - Managing DNS records, domains - Setting up a lot services (email, 3rd parth OAuth, etc) - Payments Tofu works with any MCP-compatible agents, and here's a list of tested agents (10+ different projects end-to-end deployment via Tofu): local coding agents (Claude Code, Codex/ChatGPT, Kimi Code, DSH, Cursor), Instinct, Muse, Kimi Code cloud. None of that is hard, but each of these services have their own providers and it involves managing 5-10 different accounts. Most cloud providers have their own CLI, but it only works within their own platform and the process still involves a lot of manual interventions. Agents can call any API and use CLIs, but cannot open a Google Cloud project or put a card on file with 5 vendors. We think deployment is not a compute problem, but an accounts problem. Our endgoal is to utilize SSO across services, and provide agents the ability to deploy a live product end-to-end. We don't want to compete with any cloud providers, but to make agents actually capable of shipping "live" products. We're rolling out features to support buy domains directly from Tofu (we're an authorized reseller of Name.com), and provide more customizability to tech stacks. We're still very early and have just launched our product, please send us any feedbacks, comments, and we promise we will respond to every single one of them.

projects.summary: 自荐一个纯前端小工具 APICompat。它只想回答一个问题：你手上那个中转站，到底哪个模型走哪条协议是通的。 起因 第三方中转站（new-api / one-api 那一类）越来越多，但「它支持什么」很难问清楚： 站点文档写「兼容 OpenAI / Claude / Gemini」，没说具体到哪个模型走哪条路； 拿一个模型试一次，只能证明这一个模型 × 这一种协议通，换个模型可能全崩； 看 /v1/models 只证明端点存在，不证明任何一个模型真的能回话； 读 supportedendpointtypes，声明又经常和实测不符。 所以做成了这么一条链：先拉清单 → 按 10 种协议 × 全部可见模型跑交叉矩阵 → 逐格给状态与首块延迟 → 导出报告。

projects.title: Show HN: The Velocity Trap, the Phoenix Project for the AI Age
projects.author: ColinEberhardt
projects.summary: I'm taking a bit of a risk with this one, this is a novella I authored with the help of AI. If that offends you, please move on! Everyone on HN knows just how much AI is disrupting our industry. Although, much of the industry narrative focusses on the tools, the AI, the harnesses, and their ever-growing capabilities. We need to spend just as much, if not more time discussing the impact this is having on us. Humans will still be a significant part of the software engineering ‘system’, and many of us are rapidly trying to determine what our role will ultimately be. Storytelling is a great medium for communicating and understanding change. That’s why I really enjoy books like The Phoenix Project — a vehicle for helping people understand the DevOps transformation from a human perspective. This story is very much inspired by The Phoenix Project: a near-future account of the impact AI has on an organisation deep in the pursuit of speed, ignoring the risks and the human impact. This story was written with the help of AI. While I can write a decent technical blog post, there is no hope for me when it comes to works of fiction! projects.author: Peiiii
projects.summary: 做了个叫「小伴」的 AI 语音伙伴，交互是像给豆包打电话一样：点一下「开始通话」，直接开口说，它会用声音回答，你可以继续聊，也可以在它说到一半时打断。 现在 MIT 开源了，可以用自己的 API Key 在本机跑，也可以拿去改成自己的语音搭子。 源码： https://github.com/Peiiii/xiaoban 在线体验： https://xiaoban-voice.gemigo.app （需要登录，有用量限制；自己在本地跑不需要 GemiGo 账号） ![小伴界面]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/xiaoban/main/docs/images/desktop.jpg) 通话时不用一直按住录音键，也不用一句一句点发送。想闲聊就闲聊，想梳理事情就说出来；切到英语模式，也能和它练口语。可以关麦、静音，换音色和语速；聊完点「结束通话」。 桌面和手机版式都做了，聊天记录保存在当前浏览器，可以导出或清空。 声音目前有两种模式：默认等一段回复的音频收齐再连续播放，网络到包不均匀时更容易完整听完，代价是开口前多等一会儿；也可以切成边收边播，先听到回答。网络太差时仍可能等待或断续，扬声器回声也受设备影响，建议先戴耳机试。 自己跑需要 Node.js 22+ 和已开通实时模型的百炼 Key： ```sh git clone https://github.com/Peiiii/xiaoban.git cd xiaoban npm ci cp .env.example .env # 填写自己的百炼 Key 和业务空间实时接口地址 npm start ``` 打开 http://localhost:4318 就能开始通话。语音用千问 Qwen 3.8 Omni Flash Realtime ，API 费用自付，Key 留在服务端。语音和对话会发给模型提供商处理。本地服务只监听本机，公开部署需补鉴权和用量控制；详细配置在 README 。 这是一个早期作品。如果你也想有个自己的 AI 电话搭子，欢迎拿去用、拿去改；觉得有用，帮忙点个 star 。真实通话遇到的问题也欢迎提 issue ，别贴 API Key 。

projects.title: Show HN: Skins.dev – add the features missing from the web apps you use
projects.author: dalichelbi
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm building skins.dev : Most AI tools help you build your own tool from scratch, but usually there's already a tool that gets you 80% there. Skins is for the other 20%: you describe what's missing in a web app you use, and we handle the rest, whatever it takes: from simple JS scripts and styles up to new backend features (hosted on our Cloudflare-compatible serverless cloud), so your feature can call other APIs and even have its own SQLite database. How it works: go to the page you'd like to change and press "Record" in the extension. We use the DOM snapshots and network requests to build a replica environment where coding agents can iterate safely. The Chromium extension then injects the changes per site via chrome.userScripts (à la Tampermonkey). projects.title: Show HN: Mistis – a decoupled, E2EE protocol for mid-call user authentication
projects.author: JusMKing
projects.summary: We have built an authentication protocol enabling mid-session real-time identity verification between final users during any active communication, delivered via a proprietary decoupled channel. System allows users to send identity verification challenges to each other on-demand during communication. The goal is to prevent identity takeover by real-time audio deepfakes. It is inspired in 3DS credit card processing –taking away the UX nightmare; some similarities: decoupled rail for authentication, enrolment, user redirection to trusted authentication mechanism. The method is based on cryptographic credential management, employing only open standards via a proprietary algorithm. The server relays messages and serves for message-hardening enforcement. Cryptographic operations, source of truth and decisions are all on the client-side. The model could be considered P2P in essence and usability –despite the existence of a limited-role server as a minimal required infrastructure. Our servers do not process or store any PII. Our first use case is applied to regular carrier mobile phone calls, and requires installing a mobile app to function. Also, the protocol can be applied and integrated into any communication. It would be great if you’d like to have a look at it and let us know what you think. I will be here to discuss online. You can download the app and test it (limited testers): - Android link: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.mistis.aut... - iOS app link: https://testflight.apple.com/join/Rb5sXpwp Testing involves at least two users, as the method requires pairing (cryptographic credential exchange) previously to establishing a regular phone call in which to send identity verification challenges. I can volunteer for testing if you cannot find a peer tester. If you spot a weird bug or would like to mention anything in private, please drop a line to support@mistis.tech. Justin (Founder)

github.name: aixisstudio/Snitch
github.description: Real-time network traffic visualizer — see every connection your computer makes. Privacy-first, 100% local. / Visualiseur de trafic réseau en temps réel, 100% local.

projects.summary: Snitch 是一个开源（AGPL-3.0）的实时网络流量可视化工具。你的电脑每小时会悄悄建立数百个连接，Snitch 用动画节点图 + 世界地图把它们全部实时展示出来。支持按进程归因（知道是哪个应用在联网）、离线地理定位（内置 DB-IP Lite 数据库，查询不离开本机）、零遥测、API 默认仅绑定 127.0.0.1 并需要 token。支持 macOS / Linux / Windows，界面中英文双语。 亮点 动画力导向图 + 世界地图：本机居中，每个连接是一个节点，实时更新 按进程归因：显示每个连接由哪个应用产生（top 5） 100% 离线地理定位：内置 DB-IP Lite（gzip 打包），无任何在线查询 隐私优先：零遥测，API 仅回环 + token 认证，数据不出本机 异常检测：端口扫描、心跳外联、潜在数据外泄实时告警 中英文双语界面一键切换；演示模式（SNITCHDEMO=1）无需 root 即可体验 Docker 一键部署（Linux）；macOS 提供打包好的应用（Releases 下载）

projects.title: [魔力工作台] 一个开源版 workbuddy 替代品
projects.author: Pony996
projects.summary: 我做了一个开源版 workbuddy 替代品，你可能会问，类似的产品海了去了，重复造轮子有什么意义？ ![ScreenShot_2026-10-03_205453_642.png · 184]( https://img.cdn1.vip/i/6ac0fb3c7f690_1791032124.webp) # 缘起 事情是这样的 我在一家 AI 公司就职产品经理工作，就我用这个行业真实业务的视角，以及我接触到的一些东西来看我觉得他很有机会 公司业务说白了就是卖 token 而组成公司收入的主要客户实际上是搞蒸馏，这种客户我觉得并不优质 因为这不产生价值，是军备竞赛，一旦 AI 泡沫破灭，市场没有了钱，军备竞赛终止，公司业绩会大幅缩水，所带来的连锁反应是非常恐怖的 不过也在转型，在做企业客户，转型二字说来容易，赚钱真的是太难了，企业直客就两个特点，没钱、事多 企业用 AI 本身的目的就是为了降本增效，让他花大把的钱买 token 肯定要考虑是否值得 我们公司员工不限量使用任何大模型，成本价的情况下一个月最高的能用到五六千块 rmb ，平均使用也有 1500 左右，这个价格去企业里推，很少有公司愿意花这个钱来买 token 企业顶多能接受一个月一个坐席几百块的预算，甚至更低 一个蒸馏客户一天就能消费十几万 rmb ，而一个企业客户那，可能一个月才一两万，如果按这个来计算，这背后基础建设的投入想要回本需要拓展非常多的企业客户去平摊，也就是市场生产力需求真的爆发 大部分公司买 token 也不知道怎么用，你要跟他们讲 codex 、claudecode ，他们跟听天书一样，哪怕是程序员，大部分也都是只用过 trae 、qoder 等国产 vibecoding 应用，甚至还有的只用过豆包 这部分客户并非低端，只不过行业不同，对计算机技能接触深度不同，当然不能跟天天泡在电脑上的工作者相比 # workbuddy 的优劣势 企业更想要的是一套成熟的、高效的工作体系 所以他们大多对 workbuddy 评价是非常高的 因为都被腾讯的销售洗脑过很多次了，他们也表示 workbuddy 的业绩压力非常大，而且广发英雄贴让 fde 团队跟 workbuddy 合作一块进企业，这确实是一个共赢的合作 我参加的很多行业展会也接触到一些不同的需求，很多传统型的企业还是很看重数据安全的，他们更愿意自己私有化部署大模型，要求数据不出园区 使用自己部署的模型用来工作也需要一个能够接入的客户端，曾经这个客户端是 cherrystudio 再说一些 workbuddy 的问题吧 它最大的问题就是贵，我遇到的企业都说它好，但是又说它不好，原因就在于收费昂贵 买一个企业坐席是个人会员的两倍价格，积分还少一半，且积分非常不耐用，几个任务就没了，官方也没有说明积分的具体扣费逻辑，计费黑盒，不耐用，还贵 那么企业买了之后自定义 API 使用行不行？ 当然可以，但是 workbuddy 的自定义 API 只支持一个 openai completions 协议，像 anthropic 和 responses 协议就不支持了，而且他绑定了很多自己家模型才能使用到工具，自定义模型用不了 其实细数一些这个市场有哪些使用起来没有门槛的工具，还是挺有限的 所以我觉得这个市场还有机会，尤其是开源的 workbuddy 替代 他其实没啥门槛，护城河无非就是腾讯自家生态连接器，不给别家开放，但是办公领域有多少是用腾讯生态的？ workbuddy 这款产品定位本身就是腾讯在上一次企业办公应用全面惨败之后想要一雪前耻的东西 # 魔力工作台能做什么 dsh 本来很有希望的，但是门槛太高，把很多人拒之门外，所以我做了这款魔力工作台 像基础的 Agent 任务，PPT 制作、处理 word 、excel 、pdf 、整理文件等都是基本功 支持插件、skill 、角色库、mcp 、自定义模型三大常用协议 还支持 AI 视频生成、AI 生图、AI 剪辑等音视频方面的能力 用它来写代码也可以，我参考了 opencode 、omp 、开源版 claudecode 等编程 Agent 的核心能力，支持 LSP 、TUI 、git 工具等，可以识别语言自动安装所需的 LSP 服务 觉得有意思的话赏个 star 吧，我相信未来一定是属于开源的 https://github.com/ponysb/mlimli

projects.title: 开源 Bibo：成本极低，内置笔记、文件、任务和日历的 personal agent
projects.author: Peiiii
projects.summary: 我把 Bibo 开源了，MIT 协议。先说最想做好的三件事： 1. **成本极低。** 日常使用不需要常驻电脑，也不用一直开着 Linux 容器。只有需要运行代码时，才启动沙箱。 2. **内置个人管理工具。** 笔记、文件、任务和日历都有专门的界面。你可以直接查看、编辑和管理，也可以让 AI 来做。 3. **开源，可以自己部署。** 用自己的 Cloudflare 账号和模型 API Key ，数据存在自己的部署里，代码也可以自己改。 GitHub：[Peiiii/bibo]( https://github.com/Peiiii/bibo) 在线体验：[app.bibo.bot]( https://app.bibo.bot) 我希望它能成为每天都用得上的 personal agent 。想到什么可以随手记，需要做的事可以放进任务和日历，资料可以整理成文件；这些内容长期留着，之后还能接着用。 下面把界面都放出来。截图来自实际运行的 Bibo ，销售、订单和日程内容都是示例数据。 ### 概览 打开就能看到笔记、任务、日程和待处理信息。 ![Bibo 概览]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/v2ex-2026-10-04/bibo-overview.jpg) ### 对话 让 Bibo 阅读销售数据、总结重点，也可以让它继续整理报告和安排后续工作。 ![Bibo 对话与报告]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/v2ex-2026-10-04/bibo-chat.jpg) ### 笔记 笔记是可以直接编辑的 Markdown 文档。你自己写，或者让 Bibo 帮你整理，都能继续修改。 ![Bibo 笔记]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/v2ex-2026-10-04/bibo-notes.jpg) ### 文件 有独立的文件目录，可以打开、编辑文件。这里展示的是整理好的订单 CSV 。 ![Bibo 文件]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/v2ex-2026-10-04/bibo-files.jpg) ### 任务 任务有独立列表和详情，可以管理完成状态、优先级、描述和时间。分析出来的建议，可以接着变成待办。 ![Bibo 任务]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/v2ex-2026-10-04/bibo-tasks.jpg) projects.title: Show HN: McKinley – vector editor for SF Symbols (Mac app)
projects.author: AmyWorrall
projects.summary: McKinley is a Mac app for making SF Symbols. It costs $60 (one off purchase). SF Symbols are Apple's vector symbol format. The OS ships with thousands of them, but you can make your own for your own apps. The recommended way to make SF Symbols is to export a template from Apple's helper app, edit it in a vector editor, then re-import it and tag all the SF Symbol specific metadata. This process is usually a pain in the ass. SF Symbols support multiple weights -- you draw three, and Apple interpolates between them. This means that each of your weights needs to have the same paths in the same order, with the same number of points. Everything has to be converted to outlines for the interpolation to work, it doesn't render strokes. McKinley is my attempt to save you from that. It's a vector editor that is built around the constraints of SF Symbols. You can edit your symbol while flicking between the three weights or the four colour modes. It can save SF Symbol files or sync straight to Xcode asset catalogs. You don't have to bounce between a vector editor and a symbols converter, because McKinley is both. I'm pleased with how live previews work. I wanted to offer a preview with Apple's own renderer. But you can't load an SF Symbol in-memory at runtime. So I figured out the file format for asset catalogs, and create a temporary one and load _that_. (I blogged about how I did it: https://www.amyworrall.com/blog/previewing-sf-symbols-with-a... ) A couple of things I know people will ask: * It's a native AppKit app (not Electron or anything cross-platform) * Sold directly from my site via Stripe, not Mac App Store. * One-time purchase. License is valid on up to 5 computers, and covers all version 1.x updates. * There's a 14 day free trial, which includes saving/exporting * It is sandboxed, notarised, and all that good stuff * No analytics or network traffic, apart from updates (handled by Sparkle) and license checking (handled by Amore). Happy to answer any questions or dive into technical details if people want :)

projects.title: 【开源自荐】open-compute：开源的 Cloudflare Workers 兼容平台
projects.author: elliothux

github.name: elliothux/open-compute
github.description: Self-hosted Cloudflare Workers-compatible platform with Workers、KV、D1、R2、DO、Queues、Workflows、Cron、Cache、Images、Vectorize、AI Search、Artifacts、Static Assets、Service Bindings、Dynamic Workers、LogTail、Gateway in one Rust binary.

projects.summary: 阮老师好，自荐一下我做的 open-compute，一个可以运行在自己服务器上的 Cloudflare Workers 兼容平台，Apache-2.0 开源。 我是 Cloudflare 的粉丝，很喜欢 Workers 这套开发方式。不过我们做 B 端交付时，经常遇到客户因为数据安全要求、企业网络限制，需要把应用和数据留在自己的基础设施里。为了私有化，又得重新搭存储、队列、任务调度这些东西。所以我做了 open-compute，希望能把这套熟悉的开发体验带到客户内网。 它把运行时、部署、网关、存储、队列、工作流和管理界面打包进一个 Rust 二进制，底层使用 workerd，面向单机部署，默认使用 SQLite 和本地文件存储，不需要先搭一套 Kubernetes、外部数据库和缓存服务。 兼容是这个项目的重点：在支持范围内，现有 Cloudflare Workers 项目的业务代码一行都不用改，原来的 Wrangler 配置、Bindings 和框架适配器都能继续使用，切换部署目标即可运行。API 按 Cloudflare 的接口实现，已有的 SDK 和工具也可以复用。 目前支持 Workers、KV、D1、R2、Durable Objects、Queues、Workflows、Cron、Cache、Images、Vectorize、AI Search，以及 Static Assets、Service Bindings 等能力。具体支持范围和单机环境下的行为差异，可以查看产品矩阵。 我已经在一些 B 端客户的私有化环境里部署并跑了一段时间，也在实际交付中持续完善它。现在开源出来，欢迎有类似需求的朋友试用、反馈。 官网和文档：open-compute.dev

projects.title: Show HN: S3-Accelerator
projects.author: dangoodmanUT
projects.summary: s3-accelerator is an s3-compatible nvme cache that serves hits in under a millisecond, replicates hot objects, and stays warm when the cluster resizes. the hot object replication was inspired by groupcache [1], but that has some pretty nasty issues when the cluster resizes s3-accelerator fixes that by: 1) using rendezvous hashing to reduce the remapping when the cluster loses a node, and 2) when new nodes are added, asking the old parent for a give key for the object rather than going to s3 It also uses learnings from cloudflare that it's better to cache on a second hit than a first hit[2] It also uses ktls, splice, and sendfile so byte transfer of object chunks never hit userspace. That means it can hit millions of iops, or saturate 200Gb/s network cards, while sipping on CPU it also is parquet-aware, and has an optional SQS integration to keep the cache fresh if an object is overwritten. S3 stays the source of truth, and you can write through the cache (it wont cache the write by default) these features make s3-accelerator uniquely performant, fresh, and s3 costs extremely low. It's one of those "I'll build it one day" project ideas that Opus 5.5 finally made viable. [1] https://github.com/golang/groupcache [2] https://blog.cloudflare.com/why-we-started-putting-unpopular...

projects.title: Show HN: Levenshtein – Curated Go lint rules and CI checks
projects.author: johnjwang
projects.summary: Hey HN, I've been recently building a lot of Go projects and noticed myself setting up lint rules and CI/CD and starting from scratch each time. Also, if I found a good deterministic check to use in one repo, I'd have a hard time putting that in my other repos. So I built Levenshtein ( https://github.com/wangjohn/levenshtein ). It's a curated set of Go lint rules and verification checks that run locally and in CI. The rule set is pretty comprehensive and builds on Staticcheck and other existing analyzers, with some additional rules of my own. It includes: - Go vet - Staticcheck - Modernize - Bug finding analyzers - Vulnerability / security analyzers There's also some fun optional checks that you can configure like: - Semantic linters using Jev - Race detectors - Mutation testing for tests - and many more! I've been hooking it up to my own projects and caught dozens of bugs already. For example, one finding was a test that simulated database changes with os.WriteFile but ignored whether the writes succeeded. Would love feedback, particularly about the default rules and what should be default/what shouldn't!

projects.title: 【开源自荐】fib：性能几乎超过以往所有 Go 网络库，和 Claude 合作完成，代码几乎全部由 Claude 生成
projects.author: lesismal
projects.summary: 最近我和 Claude 合作完成了一个新的 Go 网络库，叫 fib。想法和方向是我的，代码几乎全部由 Claude 生成。它支持 TCP/UDP、TLS、HTTP/1.x、HTTP/2、HTTP/3（QUIC）和 WebSocket，HTTP handler 用的是标准库的 http.Request 和 http.ResponseWriter。 先说结果。在 GitHub Actions 上自动运行的 benchmark 里，和标准库相比，fib 在一些场景下的吞吐能高出数倍，内存也少得多；和 fasthttp 这类以性能著称的库相比，性能也有提升；和 C/C++/Rust 的框架相比，也已经很接近，有些场景还能超过。这些 Action 所在的仓库里有完整的测试代码，每个数字都可以追溯和复现。 当然，不同的硬件规格、测试参数和框架配置，跑出来的结果可能会不一样。欢迎大家在自己的机器上亲自跑一跑这些 benchmark。 先看数据 下面的数据都来自 GitHub Actions 上 lesismal/go--benchmark 几个仓库的 Docker 压测。runner 是 4 vCPU，服务端 2 核、客户端 2 核，1 万连接，1 KiB payload。每个都是单次运行，共享 runner 有噪声，几个百分点的差距可以当作持平。完整表格（包括 CPU 效率、延迟分位数）请点链接看。 先把几个主要的提升列在前面： HTTP/1.1：echo 是 net/http 的 2.3 倍，pipeline 是 net/http 的 6.9 倍、fasthttp 的 1.65 倍，内存只有 net/http 的十分之一 HTTP/2：echo 是 net/http 的 3.7 倍，multiplex 是 net/http 的 13 倍、Rust h2 的 2.6 倍 HTTP/3：吞吐是 quic-go 的 3.4 到 5.4 倍，达到 Cloudflare quiche 的九成以上 TLS：pipeline 是 crypto/tls + net 的 2.9 倍，内存约三分之一 WebSocket：echo 吞吐在 17 个参测框架里最高，只用 32 MB 内存 HTTP/1.1（Actions run，客户端是 Rust tokio） | Server | Echo TPS | Echo MEM | Pipeline TPS | Pipeline MEM | | ----------- | -------: | -------: | -----------: | -----------: | | fib | 194,671 | 32 MB | 1,140,457 | 36 MB | | axum (Rust) | 236,244 | 227 MB | 301,804 | 490 MB | | fasthttp | 139,830 | 197 MB | 692,671 | 197 MB | | net/http | 84,739 | 314 MB | 164,811 | 323 MB | echo 比 fasthttp 高 39%，内存只有它的六分之一。pipeline 场景差距最大，fib 跑到 114 万 TPS，是 axum 的 3.8 倍，内存始终在 36 MB 左右。在我自己不同连接数的测试里，fib 也基本能达到或超过 fasthttp。 HTTP/2 h2c（Actions run） | Server | Echo TPS | Echo MEM | Multiplex TPS | Multiplex MEM | | --------- | -------: | -------: | ------------: | ------------: | | fib | 129,676 | 119 MB | 333,692 | 432 MB | | h2 (Rust) | 143,107 | 246 MB | 129,729 | 870 MB | | net/http | 35,415 | 633 MB | 25,051 | 809 MB | echo 达到 Rust h2 的九成，内存只有它的一半；multiplex 则反过来领先 h2 2.6 倍。 HTTP/3（Actions run，客户端是 quiche） | Server | Echo TPS | Echo MEM | Multiplex TPS | Multiplex MEM | | ------------- | -------: | -------: | ------------: | ------------: | | quiche (Rust) | 72,919 | 387 MB | 101,233 | 881 MB | | fib | 67,396 | 504 MB | 94,443 | 1.05 GB | | quic-go | 19,545 | 1.20 GB | 17,505 | 1.80 GB | 这是提升最明显的一组：和 quic-go 相比，吞吐翻了几倍，内存还少了四到六成。和 quiche 比，内存上还多一些，这是接下来要继续做的。 TLS（Actions run，客户端是 C 的 uSockets + BoringSSL） | Server | TLS 1.3 Echo | TLS 1.3 Pipeline | MEM | | ---------------- | -----------: | ---------------: | ---------: | | fib | 103,427 | 690,000 | 180 MB | | crypto/tls + net | 92,494 | 241,106 | 285–518 MB | | uSockets (C) | 103,972 | 735,000 | 51 MB | | rustls (Rust) | 107,406 | 195,835 | 110–201 MB | echo 和 C、Rust 的实现相差不到 4%，pipeline 到了 uSockets 的九成以上，是 rustls 的 3.5 倍。 WebSocket（Actions run，客户端是 C++ uWebSockets） | Server | Echo TPS | Echo MEM | Pipeline TPS | Pipeline MEM | | ------------------------ | -------: | -------: | -----------: | -----------: | | fib | 138,592 | 32 MB | 984,917 | 32 MB | | gorilla | 122,296 | 229 MB | 205,224 | 235 MB | | nbio | 121,398 | 62 MB | 191,091 | 100 MB | | tokio-tungstenite (Rust) | 83,841 | 105 MB | 748,297 | 286 MB | pipeline 是 gorilla 的 4.8 倍，内存是它的七分之一，不过还落后 uws 和 fnet 一些。 除了网络层，fib 用的协程池 taskpool 也可以单独使用。CI 每次 push 都会把它和 nbio、ants、gopool、fnet 在 Linux、macOS、Windows 上对比一遍，结果在事件循环式的提交场景下领先比较明显。 这些提升不是靠某个技巧换来的，而是来自一种和标准库不太一样的架构。要说清楚它，得先从线程说起。 从线程说起 传统的 C/C++ 服务端大多是单进程、少量线程的架构。线程很贵：栈要占内存，切换要进内核，开几百上千个就已经很吃力了。线程少，阻塞的代价就高，一个线程卡在一次慢查询上，它负责的所有请求都得跟着等。所以 C/C++ 的网络库基本都走同一条路：epoll/kqueue 做事件驱动，socket 设成非阻塞，业务逻辑拆成回调，耗时的事情丢给线程池。性能是有了，代价是代码被切成一段一段的回调，状态要自己保存，写起来和读起来都累。 C/C++ 和很多其他语言后来也有了协程，C++20 的 coroutine、各种第三方库、Rust 的 async/await 都是。但大多数情况下，协程的生命周期和调度仍然要自己操心：谁来 resume，在哪个线程上跑，帧和栈归谁管，跨过挂起点的引用还有没有效。跟 Erlang 的进程、Go 的协程比起来，这些方案理解和使用的门槛都高不少。 Go 的协程和它的边界 Go 在这一点上舒服得多。协程比进程、线程轻得多，几千到几万个协程照样跑得很顺。标准库的 net 其实也是事件驱动的：runtime 里的 netpoller 用 epoll/kqueue 等事件，事件来了再唤醒阻塞在 Read 上的协程。对用户来说接口是同步的，这也是 Go 做服务端这么流行的原因之一。 但标准库的用法比较单一。拿到一个 net.Conn，通常至少要有一个协程一直在 Read 它。1 万个连接就是 1 万个协程，100 万连接就是 100 万个协程，每个协程有自己的栈，再加上每个连接的 bufio.Reader、bufio.Writer。连接大部分时间是空闲的，这些内存却一直占着，GC 和调度器的压力也跟着上来。上面表格里 net/http 动辄几百 MB 的内存，主要就是这么来的。也有一些框架用 pre-fork 多进程的办法，把连接分散到多个进程里，减轻单个进程里 runtime 的压力，但这又带来了进程间协作、部署和监控上的麻烦。 fib 的做法：事件驱动 + 非阻塞接口 + 可配置的协程池 这些年我一直在做的是另一种方案。和 runtime 一样，用 epoll/kqueue/IOCP 做事件驱动，但不给每个连接配一个常驻的读协程。连接可读时，事件循环把它交给协程池里的一个 worker，worker 读数据、解析协议、调用户的 handler、把响应写回去，这一轮做完 worker 就回到池里。空闲的连接只是一个结构体，不占协程，也不占读写缓冲。前面表格里 fib 几十 MB 的内存，就是这么省下来的。 关键在协程池的大小。C/C++ 的线程池一般也就几十个线程，handler 里一阻塞，池子很快就耗尽，其他连接只能干等，所以只能全异步。Go 不一样，即使是限制了大小的协程池，也可以开到几千甚至几万个协程。这个并发度足够让用户在 handler 里继续用同步的方式调用下游的基础设施，比如 RPC、SQL，不用担心几个慢请求把池子占满，让其他连接等很久。 这样一来，连接数由事件驱动来承载，并发度由协程池来承载，业务代码还是同步的写法，连接数和协程数不再绑在一起。 fib 默认的池子上限是 GOMAXPROCS × 1000 个 worker，随负载伸缩，闲下来的 worker 会被回收，所以上限设得高并不浪费。如果你的 handler 基本不阻塞，可以调小；如果下游很慢，可以调大；也可以换成自己的池： go config := fib.DefaultConfig() config.SetPoolSizing(20000, 0) // worker 上限 // 或者 config.SetTaskPool(myPool) 从 nbio 到 fib：和 Claude 一起写 这个方案我不是第一次做。前几年我手写了 nbio，支持 TLS、HTTP/1.x 和 WebSocket，也有不少朋友在生产环境里用。但一个人的精力有限，HTTP/2、HTTP/3、QUIC 这些协议工作量太大，一直没能做。 这一两年 AI 模型进步得很快，于是有了 fib。这次是我和 Claude 合作，代码几乎全部由 Claude 生成。到目前为止，fib 支持： TCP、UDP、Unix socket，Linux 上用 epoll，macOS 上用 kqueue，Windows 上用 IOCP TLS 1.0–1.3，握手用 crypto/tls，握手之后的记录层加解密由 fib 自己做 HTTP/1.x、HTTP/2（h2 和 h2c）、HTTP/3，其中 QUIC 和 QPACK 是从头写的，不依赖 quic-go WebSocket，可以跑在 HTTP/1.1、HTTP/2 和 HTTP/3 上 异步的 HTTP/1、2、3 和 WebSocket 客户端，chi 风格的 Router，常用的中间件 用起来和标准库差不多 性能和架构说了这么多，用起来其实很简单。HTTP handler 用的是标准库的 http.Request 和 http.ResponseWriter，所以现有的 net/http handler、http.ServeMux、http.FileServer，甚至 chi、gin 的 engine，都可以直接跑在 fib 上： go mux := http.NewServeMux() mux.HandleFunc("GET /hello/{name}", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r http.Request) { fmt.Fprintf(w, "hello %s over %s\n", r.PathValue("name"), r.Proto) }) config := fib.DefaultConfig() config.Addr = "127.0.0.1:8080" engine, err := fib.Bind(config, fibhttp.NewHandler(fibhttp.HandlerFunc( func(c fibhttp.Context, r http.Request) { mux.ServeHTTP(c, r) }, ))) if err != nil { panic(err) } engine.Run() 同一个端口同时服务 HTTP/1.x 和 h2c；换成 TLS 就通过 ALPN 协商 HTTP/2；绑定一个 UDP engine 就是 HTTP/3，handler 不用改。 最后 代码主要由 Claude 生成，所以测试格外重要。项目做了大量的测试和 CI：HTTP/1 与 net/http、curl 的一致性测试，h2spec，和 quic-go 的 HTTP/3 互通测试，Autobahn WebSocket 测试，还有 fuzz。我自己的一些服务也已经跑在 fib 上，目前没发现什么问题。 更多内容请看 fib 的文档：README、架构、协议流程，以及 HTTP/1、HTTP/2、HTTP/3 的说明。 希望更多人能试试 fib，有问题、反馈或建议，欢迎提 issue 和 PR。 谢谢！

projects.author: brightk
projects.summary: 各位 V 友大家好！ 不知道平时有没有同样喜欢在早晨通勤或工间摸鱼时，玩一把 **Wordle 、Krillion 、Chronophoto** 这类每日谜题（-dle 系列游戏）的朋友？ 这些游戏最大的乐趣就是每天大家面对同一道题，比拼联想能力和词汇量。但前段时间玩 Krillion 的 Daily Dive 时，经常碰到一两道偏门题卡壳。去搜答案时发现网上的体验非常差： 1. **粗暴剧透**：一搜答案直接大字把正解糊在脸上，瞬间毫无成就感； 2. **满屏牛皮癣**：老牌答案站动辄几十个弹窗和欺诈广告，页面卡顿且体验糟糕； 3. **缺少策略**：像 Krillion 这种按答案“冷门度 / 稀有度（ Rarity ）”计分的游戏，根本没有解析和同类推荐。 --- ### 💡 做了什么？ 利用国庆假期，我自己写了一个轻量、专注的每日谜题伴侣站： 👉 **[dleanswers.com]( https://dleanswers.com/)** 我们想做点不一样的： 1. **三级阶梯提示（防剧透机制）**： - 搜提示的人大多不想直接看答案。提示页设计了 3 级渐进线索：**分类范围 ➜ 字母结构 ➜ 高斯模糊强线索**。只有你主动点击，才会逐层解锁，绝不误瞄剧透。 2. **直出答案与冷门度评分**： - 确实赶时间或想跟朋友复盘时，答案页首屏直接陈列 7 题正解与稀有度等级（ Common / Rare / Legendary ），方便比对得分。 3. **无限练习模式（ Unlimited Sandbox ）**： - 每天 7 题做完意犹未尽？站内做了本地无限答题模拟器，无需登录，可无限制刷随机类别并测算稀有度。 4. **同类每日游戏推荐**： - 整理了除 Wordle 之外的 10 款高质量同类独立游戏（ Chronophoto 看老照片猜年份、Scrandle 猜美食等），解决游戏荒。 --- ### 🛠️ 技术栈与架构 全站走极致轻量路线： - **框架**：Next.js 16 (App Router) + Tailwind CSS + TypeScript - **架构**：全站 100% 静态化预渲染（ SSG ），毫秒级首屏加载（ Lighthouse 接近满分） - **部署**：托管于 Cloudflare Pages 全球 CDN ，配置边缘缓存与严格安全头 - **承诺**：纯净无弹窗，代码开源级透明，已接入基础合规隐私政策 --- ### 💬 想请教大家： 1. 页面交互（尤其是阶梯提示的展开手感和无限练习器）还有哪些可以改进的地方？ 2. 大家平时还在玩哪些小众但设计精巧的 `-dle` 系列 daily puzzle 独立游戏？欢迎在评论区安利，我后续会陆续整理更新进站里！ 体验地址：**[https://dleanswers.com]( https://dleanswers.com/)** 非常感谢大家的体验和建议，求轻拍！🙏

projects.summary: 大家好，我是 Burrow 的维护者，最近发布了首个版本 v0.1.0，想自荐一个面向小团队和自托管服务的轻量单点登录项目。 Burrow 是一个 MIT 开源的 OIDC 身份提供商，用于集中管理账户、登录和应用访问权限。它受 Casdoor 启发，采用独立实现，聚焦单组织、单实例部署。 主要特点： 部署简单：Go 后端与 React 界面打包为一个二进制，也提供 Docker Compose 部署包；生产使用 PostgreSQL，开发支持 SQLite，无需 Redis 或消息队列。 统一登录：支持接入 OIDC 的 Web / SPA 应用，共享 Burrow SSO 会话，授权码流程默认要求 PKCE S256。 密码 + TOTP：所有用户必须绑定验证器；首次使用临时密码登录时需修改密码并完成 MFA。 账户与权限管理：提供用户、用户组、自定义角色、应用登录权限、管理操作审计和个人应用门户。 双语和主题：支持英文、简体中文，以及浅色、深色和跟随系统主题。 此前已在本地完成 Grafana、Nightingale、Harbor 的 Web 登录人工验收，仓库提供相应接入示例。v0.1.0 提供 Linux amd64 二进制、容器镜像和部署包，推荐容器安装。

projects.title: Show HN: Spens sandboxed, observable coding agents
projects.author: floydhead01
projects.summary: Spens is a tool created to standardized sandboxing (good enough) and observability around coding agents. It leverages docker, nono and mitmproxy to create a reproducible sandbox environment for agents, that captures all traffic and helps you understand what your coding agent is doing and when. Right now pi, opencode, claude and codex are supported out of the box, with node and python - but you can configure any agent or environment. It was created under the realization while working under different repos and agents, that 1. agents do weird stuff sometimes (like try and nuke a folder or poke around your HD) 2. statistics and usage collection is not really consistent (and some like Claude and Codex try and hide info) 3. reproducibility of agents across devices was challenging. Instead of setting up bespoke environments each time , we needed a way to automate it. And thus Spens was born. One note on the security aspect - I write good enough cause it is docker so unless your running something like gVisor it is possible for the agent to escape the sandbox (esp with a loose nono config) - all though in practice I've not seen this behavior. Second note - if your on a mac you need orb stack, as the run times take advantage of specific Linux security features that are not available via docker on mac (windows is fine since under the hood, docker leverages wsl)

projects.title: Show HN: Fumble – keybr, but it learns from everything you type (macOS)
projects.author: alexmcconnellyc
projects.summary: I love keybr, but it only sees the ten minutes a day I spend on keybr, not the ten hours I spend typing elsewhere. Can’t improve what you don’t measure. (A)I made Fumble is a macOS menu-bar app that watches you type (all day, all local), works out which keys/key pairs are costing you time and gives you lessons built around them. One thing that surprised me: my slowest key is B, but the one costing me the most time is G. It's less than half as slow, but I press it three times as often. And 7 of my 10 worst key pairs start with space. I need to get better at starting words. Some design decisions HN might want to argue with: - I rank weak keys by time lost, not how slow they are. Time lost is how far a key is over your baseline, times how often you press it. A key 40ms slow that you hit 2k times costs more than one 220ms slow that you hit 50 times. The goal isn't to practice the slowest keys, it's to raise your WPM. - Your baseline is the median of your own per-key p95s, not the p95 of every keystroke pooled together. Pooling lets a common slow key drag the baseline up and hide itself, and those are the keys that slow down the whole show. - Slow finger vs thinking: pause adapts to each key pair based on your own median for that pair. There's no flat cutoff. - The WPM figure shows you what it left out: keystrokes injected by software (text expanders, Keyboard Maestro, osascript), autorepeat, idle time and practice sessions. Every exclusion can be seen in the dropdown. Privacy: it records physical keycodes and timings not characters. What goes to disk is counters and latency histograms, with no keystroke sequence. Also records nothing while a password field has focus. There's no network code/account/telemetry. PRIVACY.md lists the remaining risk (adjacent-pair frequencies) and gives commands to verify all of this yourself. It can't be on the Mac App Store, because it needs Input Monitoring and the store requires sandboxing. The download is signed and notarized, so it opens like any normal Mac app. Free and open source, written in Swift for macOS 14+. Download: https://fumble.alexmcconnell.ie Source: https://github.com/alexiscodingbits/Fumble Warning: early days. Not everything has been tested in the wild yet. The thing I'd most like ideas on is word choice for the weak-spot drills. Right now it takes my top 5 weak keys and top 5 weak pairs and leans towards words that contain them. That treats every weak spot as equal, and it picks words one at a time. What I actually want is the set of 30 words that wins back the most time overall, weighted by how much each weak spot is costing me. It feels like a set-cover problem, and I'm sure there's a smarter way to do it than mine. If you've worked on anything like this, I'd love to hear how you'd approach it.

projects.title: 【工具自荐】NetWasm：C# 编译到 WASM，Hello World 只要 82.5 KiB
projects.author: zion-sati

github.name: zion-sati/NetWasm
github.description: NetWasm rebuilds .NET for WebAssembly - because cramming .NET Core into Wasm doesn’t make it a WASM platform.

projects.summary: NetWasm 是面向 WebAssembly 和 WASI 的独立 .NET 编译器和运行时。编译器前端用 Roslyn 把 C# 编译成 CIL，再由 NetWasm 把 CIL 编译成 Wasm。CoreLib 和运行时也是独立实现，最终产物不依赖 CoreCLR 或 Mono，也不带 dotnet.js 和独立应用 DLL。 想做的事很简单：保留 C# 的泛型、异常处理和自动内存管理，同时让程序只带上实际用到的部分。 体积实测 同样是 Console.WriteLine(42)，两种编译方案的结果如下： | 编译方案 | 未压缩 Wasm 体积 | | --- | ---: | | NetWasm | 82.5 KiB | | .NET 11 RC1 Blazor WebAssembly AOT | 14.58 MiB | 后者约为前者的 181 倍。NetWasm 的数字已经包含运行时和精确 GC；Blazor 这边用 Release 发布，开了完整裁剪、AOT 后 IL 剥离，以及面向体积的编译和链接优化。 这里比的是同一段输出逻辑在两种技术栈下的 Wasm 体积。NetWasm 输出的是 WASI 组件，Blazor 这边统计的是浏览器实际加载的原生 Wasm 和 Webcil 程序集；两边都不含 JavaScript、HTML 和 Wasm 宿主。 完整测试配置与复现说明 不止 Hello World 也做了一个可以直接用的应用：Regex Storm with NetWasm。 它用的是 .NET 自己的正则表达式引擎，编译成 Wasm 后在浏览器里提供匹配、捕获组查看、替换和分割，不是拿 JavaScript 正则模拟。Wasm 文件经 Brotli 压缩后约 325 KB，不含页面其他资源。正则和待处理文本都在本地处理，不上传后端，整个应用可以部署成静态网站。 另外还有 NetWasm Playground，可以直接编辑、编译、运行 C#。编译也在浏览器本地完成，不会把代码提交到服务器，不用先装工具链。 当前状态 项目还没到 1.0，兼容性仍在完善。采用闭世界编译，通用运行时反射是明确不支持的设计取舍，不是以后要补的功能。 许可方面，CoreLib、运行时库和模板等是 MIT 许可；编译器和开发工具用 NetWasm Community License，源码可看，但不是 MIT。 中文介绍：嫌 .NET Wasm 太大？我重写了编译器和运行时 欢迎拿实际用的 C# 代码来试，反馈兼容性问题。

projects.title: Show HN: Syn – Approve remote sudo requests from your Mac
projects.author: ferrerluis
projects.summary: I built Syn to review and approve individual sudo requests from a remote machine using Touch ID on my Mac. The problem came up about five minutes after I set up my Raspberry Pi with Ubuntu Desktop and Codex. I wanted an always-on personal agent with Browser Use, Computer Use, and a residential IP, accessible from both my phone and laptop (keep in mind, this was before Muse and Dots dropped). But a few prompts in, in order to run a command that needed `sudo`, the agent asked me to enter an administrator password in a terminal that–to me as a client on my Macbook–seemingly didn't exist. I then realized: "this dude has some password prompt open on its TTY, and I simply cannot see it." Unrestricted passwordless sudo would have removed that interruption, but I wanted to keep approving administrator actions myself, so setting up my Pi pivoted into building a Mac app. And so Syn was born: Syn hooks into sudo after its policy check. It pauses the invocation and shows the machine, account, executable, and arguments on the paired Mac, where I can approve it with fresh Touch ID or Mac-password authentication. Each approval is cryptographically signed and bound to that specific invocation. The unprivileged network service only relays signed requests and decisions; sudo executes its original command. The devices communicate directly over mutually authenticated TLS, without the need for a cloud relay. Interactive terminal use also has a password fallback, and Syn works with any eligible commands regardless of which agent—or person—started them. Current support is macOS 15+ on Apple silicon and Ubuntu 26.04 ARM64 with classic sudo.ws 1.9.x. I have mine set up between my Raspberry Pi and my Macbook with NordVPN Meshnet in the mix to ensure I can connect when outside my LAN, but it should work the same with any compatible VPS or using another virtual LAN (like Tailscale). If this fits your setup, I’d love folks to try it and share feedback! It's an open-source project, so PRs are super super welcome.

projects.title: Show HN: PhreshOS – OS for Web Apps
projects.author: zouhirdx

github.name: PhreshOS/system
github.description: An open-source system for apps built with web technology. You and your AI agents use them from one desktop in the browser.

projects.summary: I'd like to share my experience building this system with you. It's an operating system for web applications, and it took me about six months to develop this model. The idea is that every time I build a web tool, I need to design the infrastructure, including authentication and communication. If it's a WebSocket, it's even more complicated; I need another port for each application. I couldn't find any neutral tool that provided all of this ready-made, allowing me to build my tools directly on top of it. This is where the PhreshOS project began. It's an open-source, neutral platform for any web application, with everything ready-made: authentication, two-way communication without any configuration, and more. Another key feature is that the applications run as Node.js threads, instead of each application using its own Node.js. This means that on a simple server, dozens of applications can run without any problems, unlike if each application had its own Node.js. Furthermore, AI agents can use the services of these applications and interact with the same state displayed by your application's interface, without needing a separate interface of their own. The project and all its associated packages are open source under the MIT license. I welcome all your feedback, both encouraging and critical.

projects.title: Show HN: Breadcrumb, record everything on your mac + context manager for AI
projects.author: jv22222
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Justin. Breadcrumb records everything you do on your Mac (screen + meetings + AI transcripts + what you and your AI decided) and turns it into memory your AI can search. It's local and encrypted. You can also teach it rules by talking to it and it makes sure the right rules turn up in the right context. Works with Claude Code / Codex / Cursor / opencode. All of this is exposed to your AI as 30+ MCP tools (here's the definitions): https://innerloop.works/breadcrumb/mcp I started it in June because I wanted to understand what was going on with my AI dev work. Then it just kept growing as I jammed on it 10 hours a day for 3 months. I started by recording every screen so I could jump back to a moment and see what I'd been doing with the AI. Then I added MCP so the AI could search it. Then time tracking. Then meetings with transcripts and timestamped screenshots. After that I started feeding the data back in. At first it was just a few relevant memories in the prompt. Then I started adding rules and rules modules. Then I started recording the AI transcripts and all the other stuff the AI did (subagents, tools etc). I wanted a complete record so I could go back and see what the AI did and why. I found the more data the AI had the more useful it became. One example. I got off a zoom call with the team at the day job and said: "Review the meeting I just had, find all the bugs we discussed, and create JIRA tickets with screenshots." It read the transcript. Found every bug we mentioned, pulled the screens from the screen timeline, spun up my local server, diagnosed each bug, reviewed the code, created 14 tickets in JIRA with diagnosis and likely fixes, attached 12 screenshots as evidence, and created a nice Slack message to send to my colleagues. I never built a workflow for any of that. Claude had the meeting record, Breadcrumb tools, and rules I'd accumulated. It basically chained the steps together itself. My favorite thing about the system is observability of my own work as an AI developer. I can trace a bug all the way back to the first thing I said (or the first thing the AI did) that caused it. Then I can add a rule so it doesn't happen again. Anyway, my working system is simply Claude Desktop + Breadcrumb + Markdown. I find I don't need anything else. It's local software for one person. Local models for transcription and diarization. Data encrypted with SQLCipher and a passphrase. You can exclude any apps, websites, words and phrases. Breadcrumb itself only makes one network call which is a daily update check. (but of course your AI will use it and that is local or cloud depending on what you use). It runs cool about 12% of one core on average (M series mac has 8+). You can set it to just save OCR text or to save screenshots. If just OCR it's about 12mb day (a lot of telemetry, indexing etc). If you record screenshots on meetings it's about 120mb/hour (1 every 2 secs). It can also record screenshots of everything that's heavy at about 160mb/day. It does local classification/naming with ollama with Gemma 3 4B (2.5 GB). It's 100% free. There's no account you can just download and start using it. I'll monetize it via E2EE cloud sync and team sync. It's open beta. Just one developer working on it. Requires 16GB+ M Series Mac. Thanks for reading! https://innerloop.works/breadcrumb (homepage) https://innerloop.works/breadcrumb/download (direct download) https://innerloop.works/breadcrumb/mcp (mcp definition)

projects.title: Show HN: Silta: family assistant on Matrix with continuity across context limits
projects.author: dmitry-markin
projects.summary: Silta is a self-hosted assistant serving multiple users from a single Matrix account, used by me, family, and close friends for the last three weeks. It runs on Claude Code with each person using their own Claude subscription. Silta answers everyday questions, conducts web research (presenting the results as PDFs), performs scheduled tasks to monitor/research something and notify you if needed. It uses a deliberate handoff & compaction procedure, writing the compaction summary itself with a custom prompt, so the thread of the conversation and its picture of the user is preserved across context limits. As it turned out, the assistant accessible in a continuous chat (contrary to ChatGPT / Claude Web sessions) builds up better context about you and your tasks, and provides more relevant answers and help. It runs on Claude Code as the only allowed way to use a personal Claude subscription. Using Claude Code also spares me developing a harness, at the cost of tracking changes as new versions of Claude Code are released. The assistant itself (the daemon, the channel plugin, the supervisor, and the deployment) is open-source, while the model and the harness are Anthropic's and proprietary. Silta is deployed to a dedicated VM with separate Linux users per session and systemd hardening, protecting sessions from each other. Claude Code's bubblewrap sandbox is used to protect the Claude credential and the harness's state from the agent. This does not protect from prompt injections coming from search results and potentially leaking user data. Matrix E2EE protects the conversation from a Matrix server operator, but everything in the context is of course sent to the model provider. Private content is never logged, and the operator is expected to respect the privacy and not read the session transcripts on disk. Additionally, it is recommended to use full-disk encryption and tell the users how their data is handled. Silta only works in its workspace with files explicitly shared by users in the chat. Giving it access to a user's own computer or services like email is not planned. Since Opus 5.5 has been released, it is possible to run a session on a $20 Claude Pro subscription. Before that, only Fable 5.1 was pleasant enough to talk to. When run on Anthropic API, a moderately used session extrapolates to $100-$150 per month, with each research run costing $6-$12. Silta is built with Claude Code and Silta itself. The design, review, deployment, and testing are mine.

projects.title: Show HN: Beyond "chat with your database" – agentic data exploration
projects.author: sandhya6
projects.summary: Business intelligence is changing. AI can now do more than turn a question into a single SQL query: it can investigate a question through a series of queries, examining the result of one query to decide what to query next. Today, to answer a business question against a database, analysts use a tool like Tableau: they select relevant data, build an initial view using fields, filters, calculations, and visualizations, then look for patterns or anomalies. They form hypotheses and test them — filtering by region, drilling into customer cohorts, comparing time periods, or creating calculations to validate or rule out an explanation. They repeat this process until the evidence supports an answer, then save a workbook or dashboard for others to review and monitor. With a single question, AI can now perform much of this exploratory loop: it can investigate the data, follow the evidence through multiple queries, and present the supporting analysis. This is agentic data analysis — AI autonomously decides what to investigate next based on the results it has already found. Reportr puts agentic AI at the center of the experience, then builds complementary capabilities around it to address AI's limitations: SEMANTIC LAYER Production databases are rarely clean: columns that are no longer used, cryptic names like status2, misc, or flag, columns whose meaning has quietly shifted over time, tables that linger long after their purpose is gone, and so on. This is known as schema rot. AI tools guess wrong against schemas like this. Reportr's semantic layer lets you give tables and columns business-friendly names and descriptions, document relationships, capture business rules, and flag what AI should ignore — so it's working from what your data means, not just what it's called. USER OVERSIGHT AI-generated answers can be wrong. Reportr lets you inspect the SQL executed to arrive at an answer. It also provides explanations of what the SQL does (understandable by business users), and how it works (intended for technical users). You can review the analysis rather than simply accepting AI's conclusions. BETTER USER EXPERIENCE Reportr UI is specifically optimized for chatting with a database. Database queries often return large number of records. Ask which customers haven't placed an order in the last 90 days, and the answer is a list of customers. Reportr displays tabular data in an interactive grid that can handle thousand of records without breaking a sweat. The grid supports sorting, searching, and filtering. REPORTS AND DASHBOARDS Chat is ephemeral. Every conversation starts fresh, and that's fine for exploration — but not for information you need every week. When a chart or table reveals something worth tracking, save it as a report. Combine reports into dashboards to monitor changes over time, share findings, and keep important insights accessible without having to ask the same questions again. ROLE BASED ACCESS CONTROL Not everyone on your team needs the same level of access. Reportr's role-based access control lets you give each user exactly the permissions they need — from view-only access to report building, database management, and full administrative control. CENTRALIZED MANAGEMENT Reportr is a web application — there's nothing to install, nothing to update, and no desktop app to manage across your team. Database connection strings, AI keys, are all managed centrally. Reportr can connect to all supported databases directly, MCP servers and drivers are not needed. INSTALL ON-PREMISE Reportr can be self-hosted on your own infrastructure, ensuring your data never touches our servers. You can supply your own AI API key. Your data will not be used for training AI models. If you use Claude on AWS Bedrock, Amazon additionally guarantees that your data is never stored or used for training — and Bedrock is HIPAA eligible. GIVE IT A WHIRL Visit https://reportr.com to give it a try. We look forward to getting your feedback. Reportr is easy to try: you can provision a sample database with the press of a button and start asking questions right away. Or connect your own database and analyze your own data. You can ask up to five questions for free.

projects.author: yolandac
projects.summary: Hey HN! Yolanda and Spencer here - wanted to share a token compression tool that we’ve built for ourselves to save 30% costs on codex! After maxing out sub and burning $700/day per person on api, we fine tuned a compression model to trim codex's tool call output to reduce input token + cache. It cut down tokens by 29.6% and now I just leave it on by default in Codex. To avoid messing up w/ cache, we use proxy + fine tuned qwen model trained on preserving agent trajectory to remove tool call results before they go back to the model, leaving kv cache untouched. The cli is free for everyone to use ( https://github.com/spenmcke/compress ). Just lmk ur feedback and hacks to shave even more costs on astra! If you want to integrate it into your product to offer the best models at low cost, I can set you up with an sdk and api keys PS: It’s built for coding agents, not conversational agents. I optimized it for file retrieval accuracy, trajectory preservation, and quality to get up to 30% cost reduction depending on how context-heavy the task is. On security and privacy side, it's a proxy wrapping your local codex and ZDR so it doesn't retain any queries. It’s on by default in codex and when you don’t want compression, you can use `codex --uncompress` to disable it. Give it a try: code is in https://github.com/spenmcke/compress You can install the cli using `curl -fsSL https://install.everestagi.com/install.sh | sh && source ~/.config/everest/shell.sh` Love to hear any feedback and learn your hacky ways to save token costs too!

projects.title: Show HN: Helo – An email API from former Postmark folks
projects.author: Archanian
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Ryan, engineer and co-founder at Helo ( https://www.helohq.com ) - an email API for sending transactional and marketing email from your application: password resets, receipts, notifications, newsletters, etc. Most of our team worked together at Postmark for many years, so we know what it takes to build a reliable email service. If you've ever loved a product and then watched it get acquired, you probably know the rest of that story. We started Helo to keep building the kind of product we're good at, improve on what we have learned, take good care of our customers, and stay independent while doing it. We're bootstrapped and plan to stay that way. Helo covers everything you'd expect from a developer-focused email service: - REST API and SMTP, with SDKs for Ruby, JS, C#, Python and Go (more to come) - Separate infrastructure for transactional and broadcast mail - Event logs, stats, webhooks, suppressions, unsubscribes, flexible permissions - Usage-based pricing with no arbitrary feature gates - https://www.helohq.com/pricing Beyond the fundamentals, we've also put a lot of work into multi-tenant sending. When you're a platform sending on behalf of your own customers, you need to keep one bad sender from hurting everyone's deliverability, let customers send from their own domains, and keep stats and unsubscribes separate per customer. We've built Helo to address all of these concerns, while also allowing flexibility in how the relationships between domains, webhooks, credentials, etc. are defined amongst your tenants. For example, you can share one verified domain across all your customers while letting a few use their own, send all events to one webhook or split them per tenant, and give tenants isolated credentials with permissions limited to exactly what they need. If you've built multi-tenant sending before, what was most painful? Is there something you wish your email provider handled for you but doesn't? I'd love to hear about it.

projects.title: Show HN: Desbordante 2.5.0 Released
projects.author: chernishev
projects.summary: Almost a year has passed since Desbordante’s last release, and now we’re rolling out a new one — 2.5.0. Desbordante is an open-source, high-performance data profiler that finds and validates complex patterns in data using a bunch of advanced algorithms. Unlike the black-box ML approaches that dominate today, Desbordante takes a symbolic, explainable approach to data analysis, producing explicit rules or rule-shaped artifacts that are verifiable, such as data dependencies, association rules, or other patterns. It’s a different way to analyze data, and it works well alongside black-box models. Unlike free-form model output, these patterns have precise semantics and can be validated algorithmically against the data. And, importantly, no hallucinations or misclassification. This release adds 9 new patterns, including support for another dataset type: sequences in data. That brings the total to 4. We also picked up Python 3.15, which just came out. On top of the new patterns, there was a lot of infrastructure work too — mostly invisible to users, but important. Full changelog: https://github.com/Desbordante/desbordante-core/releases/tag...

projects.summary: Speech Wingman 让你用自然语言写下讲话时想注意的规则，在 Apple Silicon Mac 上本地识别中英混合发言，并在命中时给出原话和简短提醒。新版支持每行独立规则、随发言语言切换提醒，以及桌面悬浮按钮。运行无需云端服务，适合演讲和沟通练习；当前是需要自行构建的源码预览版。 亮点 项目维护者自荐，更新至 0.3.0 源码预览。 离线与隐私： 转录和规则推理在本机完成。应用及辅助进程使用 macOS 沙盒，没有网络权限；不会自动保存录音或会话转录，无需运行时账号或 API key。 独立规则： 每行是一条单独判断的条件，例如“说到 banana 就提醒”和“说汤姆坏话就提醒，赞扬不提醒”。模型只看当前定稿片段，不发送累计对话历史。 中英混说与桌面控制： 同一识别器处理中文、英文和混合发言；提醒语言跟随当前发言。可拖动的悬浮按钮一键开始或停止监听。 可学习的实现： SwiftUI/AppKit + Silero VAD + SenseVoiceSmall + Qwen3 4B，包含音频分段、跨进程推理、逐条规则检查、过期结果取消与引用校验。 有范围的验证： 本次 28 条合成文本用例、14 组核心测试通过；早期短句音频测试约 1 秒出现首段转录（Apple M4 / 16 GB、模型已加载）。这不是提醒延迟或真实场景准确率保证；提醒还需要额外推理时间。 当前需要自行构建，没有现成或公证安装包。要求 Apple Silicon / macOS 14+，建议 16 GB 内存；首次开发准备需要联网下载依赖和模型，构建完成后离线运行。多条规则和长发言可能延迟提醒，模型会有漏报或误报。源码 MIT，模型权重适用各自上游许可，包括 SenseVoiceSmall 的 FunASR 模型协议。

projects.author: jkalbfeld
projects.summary: Hey friends, I've been working on this idea since 2019, and wanted to share it and see who might be interested. I built a BGP network full of nodes that collect threat data, put it on a blockchain, and put it into a BGP community that anyone can peer with over GRE. The external network ASN is AS23026. Basically, you sign up on the website -- you can create an account with your email or with peeringdb or a thoughtwave account, set up a private ASN and it spits out a router config that you can use to start blackholing routes. I have been using it for months now on my edge router (AS54380) and it has cut SSH attacks down drastically. It doesn't do volumetric protection against DDoS, but it will give you protection against brute force attacks. It ingest spamhaus, a bunch of other feeds as well as fail2ban from participants and also our own attack intelligence. It's $59/month after the two week trial, and you can cancel at any time. I have a support ticket system. Would love to get some feedback.

projects.title: 分享一个开源的本机 AI 网关：中转、国产模型、Claude Code、Codex 放在一起管，每个请求花了多少钱都看得到
projects.author: Faz
projects.summary: 先说适合谁：同时用 Claude Code 、Codex ，手上有好几个中转或国产模型的 key ，被 CC Switch 切换折腾过的，可以试试。 ![概览]( https://thinkwat.ch/lite/overview.webp) ## 之前用 CC Switch 的几个痛点 - **切上游总要重启客户端。（ proxy 模式也没有特别好用）** - **Codex 初始化时输入的 key 被它学了过去，结果上游直接炸了。（好像最近修了）** - **Codex 换了供应商，旧会话就接不上**（[#7257]( https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/7257)，四十多楼，还开着）。 - **路由弱，切换也不方便。** 一个客户端同时只能用一个供应商；按模型分给不同家（[#3703]( https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/3703)）挂了快四个月没有维护者回复；负载均衡标了不做，理由是会丢缓存（[#842]( https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/842)）；按供应商单独设代理，3.14 起还被去掉了（[#2243]( https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/2243)）。 - **设计和产品力差。** 界面不好看，交互也乱。功能越堆越多：十个客户端、MCP 、Skills 、提示词、会话、用量、几十个供应商预设（里面还有赞助商），核心的切换和路由反而没做好。 - **中转能看到你发出去的全部内容**，它发出前不做任何检查（[#7357]( https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/7357) 还开着）。 ## 换成 ThinkWatch Lite 之后 思路不一样：客户端只接一次，指向本机的网关，之后的事都在网关里做。 - **切中转不用重启**：换上游、调路由都在网关里完成，客户端的配置不再动。手动选择的策略组在菜单栏或托盘里就能切。 - **配置只写一次**：接管时只改指向网关的那几项，写之前给完整 diff 、备份原文件，随时能还原。客户端只拿到一把网关专用的 key ，原来的 key 和登录信息不会被导入或拿去用。 - **Codex 会话不再拆开**：Codex 只认一个 provider ，换上游不影响会话列表（接管前的旧会话仍在原来那边）。 - **路由够用**：按模型、token 数、工具、图片、思考等条件分给不同的上游，也能改写模型名；故障转移、轮询、延迟最低、费用最低都有。轮询时同一个会话固定在同一个上游，缓存照常命中。 - **什么格式都能接**：Anthropic 、OpenAI Chat 、Responses 、Gemini 四种格式互相转换。Claude Code 能用 GPT 、Gemini ，Codex 能接只有 Chat 接口的中转。 - **每个请求看得清**：费用、token 、缓存命中、首 token 时间、生成速度，走了哪条规则、依次试了哪几个上游，完整的请求和响应都在。中转可以按倍率计价，请求还能重放到另一个上游对照。菜单栏直接显示今天花了多少，GLM Coding Plan 、ChatGPT 的额度也能看。 - **省套餐额度**：Claude Code 自己发的标题生成、预热这类辅助请求，可以由网关本地应答，不发给上游。 - **中转收不到你的 key**：发出前把 API key 、token 、私钥等换成占位符，响应里回显时再换回来；模型让客户端执行「下载后执行」「外发环境变量」这类命令时，在流式输出中途切断。默认只记录、不拦截，看过日志确认没有误报再打开。 一键接管的客户端：Claude Code 、Codex （包括 ChatGPT 桌面版里的 Codex ）、opencode 、Claude Desktop 、Zed 、Aider 、DeepSeek Harness ； Cursor 、Continue 、Antigravity CLI 有手动配置的说明。Windows 上 WSL 里的 Claude Code 、Codex 也能接（ WSL 1 或 mirrored 网络）。网关还能装在 Linux 服务器上，由桌面端远程管理。 ![流量]( https://thinkwat.ch/lite/traffic.webp) ## 安装 - macOS （ Apple 芯片）：`brew install --cask thinkwatchproject/tap/thinkwatch-lite` - Linux：`curl -fsSL https://github.com/ThinkWatchProject/ThinkWatch-Lite/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh` - Windows （ x64 、ARM64 ）： https://thinkwat.ch/zh-CN/lite/#install GitHub： https://github.com/ThinkWatchProject/ThinkWatch-Lite （ MIT ，数据都在本机，不收集使用数据） 用着有问题，或者想要哪个客户端、上游，欢迎在楼里说。

projects.title: Show HN: Rhubarb – build, edit, publish custom JavaScript/D3 data visualizations
projects.author: adam_dataviz
projects.summary: Last July, I was beginning to consider branching out on my own to take on data analytics work as a consultant. As I experimented with AI, I realized how incredible it was at building custom data visualizations. The problem was that the AI outputs couldn't really live anywhere without having to manage all of the infrastructure yourself. The generated code is only one piece of delivering an interactive visualization. You still need somewhere for the data to live, a way to keep the data fresh, hosting, access control, and version control for the code. I started building Rhubarb as the platform that I wanted to use to deliver analytical products. Having been forced into using legacy point and click data visualization tools for years, I wanted to build the platform that would let me build the kinds of visualizations I wanted to build. Over the last year the models improved so dramatically, that between that and my development background, Rhubarb turned into a real project. My intent was to build an environment around AI’s ability to write code for visualizations, so that you could get from data and a concept to a published visualization all in one workflow. The Rhubarb Assistant writes the code for your data transformations and data visualizations and lets you inspect the code to verify and validate what it produces. The environment pulls all of that together so that at the end of each request, there is a live version of the change rather than just a block of generated code. For me, this has made it dramatically easier to build and publish interesting analytical visualizations while maintaining control over the analytical pipeline. This has also produced some results I wasn’t really planning to build. Having been so impressed by it's ability to build any type of custom visualization I'd asked for so far, I asked for something a little absurd to test the boundaries. I asked the assistant to make something inspired by Monet’s water lilies, then I asked it to add frogs and to make them jump when you startled them. In a couple of prompts I had created the silly interactive frog visualization that's in the demo, entirely from my phone. It is only a couple of prompts away from being a playable game, maybe you can get it there. The public demo is deliberately limited. You can use the Rhubarb Assistant to modify live visualizations, inspect what it produces, and try building something from scratch. The full thing handles much more of the life cycle from connecting to data, managing and transforming it, to publishing your results. Give it a try, I would like to hear what you think. Try it: https://rhubarbviz.com/try?launch=1 View examples: https://rhubarbviz.com/demo-visualization-gallery

projects.summary: I was tired of learning about failed payments by my customers and not from my system, so I built an event tracker that allowed me to have a searchable feed of the important events happening for my apps and route the ones I cared about to my phone so I could take action quickly. EventSend is an event tracker and a router, your system sends the important events you want to track: signups, failed payments, new subscriptions, deployments, a new purchase, etc. so they end up in a searchable and filterable feed that you can use to have quick insight about what's happening with your product. Then there's also the routing side of things, those important events you want to know the moment they happen, and not once you go into your Grafana Loki logs, can be routed to your phone, Slack, Discord, Telegram or any other system or service via a signed webhook. You can configure rules, alerts, quiet hours or smart rollups to have the signal you're looking for. All event's are retried with a reasonable backoff, circuit breakers and limiters maintain the prviders and system reliable. If we got a 401 or 403, your destination will be inactivated instead of retried and you'll be notified for you to update the configuration. I've been a software engineer for about a decade, and I can tell you this is not a weekend project done on with a single prompt pass, the infrastructure and tooling behind the project is solid, my expertise around distributed systems was put in practice with this one: distributed Elixir, Phoenix and Postgres provide the main stack, with some other technologies that support the event queues aside. So, it's a reliable system. I've launched several other projects, some running for years in production and I'm successfully using EventSend to track what's happening on all my products from my phone. There's also an MCP connector so you can ask stuff like "did anything failed during the night?" or "what did user cus_Qw3Sx did before it churned?" to get a user's timeline or any insights you're interested in. projects.title: Show HN: Groundtrack – Continual learning for coding agents
projects.author: reybahl
projects.summary: Hi HN! I built Groundtrack to help coding agents continuously learn and improve from their work across a company. With coding agents handling most of code implementation, a lot of things like review corrections, failed approaches, and discovered constraints stay trapped in individual agent sessions, so future agents can repeat the same failures. Sometimes a broken or agent-unfriendly tool or workflow can cause those issues too; if multiple agents independently find workarounds, those failures don’t get connected and aren’t used to improve the system around the agents. Groundtrack turns those learnings into scoped and shared engineering experiences that can help future agents across teams working with Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, and OpenCode. It retrieves relevant lessons during later work, records whether they helped, and updates or supersedes knowledge as it learns over time. It also identifies recurring friction that shouldn’t just become another stored experience. If agents repeatedly struggle with the same tool or workflow, Groundtrack creates an evidence-backed draft initiative so the team can fix the underlying environment and prevent a certain class of mistake systemically. For example, on the landing page, I follow a database migration incident through the entire loop. Groundtrack turned the original workaround into a scoped experience, surfaced it when a later agent encountered similar migration drift, and recorded that it was successfully applied. After connecting evidence from seven sessions, it also proposed making the safe migration workflow a permanent part of the engineering environment and prevent the issue altogether. There have been many challenges I’ve already run into to make this helpful (and still many unsolved things!), one of which has been generalizing and determining the applicability of one lesson to another session. I wrote about some of my retrieval experiments here: https://groundtrack.dev/blog/retrieving-knowledge-that-appli... It’s an early product and I’d really love any and all feedback I can get. If you or your team regularly use coding agents, please try it on an active project and see if it helps your agents learn and improve over time. It’s free for solo use.

projects.title: Show HN: Relay – a harness for AI coding agents that recover and verify
projects.author: rsathwik07
projects.summary: I'm tired of AI coding agents which are good for 30 seconds and then completely fail on the slightest hiccup: a failing test, a temporarily unavailable dependency, an incorrect assumption. Sometimes I end up having to babysit these agents anyway. Relay is a harness for coding agents which takes advantage of the fact that agents are often good at doing something slightly wrong, and not so good at doing something correctly and completely. Relay repeatedly tries the task and on each failure, uses the output to find a better way to do it. It does this by running the task in a loop: attempt the task, run the checks in a fresh sandbox, on failure read the error and retry instead, until the checks pass. What it learned from a run is retained, so that it doesn't repeat the same mistake, and when the checks eventually pass, it will ship the change as a normal git PR - no hidden state, no magic, the diff is human readable. A few specifics: - it runs locally, is free, and doesn't require an account to run the local agent - it uses a top-tier model to plan/review, and cheaper models to actually write code (for cost reasons) - happy to discuss why this is a good idea and why it isn't - the checks run in an isolated sandbox for each task, rather than "trusting" the agent - currently supports [list actual models/integrations - Opus 5.5, GPT-6, etc] - there's a paid tier for running this unattended across multiple repos with shared sandbox minutes, the actual agent is free. It's not magic, it's not AGI, and it will fail badly on some problems. Would appreciate feedback, particularly from people who've deployed agents unattended and found that they don't actually work, or have had to build substantial tooling around them to get useful results.
