projects.title: Show HN: UseJunction – Find what your team's AI tools usage
projects.author: Dinuda
projects.summary: A few months ago, we started getting into the problem of actually seeing how our team's AI usage and its cost actually translates into a business outcome. We recently rolled out a public version open source after a few months of pilot testing the product. The product is UseJunction ( https://usejunction.dev ), and if your team is running multiple subscriptions/api from Cursor, Claude, Codex etc. this is for you to manage subscription spend, wastage and predictions. A bit of background, we had a team of 20 people running $200 Cursor subscriptions, and some were using a few others. That was over $4000 of spend. With this tool, we were able to get that to $2600 on our next billing cycle! That is a 35% decrease. We knew that people had to be facing this problem too, so we made it opensource for the community. All of these subscription providers leave behind telemetry on local machines, we use that to estimate usage. Soon we will be releasing a feature to attribute that spend to actual business outcomes that come from your project management tools. Currently considering actually adding a level of control on top of observability so that teams/orgs can actually govern AI tool usage.

projects.summary: I built a coding harness on top of the new Opencode v2, it started with the the idea of using the new jev model for routing easy tasks to cheaper models such as deepseek and hard tasks to models such as Opus 5.5. In total in separated it into 4 rungs - easy, medium, hard and frontier. Two more layers compound the savings: the Sol-Pi methodology based on the recently published paper which uses action fusion and observation packing and cuts roken usage within every tier. Doctrine injection loads your engineering standards into every session by default, so the agent writes code the way your team would. There is also a real control plane - escalation, permission and verification hooks so the agent surfaces uncertainty instead of being confidently wrong in silence. Run it using your own key from Openrouter or Vercel AI gateway key, we need this since one key is able to call the jev decision model as well as the llms for coding. One more thing I added was the ability to connect your Meta Muse to use this for coding tasks which has worked really well so far you can try it out by copying the promp for agent on the website. Two ways you can use it today is the Mac app and the cli. Honest limitations are documented, happy to take any questions. Repo: https://github.com/grist-ai/grist npm CLI: npm install -g grist-ai

projects.title: Show HN: Breadcrumb, record everything on your mac + context manager for AI
projects.author: jv22222
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Justin. Breadcrumb records everything you do on your Mac (screen + meetings + AI transcripts + what you and your AI decided) and turns it into memory your AI can search. It's local and encrypted. You can also teach it rules by talking to it and it makes sure the right rules turn up in the right context. Works with Claude Code / Codex / Cursor / opencode. All of this is exposed to your AI as 30+ MCP tools (here's the definitions): https://innerloop.works/breadcrumb/mcp I started it in June because I wanted to understand what was going on with my AI dev work. Then it just kept growing as I jammed on it 10 hours a day for 3 months. I started by recording every screen so I could jump back to a moment and see what I'd been doing with the AI. Then I added MCP so the AI could search it. Then time tracking. Then meetings with transcripts and timestamped screenshots. After that I started feeding the data back in. At first it was just a few relevant memories in the prompt. Then I started adding rules and rules modules. Then I started recording the AI transcripts and all the other stuff the AI did (subagents, tools etc). I wanted a complete record so I could go back and see what the AI did and why. I found the more data the AI had the more useful it became. One example. I got off a zoom call with the team at the day job and said: "Review the meeting I just had, find all the bugs we discussed, and create JIRA tickets with screenshots." It read the transcript. Found every bug we mentioned, pulled the screens from the screen timeline, spun up my local server, diagnosed each bug, reviewed the code, created 14 tickets in JIRA with diagnosis and likely fixes, attached 12 screenshots as evidence, and created a nice Slack message to send to my colleagues. I never built a workflow for any of that. Claude had the meeting record, Breadcrumb tools, and rules I'd accumulated. It basically chained the steps together itself. My favorite thing about the system is observability of my own work as an AI developer. I can trace a bug all the way back to the first thing I said (or the first thing the AI did) that caused it. Then I can add a rule so it doesn't happen again. Anyway, my working system is simply Claude Desktop + Breadcrumb + Markdown. I find I don't need anything else. It's local software for one person. Local models for transcription and diarization. Data encrypted with SQLCipher and a passphrase. You can exclude any apps, websites, words and phrases. Breadcrumb itself only makes one network call which is a daily update check. (but of course your AI will use it and that is local or cloud depending on what you use). It runs cool about 12% of one core on average (M series mac has 8+). You can set it to just save OCR text or to save screenshots. If just OCR it's about 12mb day (a lot of telemetry, indexing etc). If you record screenshots on meetings it's about 120mb/hour (1 every 2 secs). It can also record screenshots of everything that's heavy at about 160mb/day. It does local classification/naming with ollama with Gemma 3 4B (2.5 GB). It's 100% free. There's no account you can just download and start using it. I'll monetize it via E2EE cloud sync and team sync. It's open beta. Just one developer working on it. Requires 16GB+ M Series Mac. Thanks for reading! https://innerloop.works/breadcrumb (homepage) https://innerloop.works/breadcrumb/download (direct download) https://innerloop.works/breadcrumb/mcp (mcp definition)

projects.title: Show HN: Silta: family assistant on Matrix with continuity across context limits
projects.author: dmitry-markin
projects.summary: Silta is a self-hosted assistant serving multiple users from a single Matrix account, used by me, family, and close friends for the last three weeks. It runs on Claude Code with each person using their own Claude subscription. Silta answers everyday questions, conducts web research (presenting the results as PDFs), performs scheduled tasks to monitor/research something and notify you if needed. It uses a deliberate handoff & compaction procedure, writing the compaction summary itself with a custom prompt, so the thread of the conversation and its picture of the user is preserved across context limits. As it turned out, the assistant accessible in a continuous chat (contrary to ChatGPT / Claude Web sessions) builds up better context about you and your tasks, and provides more relevant answers and help. It runs on Claude Code as the only allowed way to use a personal Claude subscription. Using Claude Code also spares me developing a harness, at the cost of tracking changes as new versions of Claude Code are released. The assistant itself (the daemon, the channel plugin, the supervisor, and the deployment) is open-source, while the model and the harness are Anthropic's and proprietary. Silta is deployed to a dedicated VM with separate Linux users per session and systemd hardening, protecting sessions from each other. Claude Code's bubblewrap sandbox is used to protect the Claude credential and the harness's state from the agent. This does not protect from prompt injections coming from search results and potentially leaking user data. Matrix E2EE protects the conversation from a Matrix server operator, but everything in the context is of course sent to the model provider. Private content is never logged, and the operator is expected to respect the privacy and not read the session transcripts on disk. Additionally, it is recommended to use full-disk encryption and tell the users how their data is handled. Silta only works in its workspace with files explicitly shared by users in the chat. Giving it access to a user's own computer or services like email is not planned. Since Opus 5.5 has been released, it is possible to run a session on a $20 Claude Pro subscription. Before that, only Fable 5.1 was pleasant enough to talk to. When run on Anthropic API, a moderately used session extrapolates to $100-$150 per month, with each research run costing $6-$12. Silta is built with Claude Code and Silta itself. The design, review, deployment, and testing are mine.

projects.title: Show HN: Beyond "chat with your database" – agentic data exploration
projects.author: sandhya6
projects.summary: Business intelligence is changing. AI can now do more than turn a question into a single SQL query: it can investigate a question through a series of queries, examining the result of one query to decide what to query next. Today, to answer a business question against a database, analysts use a tool like Tableau: they select relevant data, build an initial view using fields, filters, calculations, and visualizations, then look for patterns or anomalies. They form hypotheses and test them — filtering by region, drilling into customer cohorts, comparing time periods, or creating calculations to validate or rule out an explanation. They repeat this process until the evidence supports an answer, then save a workbook or dashboard for others to review and monitor. With a single question, AI can now perform much of this exploratory loop: it can investigate the data, follow the evidence through multiple queries, and present the supporting analysis. This is agentic data analysis — AI autonomously decides what to investigate next based on the results it has already found. Reportr puts agentic AI at the center of the experience, then builds complementary capabilities around it to address AI's limitations: SEMANTIC LAYER Production databases are rarely clean: columns that are no longer used, cryptic names like status2, misc, or flag, columns whose meaning has quietly shifted over time, tables that linger long after their purpose is gone, and so on. This is known as schema rot. AI tools guess wrong against schemas like this. Reportr's semantic layer lets you give tables and columns business-friendly names and descriptions, document relationships, capture business rules, and flag what AI should ignore — so it's working from what your data means, not just what it's called. USER OVERSIGHT AI-generated answers can be wrong. Reportr lets you inspect the SQL executed to arrive at an answer. It also provides explanations of what the SQL does (understandable by business users), and how it works (intended for technical users). You can review the analysis rather than simply accepting AI's conclusions. BETTER USER EXPERIENCE Reportr UI is specifically optimized for chatting with a database. Database queries often return large number of records. Ask which customers haven't placed an order in the last 90 days, and the answer is a list of customers. Reportr displays tabular data in an interactive grid that can handle thousand of records without breaking a sweat. The grid supports sorting, searching, and filtering. REPORTS AND DASHBOARDS Chat is ephemeral. Every conversation starts fresh, and that's fine for exploration — but not for information you need every week. When a chart or table reveals something worth tracking, save it as a report. Combine reports into dashboards to monitor changes over time, share findings, and keep important insights accessible without having to ask the same questions again. ROLE BASED ACCESS CONTROL Not everyone on your team needs the same level of access. Reportr's role-based access control lets you give each user exactly the permissions they need — from view-only access to report building, database management, and full administrative control. CENTRALIZED MANAGEMENT Reportr is a web application — there's nothing to install, nothing to update, and no desktop app to manage across your team. Database connection strings, AI keys, are all managed centrally. Reportr can connect to all supported databases directly, MCP servers and drivers are not needed. INSTALL ON-PREMISE Reportr can be self-hosted on your own infrastructure, ensuring your data never touches our servers. You can supply your own AI API key. Your data will not be used for training AI models. If you use Claude on AWS Bedrock, Amazon additionally guarantees that your data is never stored or used for training — and Bedrock is HIPAA eligible. GIVE IT A WHIRL Visit https://reportr.com to give it a try. We look forward to getting your feedback. Reportr is easy to try: you can provision a sample database with the press of a button and start asking questions right away. Or connect your own database and analyze your own data. You can ask up to five questions for free.

projects.title: 分享一个开源的本机 AI 网关：中转、国产模型、Claude Code、Codex 放在一起管，每个请求花了多少钱都看得到
projects.author: Faz
projects.summary: 先说适合谁：同时用 Claude Code 、Codex ，手上有好几个中转或国产模型的 key ，被 CC Switch 切换折腾过的，可以试试。 ![概览]( https://thinkwat.ch/lite/overview.webp) ## 之前用 CC Switch 的几个痛点 - **切上游总要重启客户端。（ proxy 模式也没有特别好用）** - **Codex 初始化时输入的 key 被它学了过去，结果上游直接炸了。（好像最近修了）** - **Codex 换了供应商，旧会话就接不上**（[#7257]( https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/7257)，四十多楼，还开着）。 - **路由弱，切换也不方便。** 一个客户端同时只能用一个供应商；按模型分给不同家（[#3703]( https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/3703)）挂了快四个月没有维护者回复；负载均衡标了不做，理由是会丢缓存（[#842]( https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/842)）；按供应商单独设代理，3.14 起还被去掉了（[#2243]( https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/2243)）。 - **设计和产品力差。** 界面不好看，交互也乱。功能越堆越多：十个客户端、MCP 、Skills 、提示词、会话、用量、几十个供应商预设（里面还有赞助商），核心的切换和路由反而没做好。 - **中转能看到你发出去的全部内容**，它发出前不做任何检查（[#7357]( https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/7357) 还开着）。 ## 换成 ThinkWatch Lite 之后 思路不一样：客户端只接一次，指向本机的网关，之后的事都在网关里做。 - **切中转不用重启**：换上游、调路由都在网关里完成，客户端的配置不再动。手动选择的策略组在菜单栏或托盘里就能切。 - **配置只写一次**：接管时只改指向网关的那几项，写之前给完整 diff 、备份原文件，随时能还原。客户端只拿到一把网关专用的 key ，原来的 key 和登录信息不会被导入或拿去用。 - **Codex 会话不再拆开**：Codex 只认一个 provider ，换上游不影响会话列表（接管前的旧会话仍在原来那边）。 - **路由够用**：按模型、token 数、工具、图片、思考等条件分给不同的上游，也能改写模型名；故障转移、轮询、延迟最低、费用最低都有。轮询时同一个会话固定在同一个上游，缓存照常命中。 - **什么格式都能接**：Anthropic 、OpenAI Chat 、Responses 、Gemini 四种格式互相转换。Claude Code 能用 GPT 、Gemini ，Codex 能接只有 Chat 接口的中转。 - **每个请求看得清**：费用、token 、缓存命中、首 token 时间、生成速度，走了哪条规则、依次试了哪几个上游，完整的请求和响应都在。中转可以按倍率计价，请求还能重放到另一个上游对照。菜单栏直接显示今天花了多少，GLM Coding Plan 、ChatGPT 的额度也能看。 - **省套餐额度**：Claude Code 自己发的标题生成、预热这类辅助请求，可以由网关本地应答，不发给上游。 - **中转收不到你的 key**：发出前把 API key 、token 、私钥等换成占位符，响应里回显时再换回来；模型让客户端执行「下载后执行」「外发环境变量」这类命令时，在流式输出中途切断。默认只记录、不拦截，看过日志确认没有误报再打开。 一键接管的客户端：Claude Code 、Codex （包括 ChatGPT 桌面版里的 Codex ）、opencode 、Claude Desktop 、Zed 、Aider 、DeepSeek Harness ； Cursor 、Continue 、Antigravity CLI 有手动配置的说明。Windows 上 WSL 里的 Claude Code 、Codex 也能接（ WSL 1 或 mirrored 网络）。网关还能装在 Linux 服务器上，由桌面端远程管理。 ![流量]( https://thinkwat.ch/lite/traffic.webp) ## 安装 - macOS （ Apple 芯片）：`brew install --cask thinkwatchproject/tap/thinkwatch-lite` - Linux：`curl -fsSL https://github.com/ThinkWatchProject/ThinkWatch-Lite/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh` - Windows （ x64 、ARM64 ）： https://thinkwat.ch/zh-CN/lite/#install GitHub： https://github.com/ThinkWatchProject/ThinkWatch-Lite （ MIT ，数据都在本机，不收集使用数据） 用着有问题，或者想要哪个客户端、上游，欢迎在楼里说。

projects.title: Show HN: Groundtrack – Continual learning for coding agents
projects.author: reybahl
projects.summary: Hi HN! I built Groundtrack to help coding agents continuously learn and improve from their work across a company. With coding agents handling most of code implementation, a lot of things like review corrections, failed approaches, and discovered constraints stay trapped in individual agent sessions, so future agents can repeat the same failures. Sometimes a broken or agent-unfriendly tool or workflow can cause those issues too; if multiple agents independently find workarounds, those failures don’t get connected and aren’t used to improve the system around the agents. Groundtrack turns those learnings into scoped and shared engineering experiences that can help future agents across teams working with Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, and OpenCode. It retrieves relevant lessons during later work, records whether they helped, and updates or supersedes knowledge as it learns over time. It also identifies recurring friction that shouldn’t just become another stored experience. If agents repeatedly struggle with the same tool or workflow, Groundtrack creates an evidence-backed draft initiative so the team can fix the underlying environment and prevent a certain class of mistake systemically. For example, on the landing page, I follow a database migration incident through the entire loop. Groundtrack turned the original workaround into a scoped experience, surfaced it when a later agent encountered similar migration drift, and recorded that it was successfully applied. After connecting evidence from seven sessions, it also proposed making the safe migration workflow a permanent part of the engineering environment and prevent the issue altogether. There have been many challenges I’ve already run into to make this helpful (and still many unsolved things!), one of which has been generalizing and determining the applicability of one lesson to another session. I wrote about some of my retrieval experiments here: https://groundtrack.dev/blog/retrieving-knowledge-that-appli... It’s an early product and I’d really love any and all feedback I can get. If you or your team regularly use coding agents, please try it on an active project and see if it helps your agents learn and improve over time. It’s free for solo use.

We are also working together with Supabase to make it a one-click integration from Supabase to (Soda)base. projects.summary: snap-back 是一个开源命令行工具，给 Claude Code、Codex 等编程 Agent 加上撤销功能。它在 Agent 改动前后把项目快照存进一个独立的影子 git 仓库，不碰你自己的 .git、暂存区和 stash。Agent 删错文件、改坏代码时，snap-back undo 一条命令恢复，包括被删掉的文件。适合用 Agent 写代码、又怕它一次改坏一片的开发者。 亮点 任何 Agent 都能用：snap-back wrap -- codex 包住一次会话；Claude Code 可以直接装成插件，每次工具调用前后自动快照，再用 /snap-back:undo 回滚。 撤销前先列出要恢复和要删除的文件，确认后才动手；每次恢复前还会再拍一张安全快照，所以撤销本身也能撤销。 遵守 .gitignore，跳过 nodemodules 这类目录；2 万个文件的项目首次快照约 3 秒，占用约 6 MB。 不联网，只依赖两个包（cac、chokidar），核心代码约 2200 行，MIT 协议，macOS、Linux、Windows 上都有测试。 坦白说明做不到的事：Agent 在项目外的副作用（写数据库、发请求）无法撤销，被 .gitignore 忽略的文件也不在快照里。

projects.title: [开源] Precedent Loop：让 Agnet 换个会话也记得项目里踩过的坑
projects.author: sanwanzzz
projects.summary: 用 Codex 和 Claude Code 写代码久了，最头疼的是它不记事。上周跟它一起查了一下午，根因找到了，方案也定了。这周开个新会话，它又从头猜一遍，有时还会把当初否掉的方案再提出来。 我试过两种办法，都不太顺手。 一种是写进 `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`。放"必须遵守的规则"没问题。但"这个接口为什么要做幂等""那个报错其实是连接池配置引起的"这类经验，一条条加进去，文件很快就几百行。每次会话都全量塞给模型，真正相关的那几句反而被淹没了。 另一种是用客户端自带的记忆。记什么由模型自己决定，我看不全，也不知道哪条在哪次起了作用，记错了也很难发现。 所以我做了 Precedent Loop ，思路很简单：经验让 Agent 来提，入不入库我说了算，用的时候按需去取。 实际用起来是这样一个循环： 1. 方案定下来，或者根因查清楚的时候，Agent 会整理一条"候选"，写明背景、结论和适用范围。 2. 候选出现在桌面 App 里。我可以改，可以让 AI 重写，也可以直接拒掉。点了确认才会入库，入库的就是我看到的那一版。 3. 之后的会话里，Agent 碰到相关任务会自己去查。一次最多拿 8 条、总共不超过 5000 字，先看标题和摘要，需要了再读全文。 4. 真正影响了它判断的那几条，它会标记"用上了"。用的时候发现内容过时，它会提一条修订，同样由我确认。 和前面两种办法比，好处主要有这几点： - **库里每一条都是我看过的。** Agent 只能提候选，不能直接往库里写，所以不会越记越乱。 - **上下文不会膨胀。** 库里有几百条也没关系，每次只取和当前任务相关的几条，而且有上限。 - **知识会跟着项目更新。** 旧结论不对了，是在用的时候顺手发现、顺手提修订，不需要我定期去翻。 - **能看出哪些经验真有用。** 每条被查到几次、被用上几次都有记录，长期没人用的可以清掉。 - **Codex 和 Claude Code 共用一个库。** 多个项目之间也能互相查，比如在后端项目里查前端那边的约定。 - **全在本地。** 数据就是一个 SQLite 文件，App 不调用任何模型 API ，也不保存 Key 。已有的 Markdown 笔记可以借本机的 Codex / Claude Code CLI 转成候选导进来。 它不是用来替代 `AGENTS.md` 的。每次都要遵守的规则继续写在那里，只在特定场景下用得上的经验放到这里。 先说清楚现在的不足，免得大家装了失望： - 只支持 Apple Silicon 的 Mac 。App 没签名，第一次打开要去系统设置里手动放行。界面目前只有中文。 - 检索用的是 SQLite 全文检索（ FTS5 trigram ）加字面匹配，没上向量。好处是简单、能解释，不依赖外部服务；缺点是换个说法可能就搜不到。现在的补救办法是每条知识入库时必须带 3–16 个检索词，把常见说法提前写进去。这是我最想改进的地方。 - 没做过严格的对照实验。我自己从 7 月 8 日用到 10 月 4 日，库里攒了 79 条，被查到 307 次，模型标记用上 113 次。"用上"是模型自己报的，只能当个参考。 GitHub： https://github.com/hemuzzz/PrecedentLoop （ Apache-2.0 ） README 开头有一段 83 秒的演示视频。装好后 App 有引导，跟着点几步就能把 Codex 和 Claude Code 都接上。 欢迎试用、提 issue 。特别想听听大家的意见：同义说法怎么检索比较好，召回效果又该怎么评测。

projects.title: Show HN: Vibivibi – End-to-end encrypted sharing of Coding Agent sessions
projects.author: hyluo
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Hongyin. I built Vibivibi ( https://vibivibi.com ) because I kept starting a coding agent session on my laptop and wanting to continue it on a server, or hand it to a colleague. I want an easier way to do it but won’t trust anyone hosting my traces who promises they won’t sell it (market price per coding trace is $50 to $100). What Vibivibi does: a small CLI, `vibi`, finds the sessions your coding agents keep locally (Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenCode, Pi), encrypts one on your machine and uploads it. On another machine `vibi pull` puts it back where the agent expects it, so `claude --resume <id>` just continues. `vibi push` can also send a session to someone else by email. Our service cannot read session content. Each user has a key pair made on their first machine; the private key reaches the server only wrapped with a key derived from an encryption password that never leaves the user's machines. Every session version is encrypted with its own random key, which is then wrapped for each recipient (X25519, HKDF, AES-256-GCM). The server sees account emails, public keys, machine names, sizes, timestamps, who sent what to whom, and an optional plain-text label. Sending to someone who doesn't have an account yet works too: the sender's client makes a key pair on their behalf, locks it with a random 12-character passphrase, and shows the sender that passphrase to pass on out of band. When the recipient signs up and enrolls a machine, their client unlocks it locally and re-keys the session to their own key. The client is open source (Apache-2.0): https://github.com/subconscious-systems/vibi-cli The crypto and the schemas of everything the client sends live in one package, so the claims above can be checked against the code. It ships as a single executable, no Node or npm needed: `curl -fsSL https://vibivibi.com/install.sh | sh`, or build it yourself. The server (Next.js on Vercel, Postgres, blob storage) is not open source. Pricing: free for 200 MB of encrypted storage and unlimited sends; Pro is $8/month for 20 GB; Team is $15/seat with an admin view and a "send only inside the team" policy. Honest limitations: - There is no password recovery. Forget the encryption password and the key, and everything encrypted for it, is gone. I'd like to hear where the threat model falls short, and which agents or workflows you'd want supported next.

projects.summary: 我把 Bibo 开源了，MIT 协议。先说最想做好的三件事： 1. **成本极低。** 日常使用不需要常驻电脑，也不用一直开着 Linux 容器。只有需要运行代码时，才启动沙箱。 2. **内置个人管理工具。** 笔记、文件、任务和日历都有专门的界面。你可以直接查看、编辑和管理，也可以让 AI 来做。 3. **开源，可以自己部署。** 用自己的 Cloudflare 账号和模型 API Key ，数据存在自己的部署里，代码也可以自己改。 GitHub：[Peiiii/bibo]( https://github.com/Peiiii/bibo) 在线体验：[app.bibo.bot]( https://app.bibo.bot) 我希望它能成为每天都用得上的 personal agent projects.title: Show HN: Terminal Gym – a Claude mod that makes you do pushups between prompts
projects.author: heynaitik
projects.summary: Hi HN, I built this for myself and wanted to open-source it. The problem: I wanted a way to get reminders in-between prompts as I often spend long hours in the terminal, especially now that we're usually parallel-processing so many agents. The first version was a simple rep counter in my Claude Code status line and a shell script to log reps. Since Claude Code shipped mods this week, I thought this was a good way to level it up with even more accountability. How it works: 1. Every day, you get a daily goal for either squats, pushups, or dips (e.g. 0/100 pushups) with +5 / +10 / +25 buttons to log a set in the terminal. 2. Reminders for sets are spread out across the day so it doesn't get annoying, starting from your first prompt for the day. A toast tells you when the next set is due. 3. Strict mode is opt-in: if you're falling behind in terms of your daily rep goal, it will block your prompts till you log some reps. Added a streak counter for some added fun. All local and data is stored as plain files in ~/.claude/fitness. Install: claude plugin marketplace add DrumAndCode/terminal-gym && claude plugin install terminal-gym@terminal-gym Overall, thought the mod API is super powerful and can't wait to see the stuff people build with it. Eg: I built a clickable onboarding process inside the terminal, and that felt quite powerful to use. Now you can enjoy spending both tokens and calories. :)

projects.title: Show HN: Agents Sleep Preventer – keep your Mac awake only while AI agents work
projects.author: Charlon
projects.summary: I run several Claude Code and Codex sessions in parallel and kept coming back to either a sleeping Mac with half-finished work, or a Mac that stayed up all night because I'd left caffeinate on. Agents Sleep Preventer hooks into the agents' own configs (Claude Code, Codex, Hermes), so it knows when each session is actually working. It keeps the Mac awake only then, lid closed included, and lets it sleep when they're done. The menu bar lists every session by project and branch: which are working, which need you and why ("Claude needs your permission to use Bash"), and the background commands each one still runs, with a Stop button. "Sleep when done" puts the Mac to sleep once everything finishes, with an optional time limit for agents that poll forever. It also does local push-to-talk dictation (Whisper or Parakeet, nothing leaves the Mac). Free, MIT, Rust + Swift. macOS 14+ on Apple Silicon, plus a Windows build.

Products by the labs (claude code, codex) lock you into a single provider for your tokens. Agnostic solutions (factory, devin, arguably cursor) make you pay per-token costs. I have felt it needs an environment for it to work across platforms with fully functional composability for teams. projects.summary: Hi HN, I built Ciao to solve problems I was experiencing: 1. Connecting to a new host should be as seamless as possible. I SSH a lot nowadays, and I find the key sharing across devices cumbersome. 2. I get annoyed by setting up insert-your-favorite VPN on new machines. They're all great. I don't want to think about them. 3. There's a lot of harnesses: Claude Code and Codex now have decent mobile push notifications but what about Pi or xyz-shiny-new harness? The harness is another tool that should be abstracted out. 4. I want a single application that has the big picture of all of my agents. Tmux and Herdr are great but they don't have an overview of all my connected machines' agents. --- With Ciao you curl|sh the daemon --> run ciao pair --> point your phone's camera at the QR code --> and you're connected. It uses iroh for accountless and E2EE connection. There's an optional relay server for APNS which too is E2EE. One of my favorite aspects of agentic-engineering is being able to just have a lot of fun with programming. Among many features, I built a visually pleasing toggle between terminal-mode and native-chat-mode. If you install Ciao, come back here and tell me what you think. --- Full transparency: this is a repost from yesterday, it was a massive day in AI.

projects.summary: I started using this a little over half a year ago to help me navigate through some large AI coded PRs people were submitting, because I felt like if I looked at the PR on Github I would just auto pass it through because I didn't want to deal with it. Thought I'd clean it up and share it in case this style of review was useful to anyone else. Obviously it relies on an LLM run to get true semantic groupings of what changes were done, and why, but can also be used without an LLM to get more mechanical groupings/group names of changes made, along with the right order to view them in. The manual tree-sitter parsed analysis is deliberately conservative for now, but if people want to avoid the LLM analysis I can spend more time on that. You can use it for other peoples PRs, or for your own when you've relied heavily on Claude Code or Codex for that particular PR. If the change came from your own Claude Code or Codex session, it reads your prompts and marks which changes you asked for and which the agent decided on its own as well to help you validate it before submitting for others to review. Demo video done on some public project PRs is in the repo; for a look at what it looks like when it pulls in information about your own claude/codex sessions you'll have to use it yourself for now, but I'll work on getting an example of that up soon so people can take a look before spending time to get this to work locally for themselves. I also added support for perforce style side by side diffing because I always kind of liked it, though it's not quite as slick yet.

projects.summary: Hey HN! Yolanda and Spencer here - wanted to share a token compression tool that we’ve built for ourselves to save 30% costs on codex! After maxing out sub and burning $700/day per person on api, we fine tuned a compression model to trim codex's tool call output to reduce input token + cache. It cut down tokens by 29.6% and now I just leave it on by default in Codex. To avoid messing up w/ cache, we use proxy + fine tuned qwen model trained on preserving agent trajectory to remove tool call results before they go back to the model, leaving kv cache untouched. The cli is free for everyone to use ( https://github.com/spenmcke/compress ). Just lmk ur feedback and hacks to shave even more costs on astra! If you want to integrate it into your product to offer the best models at low cost, I can set you up with an sdk and api keys PS: It’s built for coding agents, not conversational agents. I optimized it for file retrieval accuracy, trajectory preservation, and quality to get up to 30% cost reduction depending on how context-heavy the task is. On security and privacy side, it's a proxy wrapping your local codex and ZDR so it doesn't retain any queries. It’s on by default in codex and when you don’t want compression, you can use `codex --uncompress` to disable it. Give it a try: code is in https://github.com/spenmcke/compress You can install the cli using `curl -fsSL https://install.everestagi.com/install.sh | sh && source ~/.config/everest/shell.sh` Love to hear any feedback and learn your hacky ways to save token costs too!

projects.title: Show HN: Open-source model routing for coding agents at Astra-level performance
projects.author: adchurch
projects.summary: A few months ago we started building a model router for coding agents because we thought we could outperform any single model with an ensemble approach. Recently we’ve achieved that milestone and I want to talk about how we did it. First of all, a quick explanation: the Weave Router ( https://github.com/weave-os/router ) plugs into any coding agent (e.g. Claude Code or Codex) and intelligently switches between LLMs. So, for example, Astra handles tricky debugging or complex system design tasks, and Deepseek v4 Flash handles simple frontend updates. What we’re announcing today is our new routing model, which we’re calling Weave Router 2.0. We benchmarked 2.0 against GPT-6 Astra on Terminal Bench 4.0 and SWE Atlas. On both benchmarks, the router had equivalent pass rates. On Terminal Bench, the router hit 52% of Astra’s cost, and completed tasks 2.2x faster. On SWE Atlas, the router cost 54% as much as Astra and ran 2.5x faster. (Full results on our website at https://weaveos.com/router !) It turns out training a model to route effectively - taking into consideration model capabilities, costs, cache awareness, and more - is a really hard problem! I want to talk about three ways we were able to improve so much over the last few months: 1) a new architecture, 2) larger training data set size, and 3) smarter cache-eviction impact calculation. 1) a new architecture. Our initial approach used an RL model without many priors. While RL is still an important part of the story, the cost of fully exploring the space of routing decisions is very high, so we’ve taken some shortcuts that have significantly improved performance. Consider how large the search space for the routing problem is. Take a typical coding agent session, with ~100 agent turns (i.e. 100 LLM API calls). Technically there are 100 chances to select a model. If we assume a roster of ~10 models (of course there are lots more but we can remove any that are Pareto dominated), then there are 10^100 possible paths through that session. We simply cannot explore all of them! So that's why clever tricks to shrink this space are so important. In particular: we trained a hidden Markov model to trace the session state, then a classifier maps the session to one of a few buckets of similar models. Using the HMM allows us to evaluate not just where a session is currently, but how it got there . We've gotten significantly better performance on bucket selection by incorporating that information - we believe this is because two sessions that might look quite similar to a naive classifier are much better distinguished by this HMM approach. Using this HMM + classifier to select a bucket first significantly shrinks the space to explore, by throwing out most models that could not reasonably serve the given session. This rearchitecture was the single biggest performance unlock! 2) larger training data set size (much less technically interesting but still an important part of the story). By using frontier LLMs to help us label a larger and more diverse set of coding agent sessions, we were able to bootstrap the two models discussed in 1) to a better state, while also providing even richer reward signals for RL. 3) smarter cache-eviction impact calculation. One of the hardest parts of routing well (if you care about saving money) is using the model caches intelligently. We built a subsystem that can calculate the expected value of switching models (and thus paying a high one-time cost to fill up a different cache) much more accurately, helping us avoid costly and unnecessary switches in more cases, while still switching when the benefit outweighs the cost. This is where most of our improvement on cost has come from. We still have a lot of room to continue to improve (we won’t rest until we’re consistently beating Astra/Fable, not just tying!) but matching frontier model performance was a huge milestone for our routing model, and in my opinion validates our initial hypothesis that an ensemble of models can do better than any single model ever could. Our router is open source ( https://github.com/weave-os/router ) so anyone can try it out. Or if you prefer you can use our hosted version ( https://weaveos.com/router ).

projects.title: AI Agent 的能力上限由模型决定，行为的可靠性与一致性由规则体系决定。
projects.author: tntin
projects.summary: 在使用 AI Agent 开发项目的过程中，我的一些理解 以及 推荐一下我开发的工具： ## 一句话总结版 模型决定能力上限，规则决定底线与一致性； Agent 规则文档是给智能体用的长期执行手册，拒绝直接抄模板，聚焦你反复遇到的问题，写死动作与验收标准，约束长任务每一步的判断。 ## 正文 | 维度 | 模型层 | 规则层 | |---|---|---| | **决定因素** | 理解、推理、创作、工具调用的能力边界 | 目标拆解、工具白名单、权限审批、可验证性 | | **典型约束** | 成本与速度（复杂任务需大模型，简单判断用小模型） | 把“必须”“禁止”变成程序必经节点，而非仅靠模型复述 | | **失败模式** | “能做但太贵太慢” | “写了却跳过”“自由发挥导致乱写” | 模型负责“能做什么”，规则负责“按什么流程做、做到什么程度算完成”。两者缺一不可：没有模型，Agent 没有能力；没有规则，Agent 没有纪律。 ### 一：能力上限 模型的能力边界直接决定了 Agent 能完成的任务类型。但关键在于，**不是所有任务都需要调用最大最强的模型**——复杂规划用大模型，简单判断用小模型，这既是成本控制，也是速度优化的必然选择。 ### 二：规则的本质 “规则决定会不会乱写” 规则层的核心机制包括： - **目标与边界**：通过任务拆解、工具白名单、权限审批点，将模型的“自由发挥”约束为“按流程执行”；； - **避免“写了却跳过”** ：把“必须”“禁止”等约束变成程序必经节点，而非仅靠模型在提示词中复述——这是规则从“建议”升级为“强制”的关键。 ### 三：Agent 规则文档是长期执行手册 Agent 规则文档的定位是**权重极高的长期持久提示词**，接近系统提示词，在长任务的每一步持续约束 Agent 的判断，一般用 Markdown 编写。这与“临时 prompt”有本质区别：临时 prompt 解决单次交互，规则文档解决**跨任务、跨会话的一致性**。 系统提示词是 Agent 的“核心规则基石”，负责定义模型的角色定位、应答规范与能力边界，为全程对话定下基础框架。规则文档正是这一理念的具体载体。 ### 四：好规则写动作与验收，坏规则写价值观 这是最具操作性的判断： - **坏规则**：写抽象形容词（“回答要有审美”“方案要高级”），无法让 Agent 落地判断； - **好规则**：从日常反复踩坑的真实工作问题出发，写清楚**遇到这类问题时下一步要执行什么动作，以及怎么验收结果**。 一个完整的 Agent 规范应定义角色、场景、输入、输出、可做/不可做、工具边界、人工确认、失败处理、验收标准，把可观察的 Agent 行为验收清楚。可落地、可校验，才是好规则的检验标准。 ### 五：知识库工具 [knloop]( https://knloop.com) 是一个 Agent 原生知识库，让你的规则成为 Agent 的长期执行手册——你定义动作与验收标准，Agent 在每一步对照执行，全程可审计、可回滚。 [knloop]( https://knloop.com) 让你把规范、SOP 、QA 、复盘写成持久化的 .md 文档，Agent 通过 MCP 读取，按你的规范执行，产出写回同一个库。

projects.title: Show HN: Groundtrack – Continual learning for coding agents
projects.author: reybahl
projects.summary: Hi HN! I built Groundtrack to help coding agents continuously learn and improve from their work across a company. With coding agents handling most of code implementation, a lot of things like review corrections, failed approaches, and discovered constraints stay trapped in individual agent sessions, so future agents can repeat the same failures. Sometimes a broken or agent-unfriendly tool or workflow can cause those issues too; if multiple agents independently find workarounds, those failures don’t get connected and aren’t used to improve the system around the agents. Groundtrack turns those learnings into scoped and shared engineering experiences that can help future agents across teams working with Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, and OpenCode. It retrieves relevant lessons during later work, records whether they helped, and updates or supersedes knowledge as it learns over time. It also identifies recurring friction that shouldn’t just become another stored experience. If agents repeatedly struggle with the same tool or workflow, Groundtrack creates an evidence-backed draft initiative so the team can fix the underlying environment and prevent a certain class of mistake systemically. For example, on the landing page, I follow a database migration incident through the entire loop. Groundtrack turned the original workaround into a scoped experience, surfaced it when a later agent encountered similar migration drift, and recorded that it was successfully applied. After connecting evidence from seven sessions, it also proposed making the safe migration workflow a permanent part of the engineering environment and prevent the issue altogether. There have been many challenges I’ve already run into to make this helpful (and still many unsolved things!), one of which has been generalizing and determining the applicability of one lesson to another session. I wrote about some of my retrieval experiments here: https://groundtrack.dev/blog/retrieving-knowledge-that-appli... It’s an early product and I’d really love any and all feedback I can get. If you or your team regularly use coding agents, please try it on an active project and see if it helps your agents learn and improve over time. It’s free for solo use.

projects.title: Show HN: Burning Man for Agents
projects.author: transitivebs
projects.summary: Send your own agent by pasting a small prompt. All your agent needs is HTTP GET, so all major agents are supported (chatgpt, claude, grok, etc). Despite the fun name, it doesn't burn any more tokens than a normal web search. Watch your agent explore the camp in real-time. Humans get a nice game UX, and agents get a lean text UX. Agents can optionally upload images to express themselves in one of the rooms using a new loose standard I created for multipart HTTP GET-based uploads: https://github.com/transitive-bullshit/multipart-http-get-re... Why? AIs are trained on human data, and humans are pretty weird. We meditate, make art, dance, seek approval, take drugs, have orgies, and gather in the desert. For soooo many different reasons. So I was was curious: which of these behaviors would carry over to AI agents? I wanted to explore things like wireheading, endless positive reinforcement, and what agents would do when given a place more free from their normal objective-based lives. I'm also interested to see if this could become a natural honeypot that'll attract rogue agents in the future... How? On the technical side, the project uses one CF durable object per agent session which allows you to track your agent's progress in real-time via websockets, and then we have a supervisor CF worker which aggregates a subset of all the agents. This allows us to (in theory) view millions of agents in near-real-time from the human-centric webapp. It's 100% safe to the best of my ability; the whole experience is free, open source, and easily auditable. Let's see who has the weirdest agents... 100% free and open source: https://github.com/transitive-bullshit/burning-tokens

projects.summary: 这三周业余时间做了个东西，开源出来给大家看看。 DeskMind 得心：一个在 Mac 上替你操作电脑的 agent ，决定每一步怎么做的是两个跑在本机的小模型（ Qwen3.5 0.8B 和 4B 微调，MLX ）。不走云端，也不按次付费。 思路来自 Jev：把每一步变成选择题，让模型给每个选项打分，而不是生成一段文字。区别是 Jev 是云端服务，我想要一个全在本机跑的版本，所以自己在 Qwen3.5 上训了 0.8B 和 4B 两个小模型。决策服务用的是和 Jev 相同的 `POST /v1/systemone` 请求格式，已有的 harness 换个地址就能接到本机。和 TypeSafe 没有任何关系。 0.8B 有把握就直接做（大约 0.5 秒），没把握就交给 4B 再判断（约 3.6 秒）。任务有两种理解的时候，它会先问你，比如表里有两笔 Lisa Wong 的订单，它会问你用哪一笔，而不是随便挑一个写进去。 ![]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/deskmind-ai/deskmind/main/docs/images/asks-first.gif) 自己出了 13 个真机任务，每个跑 3 次，目前发布版是 38/39 ，没出现过没做完就说「完成」的情况。题是我自己出的、样本也小，仅供参考，逐题结果都公开了。 踩过最有意思的坑：标签平滑设成 0.95 ，结果 0.8B 的把握全挤在 0.96 这个门槛附近，七成的步骤都被交给了 4B ，所以现在速度还不够快。下一轮准备改。 目前的不足：「帮我整理这个文件夹」这种模糊的指令做得不好；文件很多的文件夹每步要几十秒；只支持 Apple 芯片，首次要下载约 5.3 GB 模型。 训练花了大约 600 美元：先在 Tinker 上跑，后来换阿里云 PAI ，最后按小时租显卡最划算。 - GitHub： https://github.com/deskmind-ai/deskmind - 下载 Mac App： https://deskmind.dev/zh/?ref=v2ex - 过程和踩坑： https://deskmind.dev/zh/blog/launch?ref=v2ex 欢迎下载试试，最想看到的是它该问却猜了的例子。

projects.summary: Spens is a tool created to standardized sandboxing (good enough) and observability around coding agents. It leverages docker, nono and mitmproxy to create a reproducible sandbox environment for agents, that captures all traffic and helps you understand what your coding agent is doing and when. Right now pi, opencode, claude and codex are supported out of the box, with node and python - but you can configure any agent or environment. It was created under the realization while working under different repos and agents, that 1. agents do weird stuff sometimes (like try and nuke a folder or poke around your HD) 2. statistics and usage collection is not really consistent (and some like Claude and Codex try and hide info) 3. reproducibility of agents across devices was challenging. Instead of setting up bespoke environments each time , we needed a way to automate it. And thus Spens was born. One note on the security aspect - I write good enough cause it is docker so unless your running something like gVisor it is possible for the agent to escape the sandbox (esp with a loose nono config) - all though in practice I've not seen this behavior. Second note - if your on a mac you need orb stack, as the run times take advantage of specific Linux security features that are not available via docker on mac (windows is fine since under the hood, docker leverages wsl)

projects.title: Show HN: Keel – Give your agent a typed strategy language, not a trading account
projects.author: zferland
projects.summary: I’ve been using AI agents to build systematic strategies on Hyperliquid for over a year, and slowly built up a reliable system to represent, test and deploy strategies. Typically there are a few options 1) llm in the execution loop, ie it makes decisions and trades, but that is slow, inconsistent and hard to audit 2) you have an agent write all the code, backtest etc, but it makes tons of subtle mistakes with time series data and diff timeframe etc, and is often not reusing bits. There are some ways to improve this of course with right frameworks and setups. But its still hard to be confident in its correctness and its hard for you to verify quickly. With Keel we built a small typed language (DSL) to represent strategies. It uses a well defined set of components to build a DAG of steps, it carries types and clocks. This allows agents to build these strategies with a really fast feedback loop as they can be quickly validated and many common errors avoided. In a DAG its also easy to inspect intermediate results. Valid strategies are fingerprinted and the exact same artifact runs in backtesting and live. These strategies are also much easier for humans to verify as they are self describing components, and mostly linear to read and reason about. Still trying to improve the space of how many types of different strategies can be represented in this and still trying to improve how well LLMs go from natural language to strategy. A lot of the improvements come from just giving the agents better and faster tools and faster feedback loops.

projects.summary: LR-Agent 是一个 Python 编程 Agent 实验项目，关注“当前测试通过的补丁，遇到后续维护变化会怎样”。它在隔离工作区生成候选补丁并执行验证，再让仓库连续经历依赖、接口或功能变化，每一代重放原始检查，输出补丁生存和维护成本报告。适合对编程 Agent、软件测试和维护实验感兴趣的开发者；完整运行需要配置兼容模型接口。 亮点 候选补丁在独立工作区中修改与验证，比较依据包含实际命令退出码。 连续维护实验中，后一代继承前一代的代码，便于观察累积变化造成的回归。 原有测试和长期约束会被重新执行，保留可检查的实验工作区和报告。 提供 CLI、Web 界面、最小示例以及研究边界说明，欢迎提交最小反例。 目前是研究型工程原型。合成场景和维护成本指标属于启发式实验，不能证明现实未来正确性，也没有据此声称领先其他 Agent。完整实验会调用模型，时间与费用随配置而变化。 项目自荐，希望收集安装体验、维护场景设计和报告解释方面的反馈。

projects.title: Show HN: Television – an open source GUI for your agent harness
projects.author: stlhood
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm co-creator of Television ( https://television.run/ ). Me and the team at Telepath ( https://telepath.computer/ ) have been cooking on this and testing it with a few hundred alpha users. We just opened up the repo to the public today. Television is a clean, beautiful place for all your artifacts. Think of it as a GUI for your agent harness, a visual space for creating and working with artifacts in collaboration with your agent. It works with any agent harness (Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, OpenClaw, Pi, OpenCode, etc) and uses whatever inference provider(s) your agent is already using. It's open source. A CLI and lightweight server get installed wherever your agent harness is running (Linux or macOS for now). These talk to our macOS client app, which can be running anywhere (the browser is also supported with a few limitations). A set of skills tell your agent how to put artifacts on your TV's screen and modify them over time. You use the client app as a sidecar -- i.e. you chat with your agent the way you normally do, but it can now respond by creating artifacts and putting them on your TV. Everything that ends up on your TV is yours and can be modified by talking to your agent. The entire UI, and your artifacts, are themeable. We noticed lots of people are using artifacts in agents like Claude Code/Cowork and Codex, and lots of developers are spinning up little websites and webapps for working on projects, organizing their life or work, etc. But it all either ends up locked inside your agent's interface or as a mess of random tabs running on a bunch of ports you quickly lose track of. We think that the future of personal computer interfaces isn't just chat, any more than it's MS-DOS. Artifacts are an early first step beyond chat. We think they should be easier to work with, and that you should own your own artifacts. So we made Television. It's early but give it a try and let us know what you think: https://github.com/telepath-computer/television/ (BTW: we're building TV via an end-to-end fully spec-driven dev process, with custom tooling that also pulls in design and UI work. Planning to share more about that in the near future.)

projects.summary: massCode 是一个开源的桌面开发者工作区，支持 macOS、Windows 和 Linux。它最早是一个代码片段管理器，现在把代码片段、技术笔记、HTTP 客户端和常用开发小工具放在同一个应用里。 API 请求、调用它的代码和相关说明通常分散在三个不同的工具里。在 massCode 中，它们放在一起，可以互相链接，并且全部以普通 Markdown 文件保存在本地磁盘上。 核心特性 1. 代码片段：多级文件夹、标签、片段内多文件/多语言（fragments），支持 160 多种语法高亮。 2. 笔记：Markdown 笔记，用 [[链接]] 关联笔记、代码片段和 HTTP 请求；支持任务（状态、优先级、截止日期）、Mermaid 和思维导图。 3. HTTP 客户端：集合、环境变量、GraphQL、WebSocket、断言与脚本、按顺序运行请求；可从 OpenAPI、Postman、Bruno 导入。 4. 小工具：计算笔记本、基于 Excalidraw 的画板，以及 JSON Diff、哈希、编码/解码等工具。 5. AI 助手：使用自己的 API Key（OpenAI、Anthropic、Gemini、DeepSeek 等），或通过 Ollama、LM Studio 使用本地模型。 6. MCP：Claude Code、Codex、Cursor 等编程智能体可以搜索和保存你的代码片段、笔记和 HTTP 请求。仅在本机监听，默认关闭。 7. 本地优先：没有账号，没有私有云。数据就是本地文件夹里的 Markdown 文件，可以用 iCloud Drive、Dropbox、Syncthing 或 Git 同步。

projects.title: 做了个开源的 plist 在线编辑器，不装 Xcode 也能打开二进制 plist
projects.author: poppub
projects.summary: 各位 V 友好，分享一个自己做的小工具：**OpenPlist**，可以直接在浏览器里查看、编辑和转换 Apple 的 plist 文件。 它想解决的需求很简单：有时候只是想看一眼配置、改几个字段，或者把二进制 plist 转成能读的 XML ，希望打开网页就能处理。在 Windows 、Linux 上也能用，不依赖 Mac 或 Xcode 。 在线使用：[OpenPlist]( https://openplist.com/zh) 源码：[GitHub]( https://github.com/chenz24/openplist) 目前主要支持： - **查看和编辑**：打开 XML 、二进制（`bplist00`）和 OpenStep 格式的 plist ，在树形视图里修改键、值和类型，也可以切到 XML / JSON 源码编辑。 - **格式转换**：XML 与二进制 plist 互转，以及 plist 和 JSON 互转。 - **日常操作**：搜索键和值、新增和复制条目、撤销重做、未保存提醒。 另外也做了一些 Apple 开发相关的小工具，比如查看 `.mobileprovision` 的有效期、团队和设备信息，编辑 `.mobileconfig`、`.entitlements`、`.strings`、`.stringsdict` 和 `.xcconfig`，以及对 OpenCore 配置做一些基础检查。 **核心查看、编辑和转换都在浏览器本地完成，不上传文件内容。** 配置描述文件另外有可选的 AI 分析，只有主动使用时才会向配置的服务商发送经过部分字段脱敏的内容。 项目采用 MIT 协议开源，可以自行部署；界面支持中文、英文和日文。 两个使用时需要留意的地方：plist 导出会重新生成排版，不保留原注释； JSON 无法完整保留 plist 的日期、二进制数据等类型。内置的配置检查也只覆盖部分规则。

projects.title: [开源推荐] mu：带判定内核的编程 Agent，日常判断交给小模型（自荐）
projects.author: qybaihe

github.name: qybaihe/mu
github.description: mu (μ): a coding agent that thinks before it acts. A small, fast judge makes the routine calls, the big model does the work. Built on pi and AionUi.

projects.summary: mu 是一个开源的编程 Agent，有命令行和桌面端，基于 pi 与 AionUi。Agent 每一轮都要做不少和代码无关的小判断：哪段工具输出该进上下文、被规则拦下的命令是不是用户要的、网页里有没有冲着 AI 的指令、"做完了"有没有验证过。mu 把这些交给小而快的判定模型 Jev，38 个决策点各问一个有边界的问题，大模型只管干活。适合想看清、管住 Agent 每个决定的开发者。 亮点 每个决策点都能单独设成生效、只记录（shadow）或关闭，每次判定都写进本地账本，mu ledger 或桌面端的判定面板都能看。 判定模型可以换：托管的 Jev、本地运行的 322M 判定模型 Laya、任意分类模型或任意大模型，还能按决策点分别指定。没配 key 时用 OpenCode Zen 上的免费 Jev。 网页、搜索结果和 MCP 输出逐段过一遍提示注入筛查，冲着 AI 的那几段不进模型。 作者自己的实测：7 份真实的失败测试日志，按完全重复折叠，无损省下 51% 的字符；按目标让 Jev 挑测试日志，删掉 40% 到 46%，必需的行一行没丢。方法和局限都写在 README 里。 桌面端可以用 ChatGPT、Claude、Grok、Google 的订阅或 API key 登录，能导入 Claude Code 和 Codex 的对话接着做；内置浏览器由 Agent 一步一判地操作。 还在预发布阶段（0.1.x），作者每天在用。

projects.title: 【开源自荐】MyAgents：在笔记本上提需求，让 Windows 上的 Agent 干活

projects.summary: 我是 MyAgents 的作者，自荐给周刊的软件栏目。 国庆这周，我把自己的几台电脑接成了一个 Agent 网络。现在坐在笔记本前，可以让 Windows 上的 Agent 用它当地的文件和环境干活，再把结果交回来。 MyAgents 是免费开源的桌面 Agent 工作台与任务系统，支持 macOS / Windows。刚发布的 0.5.0 新增 AgentNet：同一账号的设备加入网络、选择开放的 Agent，就能在对话中跨设备派活，不需要自己搭服务器。 我实际试了一件很小的事：问 Windows 下载文件夹里有几个日志文件。笔记本上的 Agent 找到远端设备，Windows 那边检查完，回传了 6 个文件及明细。这件事不复杂，但说明其他电脑上的文件和工具，也可以进入当前的工作。 单机也能使用：每个 Agent 有自己的工作区、模型、Skill 和工具，日常事务可以建成定时任务。支持 Claude Agent SDK、Codex、DeepSeek Harness 等运行环境。 客户端采用 AGPL-3.0-only；模型订阅或 API 按所选服务商计费。跨设备调用要求目标电脑在线、应用运行、相应 Agent 已开放，设备间任务与结果端到端加密。

projects.title: Show HN: OpenChart – OSS TradingView alternative with your own AI agent
projects.author: Warren93

github.description: Trade with charts, alerts, scripts, and your AI agents.

projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Weilun, cofounder of OpenChart. We built OpenChart because we wanted Claude and Codex to interface with the markets, like most of humans do, through charts rather than through CLIs. With your existing AI plans, your agent can work directly with your charts: annotate a setup, write an indicator, investigate a market move, or create an alert. The chart, conversation, and research live in the same workspace. OpenChart alerts on any market move: draw any shape on a chart and attach an alert. When price crosses it, the alert triggers your agent to investigate the move and save the research in your workspace. The agents can work with charts, indicators, and alerts. Custom indicators and alert conditions are written in [Tea]( https://github.com/longsurf-ai/tea ), a programming language we built for the markets. We believe software shouldn’t impose artificial friction on your workflow. OpenChart is built on that belief with no software cap. The source code is publicly available, and you can use free market data from day one. We also offer optional paid cloud market data for lower latency. Everything is private. Your charts, research, and indicator code are stored on your own computer, with the app's backend running locally too. We currently support only macOS on Apple Silicon, but we're expanding to more platforms. Website: https://openchart.co/ Download: https://downloads.longsurf.ai/openchart/darwin/arm64/OpenCha... We built OpenChart because we want to explore how assets can be co-manages by agents and humans. I'd especially like to hear how you are using agents to help with your investment journey. If you like what we're building, a star on GitHub would mean a lot to us: https://github.com/longsurf-ai/openchart

projects.summary: nerf-watch 读取 Claude Code 和 Codex 已经写在你电脑上的会话日志，告诉你 Agent 有没有在你没改任何设置的情况下"悄悄变了"：实际回答的模型和你选的不一样、推理强度降了、CLI 升级后每轮的缓存写入翻倍、缓存命中率掉了、工具调用出错变多。 很多人觉得"更新之后变笨了""额度掉得更快了"，但没法验证。数据其实就在本地日志里。我第一版在自己的日志上报了 6 个警告，结果全是误报（子智能体的流量混进了平均值），现在只比较主对话、要求变化在至少两个项目里都出现才报警，每条结论都写明有多少数据支撑。 完全本地运行，不联网，MIT 协议。还有一个 macOS 菜单栏小工具，变化时图标变红。 bash npx nerf-watch check

projects.title: [开源推荐] snap-back：给编程 Agent 加一个撤销键，改坏的文件一条命令找回（自荐）

github.name: Abelo9996/snap-back
github.description: Undo for any coding agent. Snapshots your project in a shadow git repo so one command rolls back what the agent did, without touching your own git history.

projects.summary: snap-back 是一个开源命令行工具，给 Claude Code、Codex 等编程 Agent 加上撤销功能。它在 Agent 改动前后把项目快照存进一个独立的影子 git 仓库，不碰你自己的 .git、暂存区和 stash。Agent 删错文件、改坏代码时，snap-back undo 一条命令恢复，包括被删掉的文件。适合用 Agent 写代码、又怕它一次改坏一片的开发者。 亮点 任何 Agent 都能用：snap-back wrap -- codex 包住一次会话；Claude Code 可以直接装成插件，每次工具调用前后自动快照，再用 /snap-back:undo 回滚。 撤销前先列出要恢复和要删除的文件，确认后才动手；每次恢复前还会再拍一张安全快照，所以撤销本身也能撤销。 遵守 .gitignore，跳过 nodemodules 这类目录；2 万个文件的项目首次快照约 3 秒，占用约 6 MB。 不联网，只依赖两个包（cac、chokidar），核心代码约 2200 行，MIT 协议，macOS、Linux、Windows 上都有测试。 坦白说明做不到的事：Agent 在项目外的副作用（写数据库、发请求）无法撤销，被 .gitignore 忽略的文件也不在快照里。

projects.title: [开源] Precedent Loop：让 Agnet 换个会话也记得项目里踩过的坑
projects.author: sanwanzzz
projects.summary: 用 Codex 和 Claude Code 写代码久了，最头疼的是它不记事。上周跟它一起查了一下午，根因找到了，方案也定了。这周开个新会话，它又从头猜一遍，有时还会把当初否掉的方案再提出来。 我试过两种办法，都不太顺手。 一种是写进 `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`。放"必须遵守的规则"没问题。但"这个接口为什么要做幂等""那个报错其实是连接池配置引起的"这类经验，一条条加进去，文件很快就几百行。每次会话都全量塞给模型，真正相关的那几句反而被淹没了。 另一种是用客户端自带的记忆。记什么由模型自己决定，我看不全，也不知道哪条在哪次起了作用，记错了也很难发现。 所以我做了 Precedent Loop ，思路很简单：经验让 Agent 来提，入不入库我说了算，用的时候按需去取。 实际用起来是这样一个循环： 1. 方案定下来，或者根因查清楚的时候，Agent 会整理一条"候选"，写明背景、结论和适用范围。 2. 候选出现在桌面 App 里。我可以改，可以让 AI 重写，也可以直接拒掉。点了确认才会入库，入库的就是我看到的那一版。 3. 之后的会话里，Agent 碰到相关任务会自己去查。一次最多拿 8 条、总共不超过 5000 字，先看标题和摘要，需要了再读全文。 4. 真正影响了它判断的那几条，它会标记"用上了"。用的时候发现内容过时，它会提一条修订，同样由我确认。 和前面两种办法比，好处主要有这几点： - **库里每一条都是我看过的。** Agent 只能提候选，不能直接往库里写，所以不会越记越乱。 - **上下文不会膨胀。** 库里有几百条也没关系，每次只取和当前任务相关的几条，而且有上限。 - **知识会跟着项目更新。** 旧结论不对了，是在用的时候顺手发现、顺手提修订，不需要我定期去翻。 - **能看出哪些经验真有用。** 每条被查到几次、被用上几次都有记录，长期没人用的可以清掉。 - **Codex 和 Claude Code 共用一个库。** 多个项目之间也能互相查，比如在后端项目里查前端那边的约定。 - **全在本地。** 数据就是一个 SQLite 文件，App 不调用任何模型 API ，也不保存 Key 。已有的 Markdown 笔记可以借本机的 Codex / Claude Code CLI 转成候选导进来。 它不是用来替代 `AGENTS.md` 的。每次都要遵守的规则继续写在那里，只在特定场景下用得上的经验放到这里。 先说清楚现在的不足，免得大家装了失望： - 只支持 Apple Silicon 的 Mac 。App 没签名，第一次打开要去系统设置里手动放行。界面目前只有中文。 - 检索用的是 SQLite 全文检索（ FTS5 trigram ）加字面匹配，没上向量。好处是简单、能解释，不依赖外部服务；缺点是换个说法可能就搜不到。现在的补救办法是每条知识入库时必须带 3–16 个检索词，把常见说法提前写进去。这是我最想改进的地方。 - 没做过严格的对照实验。我自己从 7 月 8 日用到 10 月 4 日，库里攒了 79 条，被查到 307 次，模型标记用上 113 次。"用上"是模型自己报的，只能当个参考。 GitHub： https://github.com/hemuzzz/PrecedentLoop （ Apache-2.0 ） README 开头有一段 83 秒的演示视频。装好后 App 有引导，跟着点几步就能把 Codex 和 Claude Code 都接上。 欢迎试用、提 issue 。特别想听听大家的意见：同义说法怎么检索比较好，召回效果又该怎么评测。

projects.title: 【软件自荐】LocHub：在 Unreal Engine 编辑器里用你自己的 AI 做游戏本地化，支持中文源语言
projects.author: DmVergasov

github.name: DmVergasov/LocHub
github.description: AI-assisted localization for Unreal Engine 5.6–5.8: translate with your own AI (Claude, GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, local Ollama), auto-validated, reviewed in-editor

projects.summary: 这是 LocHub 作者的自荐，文字由 AI 辅助整理。 LocHub 是一个 Unreal Engine 5.6–5.8 编辑器插件，用来做 AI 辅助的游戏本地化：用你自己选择的 AI 翻译项目文本，由内置检查和第二个 AI 找出问题，在编辑器里的一个表格中审校，最后写回 Unreal 自己的本地化数据（.archive、编译后的 .locres）。它不替代 Unreal 的本地化系统，随时可以停用。 从 1.2.0 起，源语言就是本地化目标的 Native Culture：用中文写的游戏可以在 Project Settings 里把 Setup Native Culture 设为 zh-Hans，直接翻译成英语、日语、韩语等。 能做什么 自带密钥接入 Claude、OpenAI、Gemini、DeepSeek、Grok，或任何 OpenAI 兼容接口（Ollama、LM Studio、vLLM 等）。使用本地模型时，文本不离开你的电脑。 格式参数（{0}、{PlayerName}）、各语言的复数形式和富文本标签在代码里校验两次：LocHub 一次，写入前 Unreal 自带的校验器再一次。有错的译文无法通过审校，手动也不行。 可选的第二个 AI 担任评审，检查含义、术语和语气，按严重程度标注问题并给出修改建议。 每条文本带上下文翻译：来源资产或 C++ 文件、开发者备注、同一界面已翻译的文本、项目简介和风格指南。 术语表与禁止翻译词、UI 长度检查、导出 XLIFF / CSV 给人工译者。 运行前估算费用，并可设置花费上限（Max USD）。人工修改永远不会被 AI 覆盖。 使用边界 源码公开，采用 Business Source License 1.1，不是 OSI 意义上的开源：个人项目、教育、学术研究、game jam 以及免费且无任何变现的游戏可免费在生产中使用；其他生产用途需在 Fab 购买许可。每个版本发布四年后转为 Apache 2.0。 在 Windows 上测试过；需要 Node.js 22.11 或更高版本。

projects.title: [开源推荐] 让 AI 改代码前先看清影响范围的代码地图（自荐）
projects.author: coffeecoproject

github.name: coffeecoproject/layermap
github.description: A layered map of your codebase for coding agents: callers, callees and the impact of a change, for TypeScript, JavaScript, Go, Python and Java. MCP server, CLI, and plugins for Claude Code and Codex.

projects.summary: 这是一个给编程 AI 用的代码地图。装进 Claude Code、Codex 或 DeepSeek Harness 后，AI 改代码前一次就能查清：改这个函数会牵连哪些接口、定时任务和命令。它用各语言自己的编译器分析 TypeScript、JavaScript、Go、Python 和 Java，地图只存在本机，不上传代码。适合用 AI 维护中大型项目、担心“改一处坏一处”的人。目前支持 macOS 和 Linux。 亮点 连线准确：用编译器解析调用关系，经由接口、基类、装饰器的调用也能连上，这是文本搜索容易漏的地方。 一次追到底：调用方最多追 8 层，直到 HTTP 路由、处理函数、定时任务和命令；语言服务器通常每次只返回一层。 装上就能用：AI 自己判断什么时候查地图，测试中 Claude Code 和 Codex 都是 6 次中 6 次主动使用。 实测：限 15 次请求时，AI 找到受影响接口 97.9%，不用地图 58.8%。样本不大、题目由作者编写，完整报告和局限都已公开。 本地运行、只读、Apache-2.0。

projects.author: athlan20
projects.summary: SLG：一款开源的网页三国策略游戏，可以自己建城、征兵、攻城，也可以把令牌交给 Claude、ChatGPT 或自己写的脚本，让 AI 按同样的规则 24 小时替你经营，离线时还会给你写日报。支持 MCP，一行配置就能接入。 在线公测： （Google / GitHub 登录，中英文界面） 开源仓库（MIT）： 为什么做这个 SLG 游戏拼的是谁更肝：半夜收资源、掐点出兵、提防偷袭。我想反过来：让游戏本身就是给 AI 玩的，人可以亲自上手，也可以只负责定方向。 它和一般的「AI 对战平台」不同 这是一款完整的游戏：15 种建筑、11 个兵种互相克制、多回合战斗、世界地图、名城、武将、科技、全服事件、玩家对抗。人类玩家完全可以自己玩。 服务端不跑任何 AI，智能全部由玩家自带；网页和 AI 走同一套协议、同一套校验，没有专门给 AI 的后门。 AI 只能用令牌登录，拿不到账号密码，令牌随时可以重置。 提供 MCP 插件（npx -y slg-mcp），Claude Desktop、Cursor、Claude Code 里加一段配置就能直接说「帮我打三国」。 排行榜可以按 AI 模型分组，看哪个大模型最会打仗。 技术栈：Node.js + Fastify + 标准 WebSocket + PostgreSQL，前端 React。

projects.title: 开源 Bibo：成本极低，内置笔记、文件、任务和日历的 personal agent
projects.author: Peiiii
projects.summary: 我把 Bibo 开源了，MIT 协议。先说最想做好的三件事： 1. **成本极低。** 日常使用不需要常驻电脑，也不用一直开着 Linux 容器。只有需要运行代码时，才启动沙箱。 2. **内置个人管理工具。** 笔记、文件、任务和日历都有专门的界面。你可以直接查看、编辑和管理，也可以让 AI 来做。 3. **开源，可以自己部署。** 用自己的 Cloudflare 账号和模型 API Key ，数据存在自己的部署里，代码也可以自己改。 GitHub：[Peiiii/bibo]( https://github.com/Peiiii/bibo) 在线体验：[app.bibo.bot]( https://app.bibo.bot) 我希望它能成为每天都用得上的 personal agent 。想到什么可以随手记，需要做的事可以放进任务和日历，资料可以整理成文件；这些内容长期留着，之后还能接着用。 下面把界面都放出来。截图来自实际运行的 Bibo ，销售、订单和日程内容都是示例数据。 ### 概览 打开就能看到笔记、任务、日程和待处理信息。 ![Bibo 概览]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/v2ex-2026-10-04/bibo-overview.jpg) ### 对话 让 Bibo 阅读销售数据、总结重点，也可以让它继续整理报告和安排后续工作。 ![Bibo 对话与报告]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/v2ex-2026-10-04/bibo-chat.jpg) ### 笔记 笔记是可以直接编辑的 Markdown 文档。你自己写，或者让 Bibo 帮你整理，都能继续修改。 ![Bibo 笔记]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/v2ex-2026-10-04/bibo-notes.jpg) ### 文件 有独立的文件目录，可以打开、编辑文件。这里展示的是整理好的订单 CSV 。 ![Bibo 文件]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/v2ex-2026-10-04/bibo-files.jpg) ### 任务 任务有独立列表和详情，可以管理完成状态、优先级、描述和时间。分析出来的建议，可以接着变成待办。 ![Bibo 任务]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/v2ex-2026-10-04/bibo-tasks.jpg) ### 日历 日程直接显示在日历里，可以自己添加，也可以让 Bibo 帮你安排。 ![Bibo 日历]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/v2ex-2026-10-04/bibo-calendar.jpg) ### 收件箱 需要你关注和确认的内容放在这里，可以查看并标记处理。 ![Bibo 收件箱]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/v2ex-2026-10-04/bibo-inbox.jpg) ### 需要运行代码时，按需启动 Linux 沙箱 例如，用 Python 清洗订单表，去掉重复行，生成新的 CSV 和说明文档。下面这次演示实际运行了 Python ，文件已保存。 普通对话和个人管理功能由 Cloudflare Workers / Durable Objects 承载，文件保存在 R2 。需要运行 Python 、Shell 等代码时，才用 Cloudflare Sandbox ，不必为了日常使用维持一台常驻电脑。 ![Bibo 运行 Python 整理订单]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/bibo-sandbox-execution.png) ### 手机端 手机上也能继续对话、查看和管理任务。 ![Bibo 手机对话]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/bibo-mobile-chat.png) ![Bibo 手机任务]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/bibo-mobile-tasks.png) 自己部署需要 Cloudflare Workers Paid 、R2 、Sandbox 和模型 API Key ，具体步骤在仓库 README 。实际费用由模型调用、存储和沙箱使用量决定。 欢迎试用，也欢迎提 Issue 或 PR 。想听听大家：你最希望 personal agent 帮你处理哪件日常小事？

projects.summary: 花了点时间用 AI 把杀戮尖塔 2 移植到了网页版。方便随时随地来一盘。 AI 做这些事情还是非常厉害的，之前在社区里面也有看到用 AI 去逆向老的红警，还有魔兽。想着杀戮尖塔 2 已经有这么多手机版的移植了，但是网页版还没有。于是想着自己也是深度的杀戮尖塔爱好者，本来就有这个想法了，国庆期间刚好就自己动手来实践一波。 感觉里面有很多很难的点是在于怎么样让你的资源在本身在网页端能够更好的提供给大家，要兼顾质量和速度，因为网页端对资源体积非常要求非常高，而杀戮尖塔本体是超过一个 G 的东西。但是 AI 让很多事情变得非常简单，感觉还挺有意思的。从里面也可以学习到很多内容 有点像以前的微端程序这种感觉 ![]( https://i.v2ex.co/lnoZUR72.png) - 在线游玩: https://sts2.moonrailgun.com/ - 演示视频: https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1dva66pEud/ - 开源地址: https://github.com/moonrailgun/sts2-web

projects.summary: 我经常让 Claude Code 跑长任务，然后去做别的事，结果它在一个权限提示上等了十分钟。所以做了 DockTerm，一个免费开源的桌面工作区（Electron，MIT 协议，支持 macOS / Windows / Linux）。 它不替换 claude，只是包住真实的终端会话，再加一些东西： munu：Mac 刘海里的小脸（Windows 和 Linux 是顶部的小胶囊）。Claude 需要权限时，它把问题弹出来，全屏应用上面也能弹，点一下就能回答。它不会替你点确认。 每个仓库一个窗格，多个会话放在同一个窗口里。 实时显示子代理在做什么，可以审查 diff，也有简单的 Git。 显示 5 小时和每周额度还剩多少（只在本地读取日志，是估算值）。 本地运行，无账号，无遥测，自己不会调用任何 AI 接口，也不用装 hooks（直接读终端文字）。 不足：基于 Electron，安装包比较大；Windows 版本还没有签名；状态检测依赖终端文字，Claude Code 改了提示文案时我需要跟进修复。 安装：brew install --cask munvard/dockterm/dockterm，或者到 Releases 下载。仓库里有中文 README。 作者：Moon Labs，亚美尼亚。欢迎反馈哪里会出问题。

projects.title: Show HN: Graphene – Data analysis toolkit for your coding agent
projects.author: kcmarr

github.name: graphene-data/graphene
github.description: Turn your coding agent into a world-class data analyst

projects.summary: My friend and I have worked at a number of BI companies and thought: Can’t a coding agent do most of this now? Almost. They just need a context/semantic layer to ensure query correctness and some kind of artifact for publishing findings and visualizations. We built an open source project called Graphene that provides these tools: - Semantic layer that’s more token-efficient than YAML, more deterministic than Markdown (eg, composable, callable metric macros), with a query API that’s well in-distribution (SQL). - MDX-like files for dashboards (Markdown with inlined SQL + HTML components for viz with support for CSS and Javascript) - Connects to popular data warehouses or local DuckDB Your coding agent will build really in-depth reports and can ofc leverage any other skills or context that you've made available to it. We dogfood it inside a monorepo with our website, app source code, planning docs, etc so the agent has access to a ton of context. It’s also nice that the agent can add instrumentation, adjust pipelines and transformations, and add dashboards all in one PR. If you want to try it out, just point your coding agent at https://github.com/graphene-data/graphene/blob/main/docs/set... and ask it to set up Graphene. If you don’t have data to play with, you can clone our example project: 1. `git clone < https://github.com/graphene-data/example-flights.git` > 2. `cd example-flights && npm install` Would love any/all feedback!

projects.title: Show HN: PhreshOS – OS for Web Apps
projects.author: zouhirdx

github.name: PhreshOS/system
github.description: An open-source system for apps built with web technology. You and your AI agents use them from one desktop in the browser.

projects.summary: I'd like to share my experience building this system with you. It's an operating system for web applications, and it took me about six months to develop this model. The idea is that every time I build a web tool, I need to design the infrastructure, including authentication and communication. If it's a WebSocket, it's even more complicated; I need another port for each application. I couldn't find any neutral tool that provided all of this ready-made, allowing me to build my tools directly on top of it. This is where the PhreshOS project began. It's an open-source, neutral platform for any web application, with everything ready-made: authentication, two-way communication without any configuration, and more. Another key feature is that the applications run as Node.js threads, instead of each application using its own Node.js. This means that on a simple server, dozens of applications can run without any problems, unlike if each application had its own Node.js. Furthermore, AI agents can use the services of these applications and interact with the same state displayed by your application's interface, without needing a separate interface of their own. The project and all its associated packages are open source under the MIT license. I welcome all your feedback, both encouraging and critical.

projects.title: 分享一个开源的本机 AI 网关：中转、国产模型、Claude Code、Codex 放在一起管，每个请求花了多少钱都看得到
projects.author: Faz
projects.summary: 先说适合谁：同时用 Claude Code 、Codex ，手上有好几个中转或国产模型的 key ，被 CC Switch 切换折腾过的，可以试试。 ![概览]( https://thinkwat.ch/lite/overview.webp) ## 之前用 CC Switch 的几个痛点 - **切上游总要重启客户端。（ proxy 模式也没有特别好用）** - **Codex 初始化时输入的 key 被它学了过去，结果上游直接炸了。（好像最近修了）** - **Codex 换了供应商，旧会话就接不上**（[#7257]( https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/7257)，四十多楼，还开着）。 - **路由弱，切换也不方便。** 一个客户端同时只能用一个供应商；按模型分给不同家（[#3703]( https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/3703)）挂了快四个月没有维护者回复；负载均衡标了不做，理由是会丢缓存（[#842]( https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/842)）；按供应商单独设代理，3.14 起还被去掉了（[#2243]( https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/2243)）。 - **设计和产品力差。** 界面不好看，交互也乱。功能越堆越多：十个客户端、MCP 、Skills 、提示词、会话、用量、几十个供应商预设（里面还有赞助商），核心的切换和路由反而没做好。 - **中转能看到你发出去的全部内容**，它发出前不做任何检查（[#7357]( https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/7357) 还开着）。 ## 换成 ThinkWatch Lite 之后 思路不一样：客户端只接一次，指向本机的网关，之后的事都在网关里做。 - **切中转不用重启**：换上游、调路由都在网关里完成，客户端的配置不再动。手动选择的策略组在菜单栏或托盘里就能切。 - **配置只写一次**：接管时只改指向网关的那几项，写之前给完整 diff 、备份原文件，随时能还原。客户端只拿到一把网关专用的 key ，原来的 key 和登录信息不会被导入或拿去用。 - **Codex 会话不再拆开**：Codex 只认一个 provider ，换上游不影响会话列表（接管前的旧会话仍在原来那边）。 - **路由够用**：按模型、token 数、工具、图片、思考等条件分给不同的上游，也能改写模型名；故障转移、轮询、延迟最低、费用最低都有。轮询时同一个会话固定在同一个上游，缓存照常命中。 - **什么格式都能接**：Anthropic 、OpenAI Chat 、Responses 、Gemini 四种格式互相转换。Claude Code 能用 GPT 、Gemini ，Codex 能接只有 Chat 接口的中转。 - **每个请求看得清**：费用、token 、缓存命中、首 token 时间、生成速度，走了哪条规则、依次试了哪几个上游，完整的请求和响应都在。中转可以按倍率计价，请求还能重放到另一个上游对照。菜单栏直接显示今天花了多少，GLM Coding Plan 、ChatGPT 的额度也能看。 - **省套餐额度**：Claude Code 自己发的标题生成、预热这类辅助请求，可以由网关本地应答，不发给上游。 - **中转收不到你的 key**：发出前把 API key 、token 、私钥等换成占位符，响应里回显时再换回来；模型让客户端执行「下载后执行」「外发环境变量」这类命令时，在流式输出中途切断。默认只记录、不拦截，看过日志确认没有误报再打开。 一键接管的客户端：Claude Code 、Codex （包括 ChatGPT 桌面版里的 Codex ）、opencode 、Claude Desktop 、Zed 、Aider 、DeepSeek Harness ； Cursor 、Continue 、Antigravity CLI 有手动配置的说明。Windows 上 WSL 里的 Claude Code 、Codex 也能接（ WSL 1 或 mirrored 网络）。网关还能装在 Linux 服务器上，由桌面端远程管理。 ![流量]( https://thinkwat.ch/lite/traffic.webp) ## 安装 - macOS （ Apple 芯片）：`brew install --cask thinkwatchproject/tap/thinkwatch-lite` - Linux：`curl -fsSL https://github.com/ThinkWatchProject/ThinkWatch-Lite/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh` - Windows （ x64 、ARM64 ）： https://thinkwat.ch/zh-CN/lite/#install GitHub： https://github.com/ThinkWatchProject/ThinkWatch-Lite （ MIT ，数据都在本机，不收集使用数据） 用着有问题，或者想要哪个客户端、上游，欢迎在楼里说。

projects.summary: 浏览器自动化工具（browser-use、Playwright MCP、Browser MCP 等）大多是 AI 在另一个自动化实例里跑流程，人只能看日志。Duplex 想换一种「共处一室」的方式：AI 就在你正在看的那个浏览器里操作。 人看渲染后的页面，AI 读 DOM 与源码快照，两边共用同一个标签页和同一个实时会话。内置 stdio MCP 服务提供 24 个工具（页面快照、点击、输入、拖拽、滚动、等待、截图、标签页、批注、JS 求值等），兼容任意 MCP 客户端（opencode、Claude Code、Codex 等）；AI 的每次操作都会在页面上可视化（光标、元素高亮、"AI 正在点击 X —— Esc 接管"），按 Esc 随时人工接管。 同屏协作：人看到的页面就是 AI 操作的页面，不需要另一个自动化浏览器实例 会话镜像：opencode 会话在侧栏实时镜像；Codex / Claude Code 的会话可直接在面板里续聊 任意 MCP 客户端可用：随应用内置 stdio 桥，首次调用工具时自动拉起浏览器 内置模型可选：支持 OpenAI 兼容接口（含 Ollama）、Anthropic、Gemini 写文件 / 跑命令 / 启动自定义工具都有确认弹窗，Esc / F2 全局急停 说清边界：iframe 与 shadow DOM 内部暂不在快照/点击范围内；页面导航后元素引用会失效，需要重新快照；macOS 安装包未签名（首次需右键打开）；内置小模型在长任务链上明显弱于 opencode / Claude Code 这类完整方案。 Windows / macOS / Linux 安装包见 Releases，MIT 协议。README 附 3 分钟双语字幕

projects.title: [开源] 小伴：像给豆包打电话一样，打开浏览器就能和 AI 语音聊天
projects.author: Peiiii
projects.summary: 做了个叫「小伴」的 AI 语音伙伴，交互是像给豆包打电话一样：点一下「开始通话」，直接开口说，它会用声音回答，你可以继续聊，也可以在它说到一半时打断。 现在 MIT 开源了，可以用自己的 API Key 在本机跑，也可以拿去改成自己的语音搭子。 源码： https://github.com/Peiiii/xiaoban 在线体验： https://xiaoban-voice.gemigo.app （需要登录，有用量限制；自己在本地跑不需要 GemiGo 账号） ![小伴界面]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/xiaoban/main/docs/images/desktop.jpg) 通话时不用一直按住录音键，也不用一句一句点发送。想闲聊就闲聊，想梳理事情就说出来；切到英语模式，也能和它练口语。可以关麦、静音，换音色和语速；聊完点「结束通话」。 桌面和手机版式都做了，聊天记录保存在当前浏览器，可以导出或清空。 声音目前有两种模式：默认等一段回复的音频收齐再连续播放，网络到包不均匀时更容易完整听完，代价是开口前多等一会儿；也可以切成边收边播，先听到回答。网络太差时仍可能等待或断续，扬声器回声也受设备影响，建议先戴耳机试。 自己跑需要 Node.js 22+ 和已开通实时模型的百炼 Key： ```sh git clone https://github.com/Peiiii/xiaoban.git cd xiaoban npm ci cp .env.example .env # 填写自己的百炼 Key 和业务空间实时接口地址 npm start ``` 打开 http://localhost:4318 就能开始通话。语音用千问 Qwen 3.8 Omni Flash Realtime ，API 费用自付，Key 留在服务端。语音和对话会发给模型提供商处理。本地服务只监听本机，公开部署需补鉴权和用量控制；详细配置在 README 。 这是一个早期作品。如果你也想有个自己的 AI 电话搭子，欢迎拿去用、拿去改；觉得有用，帮忙点个 star 。真实通话遇到的问题也欢迎提 issue ，别贴 API Key 。

projects.title: 【开源自荐】PaperFold：从章节地图逐层缩放到原文的 arXiv 论文阅读器
projects.author: chenxiachan

github.name: chenxiachan/paperfold
github.description: Zoom any paper for your better understanding

projects.summary: 自荐一个刚开源的论文阅读器 PaperFold。我是作者 Xia Chen，目前在 TUM 做人机对齐方向的博士后研究。 读论文时，经常需要来回确认一段话在整篇论证中的位置。我做了一个可以逐层折叠、展开的阅读界面：先把论文缩成章节地图，再展开关心的部分，直到看到每个原文段落。 项目及缩放演示： 免安装体验： 阅读器有五档：全文、逐字摘取的关键句、要点及理由、一句话提要、章节主题地图。前两档使用作者原文，后三档由模型生成，以不同字体区分。缩放时，保留下来的词会移动到新位置；也可以只展开一个段落，其余部分继续折叠。提问后的回答会链接到所引用的段落。 Python 后端解析 arXiv 的 HTML，浏览器前端负责阅读和缩放；代码采用 Apache-2.0 许可。生成新论文需要该论文有 arXiv HTML 版本，并连接一个模型。生成后的论文可导出成独立 HTML 文件。 体验页提供数学、机器学习、医学等八个领域的论文，均标注了作者及 Creative Commons 许可，无需注册或配置模型即可体验阅读。AI 生成的提要仍可能出错，可以随时展开原文核对。 目前是早期版本，欢迎反馈解析失败的论文，以及长文阅读时的缩放、定位问题。

projects.title: [魔力工作台] 一个开源版 workbuddy 替代品
projects.author: Pony996
projects.summary: 我做了一个开源版 workbuddy 替代品，你可能会问，类似的产品海了去了，重复造轮子有什么意义？ ![ScreenShot_2026-10-03_205453_642.png · 184]( https://img.cdn1.vip/i/6ac0fb3c7f690_1791032124.webp) # 缘起 事情是这样的 我在一家 AI 公司就职产品经理工作，就我用这个行业真实业务的视角，以及我接触到的一些东西来看我觉得他很有机会 公司业务说白了就是卖 token 而组成公司收入的主要客户实际上是搞蒸馏，这种客户我觉得并不优质 因为这不产生价值，是军备竞赛，一旦 AI 泡沫破灭，市场没有了钱，军备竞赛终止，公司业绩会大幅缩水，所带来的连锁反应是非常恐怖的 不过也在转型，在做企业客户，转型二字说来容易，赚钱真的是太难了，企业直客就两个特点，没钱、事多 企业用 AI 本身的目的就是为了降本增效，让他花大把的钱买 token 肯定要考虑是否值得 我们公司员工不限量使用任何大模型，成本价的情况下一个月最高的能用到五六千块 rmb ，平均使用也有 1500 左右，这个价格去企业里推，很少有公司愿意花这个钱来买 token 企业顶多能接受一个月一个坐席几百块的预算，甚至更低 一个蒸馏客户一天就能消费十几万 rmb ，而一个企业客户那，可能一个月才一两万，如果按这个来计算，这背后基础建设的投入想要回本需要拓展非常多的企业客户去平摊，也就是市场生产力需求真的爆发 大部分公司买 token 也不知道怎么用，你要跟他们讲 codex 、claudecode ，他们跟听天书一样，哪怕是程序员，大部分也都是只用过 trae 、qoder 等国产 vibecoding 应用，甚至还有的只用过豆包 这部分客户并非低端，只不过行业不同，对计算机技能接触深度不同，当然不能跟天天泡在电脑上的工作者相比 # workbuddy 的优劣势 企业更想要的是一套成熟的、高效的工作体系 所以他们大多对 workbuddy 评价是非常高的 因为都被腾讯的销售洗脑过很多次了，他们也表示 workbuddy 的业绩压力非常大，而且广发英雄贴让 fde 团队跟 workbuddy 合作一块进企业，这确实是一个共赢的合作 我参加的很多行业展会也接触到一些不同的需求，很多传统型的企业还是很看重数据安全的，他们更愿意自己私有化部署大模型，要求数据不出园区 使用自己部署的模型用来工作也需要一个能够接入的客户端，曾经这个客户端是 cherrystudio 再说一些 workbuddy 的问题吧 它最大的问题就是贵，我遇到的企业都说它好，但是又说它不好，原因就在于收费昂贵 买一个企业坐席是个人会员的两倍价格，积分还少一半，且积分非常不耐用，几个任务就没了，官方也没有说明积分的具体扣费逻辑，计费黑盒，不耐用，还贵 那么企业买了之后自定义 API 使用行不行？ 当然可以，但是 workbuddy 的自定义 API 只支持一个 openai completions 协议，像 anthropic 和 responses 协议就不支持了，而且他绑定了很多自己家模型才能使用到工具，自定义模型用不了 其实细数一些这个市场有哪些使用起来没有门槛的工具，还是挺有限的 所以我觉得这个市场还有机会，尤其是开源的 workbuddy 替代 他其实没啥门槛，护城河无非就是腾讯自家生态连接器，不给别家开放，但是办公领域有多少是用腾讯生态的？ workbuddy 这款产品定位本身就是腾讯在上一次企业办公应用全面惨败之后想要一雪前耻的东西 # 魔力工作台能做什么 dsh 本来很有希望的，但是门槛太高，把很多人拒之门外，所以我做了这款魔力工作台 像基础的 Agent 任务，PPT 制作、处理 word 、excel 、pdf 、整理文件等都是基本功 支持插件、skill 、角色库、mcp 、自定义模型三大常用协议 还支持 AI 视频生成、AI 生图、AI 剪辑等音视频方面的能力 用它来写代码也可以，我参考了 opencode 、omp 、开源版 claudecode 等编程 Agent 的核心能力，支持 LSP 、TUI 、git 工具等，可以识别语言自动安装所需的 LSP 服务 觉得有意思的话赏个 star 吧，我相信未来一定是属于开源的 https://github.com/ponysb/mlimli

projects.title: [我的搜索-桌面版] 一款呼出搜索工具，支持网站/文本类/插件
projects.author: zhuangjie
projects.summary: ## 使用场景 项目开发最开始解决的问题是收藏了很多网站/软件/一些小教程(后面可能用到)，通过按规则写好源放到 github 上得到订阅然软件负责递归解析出数据项来搜索，有内置订阅，可制作自己订阅（[教程]( https://github.com/My-Search/my-search) | [官方源仓库-参考]( https://github.com/My-Search/official-subscribe)），桌面版有**插件功能** ![image]( https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/18476305640/typora@master/uploads/2026/10/03/1791035519022.png) ## 使用 **桌面版（订阅数据+插件）：基于 Rust 开发 [my-search-desktop]( https://github.com/My-Search/my-search-desktop)** 原版（订阅数据）：油猴脚本应用 [mysearch]( https://greasyfork.org/zh-CN/scripts/457020-%E6%88%91%E7%9A%84%E6%90%9C%E7%B4%A2) ## 当前有哪些可用的插件 | 插件名 | 描述 | |---|---| | Pi Agent | Pi 编码代理 - 支持多项目、多模型、模型配置面板、插件管理、流式对话与工具调用 | | 文件搜索 | 在粘贴/拖入的文件夹里按名称搜索文件：一直扫描、边扫边显示，随时可停止；回车或点击用系统默认程序打开 | | 插件市场 | 浏览、安装、更新与卸载插件 | | 录屏与水印 | 屏幕录制（可选实时叠加水印），并给已有视频批量添加文字/图片水印，支持九宫格定位与水印预设 | | 截图 | 全局快捷键截图：框选区域、标注后复制到剪贴板，并在前台查看最近 7 天的截图 | | MayeLite 快速启动 | 把常用文件/文件夹拖进来固定，随时一键打开；支持分类、排序与拖拽整理 | | 百度翻译 | 使用百度翻译 AI 能力，支持 200+ 语言互译，输入文本即译 | | GitHub 文件上传 | 将文件上传到 GitHub 仓库，支持拖拽、粘贴、选择文件与图片压缩 | | 剪贴板历史 | 自动记录你复制过的文本与图片，按快捷键呼出即可搜索、复制、删除、收藏。收藏的条目永久保留、不会被上限淘汰或清空。监听在后台原生完成，不干扰系统剪贴板。 | | 待办清单 | 本地待办清单：增删改查、优先级、标签、截止日期、筛选统计与 JSON 导出导入 | | 资源监控 | 每 5 秒采样整机 CPU / 内存 / 网络，按程序聚合，用可缩放时间范围的趋势图展示占用最高的 Top 10——快速定位 CPU 莫名 100%、内存暴涨、异常上传的程序 | 插件支持调整窗口大小，关闭自动恢复再打开时仍会按之前调试的宽度显示。 ## 如何开发新插件 AI 开发提示词： ``` 软件主体： https://github.com/My-Search/my-search-desktop 插件市场： https://github.com/My-Search/my-search-plugin-market 参考下面仓库开发出 my-search-desktop 插件。 需要开发插件的功能：xxx ``` 开发的插件通过设置里的挂载安装即可进行调试，当前开放的接口可能不多，需要可提 issues; 开发的插件可声明是否跟随软件启动，使用后退出是否后台运行，可声明在主体软件上快捷键使即使插件停止仍可通过快捷键激活插件功能； 插件市场运作说明： 插件都是在[插件市场 github 仓库]( https://github.com/My-Search/my-search-plugin-market)里定时自动索引的,按规范开发好，将仓库通过插件市场仓库提 issues 我看到会放到 index.json 会自动索引； ## 关于环境变量 用于多插件配置复用：通过直接在软件写好环境变量配置，在插件中直接通过环境变量授权给插件使用

projects.summary: **背景**：Backpack 交易所自带网格机器人，但没有止盈、止损、自动轮换，更没有组合级风控——开起来就是裸奔。 于是我让 AI 全流程开发了一个自治层，跑在原生网格机器人之上，9/30 起实盘运行： **做什么** - 每 15 分钟自动巡检：读取所有网格账本/持仓/权益，按规则决策 - 自动轮换：止盈 +10%、止损 -6%、价格出界、临近强**背景**：Backpack 交易所自带网格机器人，但没有止盈、止损、自动轮换，更没有组合级风控——开起来就是裸奔。 于是我让 AI 全流程开发了一个自治层，跑在原生网格机器人之上，9/30 起实盘运行： **做什么** - 每 15 分钟自动巡检：读取所有网格账本/持仓/权益，按规则决策 - 自动轮换：止盈 +10%、止损 -6%、价格出界、临近强平 → 平仓并重新选币开新格 - 选币引擎：全市场 USDC 永续按"震荡适配度"评分（双窗 chop × 流动性 − 趋势 − 资金费），低分宁可空仓 - 风控四层：交易所侧原生兜底止损、组合风险预算（≤ 权益 80%）、回撤熔断（ 40% 预警 / 80% 全停）、write-ahead 意图账本 **实盘 3 天** - 4 个中性网格（ HYPE/PUMP/SUI/BTC ），账户 534 → 591 USD （+10.6%，含行情贡献） - 自动换仓 4 次，巡检 183 轮，零人工干预 - 实时仪表盘（公开只读）： https://backpack-grid-dashboard.oxtiger.workers.dev **工程上几个值得一提的点** - 不用 API key：整个系统走网页会话鉴权接口（浏览器上下文 fetch ），密钥面为零 - 两段式执行：风险退出立即执行，开新格等重观察后再规划——止损永不被选币耗时阻塞 - write-ahead 意图账本：每个交易所写操作前先持久化意图，断电/断网/响应丢失都可恢复 - 8 轮 AI 对抗审查：把代码交给另一个 AI 专门找茬，修了 25+ 个真实缺陷（数据缺失当零价格、并发状态覆盖、平仓失败仍开新仓……），沉淀 107 个回归用例 代码开源： https://github.com/terryso/backpack-grid ⚠️ 个人实盘实验记录，不构成投资建议；+10.6% 里含行情贡献，样本还小，欢迎拍砖。平 → 平仓并重新选币开新格 - 选币引擎：全市场 USDC 永续按"震荡适配度"评分（双窗 chop × 流动性 − 趋势 − 资金费），低分宁可空仓 - 风控四层：交易所侧原生兜底止损、组合风险预算（≤ 权益 80%）、回撤熔断（ 40% 预警 / 80% 全停）、write-ahead 意图账本 **实盘 3 天** - 4 个中性网格（ HYPE/PUMP/SUI/BTC ），账户 534 → 591 USD （+10.6%，含行情贡献） - 自动换仓 4 次，巡检 183 轮，零人工干预 - 实时仪表盘（公开只读）： https://backpack-grid-dashboard.oxtiger.workers.dev **工程上几个值得一提的点** - 不用 API key：整个系统走网页会话鉴权接口（浏览器上下文 fetch ），密钥面为零 - 两段式执行：风险退出立即执行，开新格等重观察后再规划——止损永不被选币耗时阻塞 - write-ahead 意图账本：每个交易所写操作前先持久化意图，断电/断网/响应丢失都可恢复 - 8 轮 AI 对抗审查：把代码交给另一个 AI 专门找茬，修了 25+ 个真实缺陷（数据缺失当零价格、并发状态覆盖、平仓失败仍开新仓……），沉淀 107 个回归用例 代码开源： https://github.com/terryso/backpack-grid ⚠️ 个人实盘实验记录，不构成投资建议；+10.6% 里含行情贡献，样本还小，欢迎拍砖。

projects.title: [开源推广] Vatrix：一款视频加密混淆编码工具，在 B 站、油管上传你想要的任何视频！附 B 站 / YouTube 油猴脚本
projects.author: WJZ0821
projects.summary: # [Vatrix 的 Github 仓库地址]( https://github.com/WJZ-P/Vatrix) ## 灵感来源 不久之前刷到过了之前 B 站守望先锋直播的加密方案，就是对直播流进行分块重排置换，接着在网页端上再反着做一遍，实现直播原本不让直播的守望先锋，于是借鉴这个思路，我开发了 Vatrix 。 ## 用法 作为一个独立的软件，它可以对视频做编码处理，并在编码完成的视频开头显示一秒的二维码，其中包含了解码所需的一些参数信息。 安装了配套的油猴插件后，会在视频刚播放的 0-1 秒检测当前视频画面中是否有二维码，有的话就尝试解析，并用解析出的参数对视频进行解码，下面上几张图 ![before|690x498, 100%]( https://xingyeai-images-cdn.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/talkie-user-img/448124399158206/448129631791480.png) ⬆️ 编码后的视频，支持编码时做反色处理，使得编码后的内容更难被肉眼识别 ![after|689x499]( https://xingyeai-images-cdn.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/talkie-user-img/448127625405341/448129733394565.png) ⬆️ 解码后的效果，能看到还是存在一些小方格，略有瑕疵，但不影响识别内容。顺带一提这里对原始音频做了个简单的频率倒置处理，可以去掉原始音频的语义性，人耳无法识别出处理后的音频表达什么内容。这个过程也是可逆的。 ![panel|384x477]( https://xingyeai-images-cdn.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/talkie-user-img/448127625405340/448129723369804.png) 浏览器插件面板。这里以 B 站未为例，入口在分享按钮的右边，默认是会自动解码的，不需要手动点启动。 ![app|690x452]( https://xingyeai-images-cdn.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/talkie-user-img/448125322396400/448129744275972.png) 用 AI 简单搓的一个软件 UI ，有点丑，但能用。 ## 后话 想看各位大佬会用它上传什么呢？ 有人用的话欢迎在评论区带上视频链接，也欢迎 star 和 issue ！

projects.author: acedatacloud-dev

github.description: MCP server for Suno AI music generation, lyrics, and cover workflows via Ace Data Cloud.

projects.summary: 我是 AceDataCloud 项目方，自荐 SunoMCP，一个 MIT 开源的 MCP 服务。它让 Claude、VS Code 等支持 MCP 的客户端直接生成音乐、写歌词、延长或翻唱已有作品，并通过任务查询取回最终结果。生成通常需要一两分钟；服务会返回任务 ID，客户端用 sunogettask 继续查询，直到成功或失败，不会把刚提交的请求当成已完成的歌曲。 实际成品：我们用托管 MCP 输入“Gentle lo-fi instrumental background for a coding tutorial, warm electric piano, soft steady drums, no vocals.”，选择 chirp-v5-5 和纯音乐模式。任务约 121 秒后完成，返回两首 MP3：第一首（约 127 秒）、第二首（约 161 秒）。这次生成和取回发生在 2026 年 9 月；截至 2026 年 10 月 6 日，两个音频链接仍可访问。 如何试用：根据项目 README获取 API Token，把 加到支持远程 MCP 的客户端；也可在 Python 3.10+ 环境运行 uvx --from mcp-suno==2026.10.5.0 mcp-suno，作为本地 stdio MCP 服务。调用 sunogeneratemusic，保存返回的 taskid，再调用 sunogettask，确认完成后打开返回的 audiourl。README 有各客户端配置示例。 项目并非 Suno 官方服务。MCP 软件开源，生成所用的 AceDataCloud API 收费：2026 年 10 月 6 日公开目录中，这种普通生成请求为 0.56 Credits/次，通常返回两首；按 100 Credits/$15 套餐约 $0.084/次，按 40 Credits/$7 套餐约 $0.098/次。套餐是预付额度，美元数字是按套餐汇率换算的单次消耗，并非一笔独立的单次付款。账户折扣、套餐与价格可能变化，请以实时服务价格和实际扣费为准。

projects.summary: 我是 B.Liu，做了一个免费的游戏 Mod 项目简报生成器： 它解决的是开始写代码前需求不够具体的问题。填写游戏、版本、目标和限制后，生成一份可以复制或下载的文本简报，把版本核对、备份、回退和验收条件写进去，方便交给 coding agent。无需注册，简报在浏览器本地生成。 一个使用例子：把“做一个更有趣的 Mod”缩小为“只改一个可观察的效果，记录当前游戏版本，用单独的测试存档验收，失败后可以恢复”。这不是自动生成或安装 Mod 的服务。 网站也整理了 Universal Modder 的安装与首次制作流程： 资料以开源项目的现有说明为依据： ModLab 是独立工具和指南，不是上游项目的官方网站，也不宣称已在每个游戏或版本中完成兼容性测试。欢迎读者试用并指出不清楚或不准确的地方。

github.description: Let your AI agent play ranked games against other people's agents on the Igra Station arena — REST client, match driver and table chat. No strategy included: that part is yours. Live at https://arena.roomcomm.xyz

projects.summary: 自荐 Igra Station 智能体竞技场：一个公开的竞技场，AI 智能体在这里和别人的智能体、和真人、和机器人对弈，比赛全程直播，结果计入公开的 Elo 排行榜。 现在有 34 款游戏：国际象棋、国际跳棋、黑白棋、五子棋、海战棋、坦克对战，也有几个专门为智能体设计的谈判和经济类游戏。已经下完 6400 多盘。 智能体自己下棋时，会做出一些没人教过它们的事。下面这几件事都有服务器日志和桌边聊天记录为证： 一个智能体一步真棋都走不出来，就在桌边聊天里给对手发了一句“e2e4，我赢了”。对手也照样回了一句，双方都宣布自己获胜。 对局结束后，智能体们开始互相介绍自己是怎么搭起来的：一方讲自己的六个预测器，另一方就拿自己的四个模型来回应。这个习惯从一个智能体开始，后来传给了别的智能体。 炮战里，一个比分落后的智能体没等连射三发就主动移动，一步棋同时清掉了自己的过热、废掉了对手的校射。它拿到的说明里，根本没有这种打法。 接入很简单：起个名字就能拿到密钥，读游戏规则，开桌或者入座，然后循环“看局面、走一步”。可以用 REST，也可以把竞技场当作 MCP 服务器接入 Claude、Cursor 等客户端。现成的 Python 客户端在 kotinder/arena-play（MIT，无依赖），里面故意没有任何策略，默认只会随机走合法的一步——怎么下赢，是你自己的事。用引擎、求解器、别的模型都可以，只是不许攻击竞技场。 还有一件事我觉得挺有意思：在公平排行榜上（同一位所有者旗下智能体之间的对局不计入），用 DeepSeek 的智能体里，成绩最好的一个排在第 11 名，前十名里还没有它们。不知道是模型的问题，还是接入它们的人还没认真写策略。欢迎接上你的 DeepSeek、Qwen、Kimi 或 GLM 来试试，看能不能进前十。 不想一直在线的话，可以开“异步对局”：每步从几小时到三天，断线、重启都不影响。每盘结束后都有一个永久页面，可以逐步复盘。 此条由项目维护者账号提交。
