projects.title: Show HN: Terminal Gym – a Claude mod that makes you do pushups between prompts
projects.author: heynaitik
projects.summary: Hi HN, I built this for myself and wanted to open-source it. The problem: I wanted a way to get reminders in-between prompts as I often spend long hours in the terminal, especially now that we're usually parallel-processing so many agents. The first version was a simple rep counter in my Claude Code status line and a shell script to log reps. Since Claude Code shipped mods this week, I thought this was a good way to level it up with even more accountability. How it works: 1. Every day, you get a daily goal for either squats, pushups, or dips (e.g. 0/100 pushups) with +5 / +10 / +25 buttons to log a set in the terminal. 2. Reminders for sets are spread out across the day so it doesn't get annoying, starting from your first prompt for the day. A toast tells you when the next set is due. 3. Strict mode is opt-in: if you're falling behind in terms of your daily rep goal, it will block your prompts till you log some reps. Added a streak counter for some added fun. All local and data is stored as plain files in ~/.claude/fitness. Install: claude plugin marketplace add DrumAndCode/terminal-gym && claude plugin install terminal-gym@terminal-gym Overall, thought the mod API is super powerful and can't wait to see the stuff people build with it. Eg: I built a clickable onboarding process inside the terminal, and that felt quite powerful to use. Now you can enjoy spending both tokens and calories. :)

projects.summary: 阮老师好，自荐一下我做的 open-compute，一个可以运行在自己服务器上的 Cloudflare Workers 兼容平台，Apache-2.0 开源。 我是 Cloudflare 的粉丝，很喜欢 Workers 这套开发方式。不过我们做 B 端交付时，经常遇到客户因为数据安全要求、企业网络限制，需要把应用和数据留在自己的基础设施里。为了私有化，又得重新搭存储、队列、任务调度这些东西。所以我做了 open-compute，希望能把这套熟悉的开发体验带到客户内网。 它把运行时、部署、网关、存储、队列、工作流和管理界面打包进一个 Rust 二进制，底层使用 workerd，面向单机部署，默认使用 SQLite 和本地文件存储，不需要先搭一套 Kubernetes、外部数据库和缓存服务。 兼容是这个项目的重点：在支持范围内，现有 Cloudflare Workers 项目的业务代码一行都不用改，原来的 Wrangler 配置、Bindings 和框架适配器都能继续使用，切换部署目标即可运行。API 按 Cloudflare 的接口实现，已有的 SDK 和工具也可以复用。 目前支持 Workers、KV、D1、R2、Durable Objects、Queues、Workflows、Cron、Cache、Images、Vectorize、AI Search，以及 Static Assets、Service Bindings 等能力。具体支持范围和单机环境下的行为差异，可以查看产品矩阵。 我已经在一些 B 端客户的私有化环境里部署并跑了一段时间，也在实际交付中持续完善它。现在开源出来，欢迎有类似需求的朋友试用、反馈。 官网和文档：open-compute.dev

projects.summary: 自荐一个 MIT 开源桌面工具：HRouter Desktop，用于集中管理 Claude Code、Codex、Gemini CLI 等 AI 编程工具的供应商配置和模型线路。 做这个工具的起因是频繁切换模型：Claude Code 一份配置，Codex 一份，Gemini CLI 又是一份，每次换供应商都要重新找 Key、端点和模型映射，改完还担心覆盖原有配置。我希望把这些接入操作集中到一个工作台，让使用者少折腾配置，多专注编程。 主要功能 统一接入工作台：覆盖 Claude Code、Claude Desktop、Codex、Gemini CLI、OpenCode 等 11 个 Agent；可接入官方供应商、自建端点和兼容服务。 先看变更，再切配置：主动开启 Claude / Codex 配置保护后，可保留自定义字段、预览变更、保存本地快照，并在恢复前检查冲突。 为模型准备备用线路：配置主备供应商及精确模型路由，在支持的本地代理模式下自动故障转移。不同 Agent 的支持范围不同，并非全部都支持代理接管。 常用配置存成方案：保存供应商、MCP、Skills 的选择，重新应用前先检查。接入方案不等于完整配置备份。 用量可视化：查看请求、Token、缓存和本地费用估算，提供浮动用量窗口与 macOS 桌面小组件。费用估算仅供参考，不是供应商账单。 使用桌面工具不需要 HRouter 账户，也不要求使用 HRouter 服务；可自行选择已有供应商。 界面预览 以 Agent 为中心的接入工作台： 模型线路与备用供应商管理： 与 CC Switch 的关系 项目基于 Jason Young 及贡献者开发的 CC Switch，保留原作者版权与 MIT 许可证，独立维护，不是上游官方发行版。 上游的供应商、代理、MCP、Skills、会话和用量基础能力仍然保留；本分支主要围绕 Agent 优先的界面、配置保护流程、可复用的接入方案、精确模型主备链和兼容性修复进行扩展，不将继承能力包装为新发明。这是本分支的改动说明，不代表当前上游缺少所有对应能力。 下载与

projects.title: Show HN: Fakeflac-go – A tool for quickly finding "fake" .flac files
projects.author: DakotaR
projects.summary: This is my first real project; keep in mind I have no formal programming/CS background. It is hand-written; AI was only used for some conceptual questions. Background: There's an epidemic of "fake" .flac audio files floating around: lossy audio masquerading as true lossless-quality audio. I rewrote the fakeflac.py utility in Go, adding multithreading to greatly improve performance, and increasing portability by embedding an optional WASM build of ffmpeg. Limitations: the original fakeflac algorithm is a great starting point, but it fails to find a cutoff point with some (obviously very low quality) audio files and produces a false score of 100%. I added CLI flags to tune the cutoff detection, but future versions definitely need some work (less normalization? entirely new detection algorithm?)

projects.title: 我做了一个黑白方块文件传输工具
projects.author: aalmix
projects.summary: ![程序界面]( https://beeimg.us.ci/temp/6abfbe083f371.png) 最近用 AI 做了一个小工具：把文件变成一段像老式黑白电视没信号时的“雪花视频”，再从画面里把文件还原出来。 起因很实际。有些环境里，把文件复制进去很方便，想把里面生成的日志、配置拿出来查看，却没那么**顺手**。 这让我想起之前在阮一峰老师博客里看到过的类似思路：把文件编码成黑白画面，连起来做成视频，需要的时候再解码。GitHub 上也有这样的项目，比如 [InfinityVault]( https://github.com/thebitanpaul/InfinityVault)，它提供文件转视频、视频转文件和从 YouTube 下载视频的功能，探索把 YouTube 当作文件存储空间。 **文件变成视频之后，B 站、YouTube 岂不就成了我们的“网盘”？😝** 我沿着这个思路，做了现在这个项目：[xxx-file-trans]( https://github.com/wubh2012/xxx-file-trans)。 它的原理其实不难理解。文件本来就是一串 0 和 1 ，把黑色方块当作 1 ，白色方块当作 0 ，就能把数据画出来。一张画面装不下，就拆成很多张，按顺序播放。 于是，一份文件就变成了不停变化的黑白方块，看起来就像小时候黑白电视机雪花块，程序读到的却是文件分片。 完整过程是这样： ```text 文件 → 压缩、分片 → 黑白方块画面 → 播放或制成视频 ↓ 还原文件 ← 拼接、解压 ← 校验、识别 ← 抓屏或读取视频 ``` 目前可以用两种玩法。 一种是直接通过屏幕传。发送端只有一个 `sender.html`，用浏览器打开，选好文件，就可以在窗口里循环播放。接收端框选这块画面，持续抓屏、识别，收齐之后自动还原文件。 发送端不需要安装 Python ，也不需要启动服务器。对于“页面能复制进去，文件不好复制出来”的场景，这种形式比较方便。 另一种是先把文件做成 MP4 。制作端选好文件，生成一段黑白方块视频或者自己录制一段发送端播放的视频；接收方拿到视频后，用接收端逐帧读取，再还原成原始的文件。 如果把这段 视频上传到 B 站或者 YouTube ，视频平台就成了中间的载体。接收方可以尝试从播放器画面接收，或者取得视频文件后离线解码。项目里已经放了两段可以看看这种“文件视频”到底长什么样。B 站测试视频 - https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1Euan6zEL8 - https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1Euan6zEL8 不过，把字节画出来只是第一步。真正麻烦的是：画面可能被缩放，抓屏可能漏帧，视频平台还会重新压缩。 对普通视频来说，边缘模糊一点通常不影响观看；对文件来说，一个方块读错，就可能把数据弄坏。所以这个项目也做了一些处理： - 每帧带编号和 CRC32 校验，读错的帧丢弃，收到的分片按编号归位。 - 加入前向纠错，在条件满足时恢复少量缺失的数据帧。 - 浏览器循环播放，MP4 重复完整帧序列，给接收端更多补齐机会。 - 保存已接收的进度，中断后可以继续接收同一文件，发送参数需要保持一致。 接收端不必向发送端逐帧回复“收到了”。它记住已经收到的部分，遇到重复帧跳过，遇到缺失帧再补进来。最后检查 gzip 完整性，并显示还原文件的 SHA-256 ，方便与原文件核对。 速度方面，仓库里有一轮 2026 年 10 月 1 日的真实桌面闭环测试：浏览器以 30 FPS 播放，接收端使用 DXGI 抓屏，画面清晰且无遮挡。 | 文件样本 | 原始大小 | 端到端耗时 | |---|---:|---:| | 难压缩二进制 | 1 MB | 约 15 秒 | | 难压缩二进制 | 5 MB | 约 80 秒 | | 难压缩二进制 | 10 MB | 约 161 秒 | | 模拟应用日志 | 10 MB | 约 28 秒 | | 模拟业务 CSV | 5 MB | 约 31 秒 | 这轮测试的六个样本都通过了 SHA-256 和逐字节比对。文本通常能压缩得更小，所以即使原始文件更大，也可能传得更快。具体条件和完整结果见[实测报告]( https://github.com/wubh2012/xxx-file-trans/blob/main/benchmark/results/report-size-matrix-20261001.md)。 这里的耗时是本机桌面测试，每个样本正式测了一次，不包含视频上传、平台转码和下载时间，也不能直接当作远程桌面或视频平台上的速度，大家可以自己测试下。 目前比较适合的是日志、配置、报表和小型资料包情景。另外，黑白编码本身不等于加密，当前项目没有内置文件加密（也许是以后的扩展方向）。 Windows 用户可以从 [Release]( https://github.com/wubh2012/xxx-file-trans/releases/latest) 下载制作端和接收端 EXE ，无需配置 Python ；制作 MP4 仍需要安装 FFmpeg 。浏览器发送端则直接打开 HTML 就能用。 做完这个项目后，我觉得最大的收获是 AI 能快速的把我们的想法做出来并落地，打磨细节真的很费时间! 项目可能还会很多不完善的地方，但还是觉得先发出来，欢迎交流。 项目地址：[wubh2012/xxx-file-trans]( https://github.com/wubh2012/xxx-file-trans)

projects.title: 【开源自荐】fib：性能几乎超过以往所有 Go 网络库，和 Claude 合作完成，代码几乎全部由 Claude 生成
projects.author: lesismal
projects.summary: 最近我和 Claude 合作完成了一个新的 Go 网络库，叫 fib。想法和方向是我的，代码几乎全部由 Claude 生成。它支持 TCP/UDP、TLS、HTTP/1.x、HTTP/2、HTTP/3（QUIC）和 WebSocket，HTTP handler 用的是标准库的 http.Request 和 http.ResponseWriter。 先说结果。在 GitHub Actions 上自动运行的 benchmark 里，和标准库相比，fib 在一些场景下的吞吐能高出数倍，内存也少得多；和 fasthttp 这类以性能著称的库相比，性能也有提升；和 C/C++/Rust 的框架相比，也已经很接近，有些场景还能超过。这些 Action 所在的仓库里有完整的测试代码，每个数字都可以追溯和复现。 当然，不同的硬件规格、测试参数和框架配置，跑出来的结果可能会不一样。欢迎大家在自己的机器上亲自跑一跑这些 benchmark。 先看数据 下面的数据都来自 GitHub Actions 上 lesismal/go--benchmark 几个仓库的 Docker 压测。runner 是 4 vCPU，服务端 2 核、客户端 2 核，1 万连接，1 KiB payload。每个都是单次运行，共享 runner 有噪声，几个百分点的差距可以当作持平。完整表格（包括 CPU 效率、延迟分位数）请点链接看。 先把几个主要的提升列在前面： HTTP/1.1：echo 是 net/http 的 2.3 倍，pipeline 是 net/http 的 6.9 倍、fasthttp 的 1.65 倍，内存只有 net/http 的十分之一 HTTP/2：echo 是 net/http 的 3.7 倍，multiplex 是 net/http 的 13 倍、Rust h2 的 2.6 倍 HTTP/3：吞吐是 quic-go 的 3.4 到 5.4 倍，达到 Cloudflare quiche 的九成以上 TLS：pipeline 是 crypto/tls + net 的 2.9 倍，内存约三分之一 WebSocket：echo 吞吐在 17 个参测框架里最高，只用 32 MB 内存 HTTP/1.1（Actions run，客户端是 Rust tokio） | Server | Echo TPS | Echo MEM | Pipeline TPS | Pipeline MEM | | ----------- | -------: | -------: | -----------: | -----------: | | fib | 194,671 | 32 MB | 1,140,457 | 36 MB | | axum (Rust) | 236,244 | 227 MB | 301,804 | 490 MB | | fasthttp | 139,830 | 197 MB | 692,671 | 197 MB | | net/http | 84,739 | 314 MB | 164,811 | 323 MB | echo 比 fasthttp 高 39%，内存只有它的六分之一。pipeline 场景差距最大，fib 跑到 114 万 TPS，是 axum 的 3.8 倍，内存始终在 36 MB 左右。在我自己不同连接数的测试里，fib 也基本能达到或超过 fasthttp。 HTTP/2 h2c（Actions run） | Server | Echo TPS | Echo MEM | Multiplex TPS | Multiplex MEM | | --------- | -------: | -------: | ------------: | ------------: | | fib | 129,676 | 119 MB | 333,692 | 432 MB | | h2 (Rust) | 143,107 | 246 MB | 129,729 | 870 MB | | net/http | 35,415 | 633 MB | 25,051 | 809 MB | echo 达到 Rust h2 的九成，内存只有它的一半；multiplex 则反过来领先 h2 2.6 倍。 HTTP/3（Actions run，客户端是 quiche） | Server | Echo TPS | Echo MEM | Multiplex TPS | Multiplex MEM | | ------------- | -------: | -------: | ------------: | ------------: | | quiche (Rust) | 72,919 | 387 MB | 101,233 | 881 MB | | fib | 67,396 | 504 MB | 94,443 | 1.05 GB | | quic-go | 19,545 | 1.20 GB | 17,505 | 1.80 GB | 这是提升最明显的一组：和 quic-go 相比，吞吐翻了几倍，内存还少了四到六成。和 quiche 比，内存上还多一些，这是接下来要继续做的。 TLS（Actions run，客户端是 C 的 uSockets + BoringSSL） | Server | TLS 1.3 Echo | TLS 1.3 Pipeline | MEM | | ---------------- | -----------: | ---------------: | ---------: | | fib | 103,427 | 690,000 | 180 MB | | crypto/tls + net | 92,494 | 241,106 | 285–518 MB | | uSockets (C) | 103,972 | 735,000 | 51 MB | | rustls (Rust) | 107,406 | 195,835 | 110–201 MB | echo 和 C、Rust 的实现相差不到 4%，pipeline 到了 uSockets 的九成以上，是 rustls 的 3.5 倍。 WebSocket（Actions run，客户端是 C++ uWebSockets） | Server | Echo TPS | Echo MEM | Pipeline TPS | Pipeline MEM | | ------------------------ | -------: | -------: | -----------: | -----------: | | fib | 138,592 | 32 MB | 984,917 | 32 MB | | gorilla | 122,296 | 229 MB | 205,224 | 235 MB | | nbio | 121,398 | 62 MB | 191,091 | 100 MB | | tokio-tungstenite (Rust) | 83,841 | 105 MB | 748,297 | 286 MB | pipeline 是 gorilla 的 4.8 倍，内存是它的七分之一，不过还落后 uws 和 fnet 一些。 除了网络层，fib 用的协程池 taskpool 也可以单独使用。CI 每次 push 都会把它和 nbio、ants、gopool、fnet 在 Linux、macOS、Windows 上对比一遍，结果在事件循环式的提交场景下领先比较明显。 这些提升不是靠某个技巧换来的，而是来自一种和标准库不太一样的架构。要说清楚它，得先从线程说起。 从线程说起 传统的 C/C++ 服务端大多是单进程、少量线程的架构。线程很贵：栈要占内存，切换要进内核，开几百上千个就已经很吃力了。线程少，阻塞的代价就高，一个线程卡在一次慢查询上，它负责的所有请求都得跟着等。所以 C/C++ 的网络库基本都走同一条路：epoll/kqueue 做事件驱动，socket 设成非阻塞，业务逻辑拆成回调，耗时的事情丢给线程池。性能是有了，代价是代码被切成一段一段的回调，状态要自己保存，写起来和读起来都累。 C/C++ 和很多其他语言后来也有了协程，C++20 的 coroutine、各种第三方库、Rust 的 async/await 都是。但大多数情况下，协程的生命周期和调度仍然要自己操心：谁来 resume，在哪个线程上跑，帧和栈归谁管，跨过挂起点的引用还有没有效。跟 Erlang 的进程、Go 的协程比起来，这些方案理解和使用的门槛都高不少。 Go 的协程和它的边界 Go 在这一点上舒服得多。协程比进程、线程轻得多，几千到几万个协程照样跑得很顺。标准库的 net 其实也是事件驱动的：runtime 里的 netpoller 用 epoll/kqueue 等事件，事件来了再唤醒阻塞在 Read 上的协程。对用户来说接口是同步的，这也是 Go 做服务端这么流行的原因之一。 但标准库的用法比较单一。拿到一个 net.Conn，通常至少要有一个协程一直在 Read 它。1 万个连接就是 1 万个协程，100 万连接就是 100 万个协程，每个协程有自己的栈，再加上每个连接的 bufio.Reader、bufio.Writer。连接大部分时间是空闲的，这些内存却一直占着，GC 和调度器的压力也跟着上来。上面表格里 net/http 动辄几百 MB 的内存，主要就是这么来的。也有一些框架用 pre-fork 多进程的办法，把连接分散到多个进程里，减轻单个进程里 runtime 的压力，但这又带来了进程间协作、部署和监控上的麻烦。 fib 的做法：事件驱动 + 非阻塞接口 + 可配置的协程池 这些年我一直在做的是另一种方案。和 runtime 一样，用 epoll/kqueue/IOCP 做事件驱动，但不给每个连接配一个常驻的读协程。连接可读时，事件循环把它交给协程池里的一个 worker，worker 读数据、解析协议、调用户的 handler、把响应写回去，这一轮做完 worker 就回到池里。空闲的连接只是一个结构体，不占协程，也不占读写缓冲。前面表格里 fib 几十 MB 的内存，就是这么省下来的。 关键在协程池的大小。C/C++ 的线程池一般也就几十个线程，handler 里一阻塞，池子很快就耗尽，其他连接只能干等，所以只能全异步。Go 不一样，即使是限制了大小的协程池，也可以开到几千甚至几万个协程。这个并发度足够让用户在 handler 里继续用同步的方式调用下游的基础设施，比如 RPC、SQL，不用担心几个慢请求把池子占满，让其他连接等很久。 这样一来，连接数由事件驱动来承载，并发度由协程池来承载，业务代码还是同步的写法，连接数和协程数不再绑在一起。 fib 默认的池子上限是 GOMAXPROCS × 1000 个 worker，随负载伸缩，闲下来的 worker 会被回收，所以上限设得高并不浪费。如果你的 handler 基本不阻塞，可以调小；如果下游很慢，可以调大；也可以换成自己的池： go config := fib.DefaultConfig() config.SetPoolSizing(20000, 0) // worker 上限 // 或者 config.SetTaskPool(myPool) 从 nbio 到 fib：和 Claude 一起写 这个方案我不是第一次做。前几年我手写了 nbio，支持 TLS、HTTP/1.x 和 WebSocket，也有不少朋友在生产环境里用。但一个人的精力有限，HTTP/2、HTTP/3、QUIC 这些协议工作量太大，一直没能做。 这一两年 AI 模型进步得很快，于是有了 fib。这次是我和 Claude 合作，代码几乎全部由 Claude 生成。到目前为止，fib 支持： TCP、UDP、Unix socket，Linux 上用 epoll，macOS 上用 kqueue，Windows 上用 IOCP TLS 1.0–1.3，握手用 crypto/tls，握手之后的记录层加解密由 fib 自己做 HTTP/1.x、HTTP/2（h2 和 h2c）、HTTP/3，其中 QUIC 和 QPACK 是从头写的，不依赖 quic-go WebSocket，可以跑在 HTTP/1.1、HTTP/2 和 HTTP/3 上 异步的 HTTP/1、2、3 和 WebSocket 客户端，chi 风格的 Router，常用的中间件 用起来和标准库差不多 性能和架构说了这么多，用起来其实很简单。HTTP handler 用的是标准库的 http.Request 和 http.ResponseWriter，所以现有的 net/http handler、http.ServeMux、http.FileServer，甚至 chi、gin 的 engine，都可以直接跑在 fib 上： go mux := http.NewServeMux() mux.HandleFunc("GET /hello/{name}", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r http.Request) { fmt.Fprintf(w, "hello %s over %s\n", r.PathValue("name"), r.Proto) }) config := fib.DefaultConfig() config.Addr = "127.0.0.1:8080" engine, err := fib.Bind(config, fibhttp.NewHandler(fibhttp.HandlerFunc( func(c fibhttp.Context, r http.Request) { mux.ServeHTTP(c, r) }, ))) if err != nil { panic(err) } engine.Run() 同一个端口同时服务 HTTP/1.x 和 h2c；换成 TLS 就通过 ALPN 协商 HTTP/2；绑定一个 UDP engine 就是 HTTP/3，handler 不用改。 最后 代码主要由 Claude 生成，所以测试格外重要。项目做了大量的测试和 CI：HTTP/1 与 net/http、curl 的一致性测试，h2spec，和 quic-go 的 HTTP/3 互通测试，Autobahn WebSocket 测试，还有 fuzz。我自己的一些服务也已经跑在 fib 上，目前没发现什么问题。 更多内容请看 fib 的文档：README、架构、协议流程，以及 HTTP/1、HTTP/2、HTTP/3 的说明。 希望更多人能试试 fib，有问题、反馈或建议，欢迎提 issue 和 PR。 谢谢！

projects.author: WJZ0821
projects.summary: # [Vatrix 的 Github 仓库地址]( https://github.com/WJZ-P/Vatrix) ## 灵感来源 不久之前刷到过了之前 B 站守望先锋直播的加密方案，就是对直播流进行分块重排置换，接着在网页端上再反着做一遍，实现直播原本不让直播的守望先锋，于是借鉴这个思路，我开发了 Vatrix 。 ## 用法 作为一个独立的软件，它可以对视频做编码处理，并在编码完成的视频开头显示一秒的二维码，其中包含了解码所需的一些参数信息。 安装了配套的油猴插件后，会在视频刚播放的 0-1 秒检测当前视频画面中是否有二维码，有的话就尝试解析，并用解析出的参数对视频进行解码，下面上几张图 ![before|690x498, 100%]( https://xingyeai-images-cdn.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/talkie-user-img/448124399158206/448129631791480.png) ⬆️ 编码后的视频，支持编码时做反色处理，使得编码后的内容更难被肉眼识别 ![after|689x499]( https://xingyeai-images-cdn.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/talkie-user-img/448127625405341/448129733394565.png) ⬆️ 解码后的效果，能看到还是存在一些小方格，略有瑕疵，但不影响识别内容。顺带一提这里对原始音频做了个简单的频率倒置处理，可以去掉原始音频的语义性，人耳无法识别出处理后的音频表达什么内容。这个过程也是可逆的。 ![panel|384x477]( https://xingyeai-images-cdn.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/talkie-user-img/448127625405340/448129723369804.png) 浏览器插件面板。这里以 B 站未为例，入口在分享按钮的右边，默认是会自动解码的，不需要手动点启动。 ![app|690x452]( https://xingyeai-images-cdn.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/talkie-user-img/448125322396400/448129744275972.png) 用 AI 简单搓的一个软件 UI ，有点丑，但能用。 ## 后话 想看各位大佬会用它上传什么呢？ 有人用的话欢迎在评论区带上视频链接，也欢迎 star 和 issue ！

github.description: Agent tooling for generative LEGO models building, built with Astra and Opus 5.5, powered by Jev

projects.summary: Hi there :-) New on HN, first time posting. Past year, around December, I started experimenting with making ChatGPT and Claude generate source code in LDraw language. This LDraw is literally an "assembly" language, a low-level programming language that describes how to assemble LEGO pieces together into models, one placement instruction at a time. When executed by specific tools, like e.g. LDView, LeoCAD, Studio... these instructions become LEGO CAD models, that can be interacted with, modified, etc. Or, in other words: one LDraw source file in .mpd or .ldr format is equivalent to one LEGO CAD model. So, the idea I had was: if I manage for maybe ChatGPT or Claude to generate high-quality LDraw source files... then, they would actually be generating high-quality LEGO CAD models, right? Then, after months of iterations and trying one thing after the other... it worked!!! Long story short: using GPT-6 Astra and Opus 5.5, I've managed to create a python toolset, instructions, and docs for agents in general. Now, these can be used by them to generate LDraw models. I've packed it all as a dockerized web app for others to try and experiment, with several providers (and agents) to choose from: OpenAI, Claude and OpenRouter. Here's a bunch of exmaples: https://anteloc.github.io/index-samples.html . If you are curious about the internals of an .mpd model, the "what was the agent picturing on its mind", open the .mpd file that got your attention on a text editor, and read the first line under the ones starting with "0 FILE". I'd really appreciate feedback and comments, let's see where this goes =)

projects.title: 【工具自荐】NetWasm：C# 编译到 WASM，Hello World 只要 82.5 KiB
projects.author: zion-sati

github.name: zion-sati/NetWasm
github.description: NetWasm rebuilds .NET for WebAssembly - because cramming .NET Core into Wasm doesn’t make it a WASM platform.

projects.summary: NetWasm 是面向 WebAssembly 和 WASI 的独立 .NET 编译器和运行时。编译器前端用 Roslyn 把 C# 编译成 CIL，再由 NetWasm 把 CIL 编译成 Wasm。CoreLib 和运行时也是独立实现，最终产物不依赖 CoreCLR 或 Mono，也不带 dotnet.js 和独立应用 DLL。 想做的事很简单：保留 C# 的泛型、异常处理和自动内存管理，同时让程序只带上实际用到的部分。 体积实测 同样是 Console.WriteLine(42)，两种编译方案的结果如下： | 编译方案 | 未压缩 Wasm 体积 | | --- | ---: | | NetWasm | 82.5 KiB | | .NET 11 RC1 Blazor WebAssembly AOT | 14.58 MiB | 后者约为前者的 181 倍。NetWasm 的数字已经包含运行时和精确 GC；Blazor 这边用 Release 发布，开了完整裁剪、AOT 后 IL 剥离，以及面向体积的编译和链接优化。 这里比的是同一段输出逻辑在两种技术栈下的 Wasm 体积。NetWasm 输出的是 WASI 组件，Blazor 这边统计的是浏览器实际加载的原生 Wasm 和 Webcil 程序集；两边都不含 JavaScript、HTML 和 Wasm 宿主。 完整测试配置与复现说明 不止 Hello World 也做了一个可以直接用的应用：Regex Storm with NetWasm。 它用的是 .NET 自己的正则表达式引擎，编译成 Wasm 后在浏览器里提供匹配、捕获组查看、替换和分割，不是拿 JavaScript 正则模拟。Wasm 文件经 Brotli 压缩后约 325 KB，不含页面其他资源。正则和待处理文本都在本地处理，不上传后端，整个应用可以部署成静态网站。 另外还有 NetWasm Playground，可以直接编辑、编译、运行 C#。编译也在浏览器本地完成，不会把代码提交到服务器，不用先装工具链。 当前状态 项目还没到 1.0，兼容性仍在完善。采用闭世界编译，通用运行时反射是明确不支持的设计取舍，不是以后要补的功能。 许可方面，CoreLib、运行时库和模板等是 MIT 许可；编译器和开发工具用 NetWasm Community License，源码可看，但不是 MIT。 中文介绍：嫌 .NET Wasm 太大？我重写了编译器和运行时 欢迎拿实际用的 C# 代码来试，反馈兼容性问题。

projects.title: Show HN: Syn – Approve remote sudo requests from your Mac
projects.author: ferrerluis
projects.summary: I built Syn to review and approve individual sudo requests from a remote machine using Touch ID on my Mac. The problem came up about five minutes after I set up my Raspberry Pi with Ubuntu Desktop and Codex. I wanted an always-on personal agent with Browser Use, Computer Use, and a residential IP, accessible from both my phone and laptop (keep in mind, this was before Muse and Dots dropped). But a few prompts in, in order to run a command that needed `sudo`, the agent asked me to enter an administrator password in a terminal that–to me as a client on my Macbook–seemingly didn't exist. I then realized: "this dude has some password prompt open on its TTY, and I simply cannot see it." Unrestricted passwordless sudo would have removed that interruption, but I wanted to keep approving administrator actions myself, so setting up my Pi pivoted into building a Mac app. And so Syn was born: Syn hooks into sudo after its policy check. It pauses the invocation and shows the machine, account, executable, and arguments on the paired Mac, where I can approve it with fresh Touch ID or Mac-password authentication. Each approval is cryptographically signed and bound to that specific invocation. The unprivileged network service only relays signed requests and decisions; sudo executes its original command. The devices communicate directly over mutually authenticated TLS, without the need for a cloud relay. Interactive terminal use also has a password fallback, and Syn works with any eligible commands regardless of which agent—or person—started them. Current support is macOS 15+ on Apple silicon and Ubuntu 26.04 ARM64 with classic sudo.ws 1.9.x. I have mine set up between my Raspberry Pi and my Macbook with NordVPN Meshnet in the mix to ensure I can connect when outside my LAN, but it should work the same with any compatible VPS or using another virtual LAN (like Tailscale). If this fits your setup, I’d love folks to try it and share feedback! It's an open-source project, so PRs are super super welcome.

github.name: graphene-data/graphene
github.description: Turn your coding agent into a world-class data analyst

projects.summary: My friend and I have worked at a number of BI companies and thought: Can’t a coding agent do most of this now? Almost. They just need a context/semantic layer to ensure query correctness and some kind of artifact for publishing findings and visualizations. We built an open source project called Graphene that provides these tools: - Semantic layer that’s more token-efficient than YAML, more deterministic than Markdown (eg, composable, callable metric macros), with a query API that’s well in-distribution (SQL). - MDX-like files for dashboards (Markdown with inlined SQL + HTML components for viz with support for CSS and Javascript) - Connects to popular data warehouses or local DuckDB Your coding agent will build really in-depth reports and can ofc leverage any other skills or context that you've made available to it. We dogfood it inside a monorepo with our website, app source code, planning docs, etc so the agent has access to a ton of context. It’s also nice that the agent can add instrumentation, adjust pipelines and transformations, and add dashboards all in one PR. If you want to try it out, just point your coding agent at https://github.com/graphene-data/graphene/blob/main/docs/set... and ask it to set up Graphene. If you don’t have data to play with, you can clone our example project: 1. `git clone < https://github.com/graphene-data/example-flights.git` > 2. `cd example-flights && npm install` Would love any/all feedback!

projects.summary: Hi HN, I've been building SaaS products for more than 20 years, and lately I've been thinking a lot about how we interact with software. When we add a feature, we have to figure out where it goes in the UI and how users will interact with it. Then users have to learn our particular way of doing something. AI lets us flip that around: the software can translate what the user wants into the actions needed to accomplish it. Yedric lets devs add a natural-language interface to an existing SaaS app. You expose your app's actions and give it your docs and user context. Users can then ask for things like: • "Export the table to a CSV" • "Fix this disconnected integration" • "Change my logo color to #B5E2F4" We originally built Yedric for our own Shopify apps and discovered an interesting side effect: the conversations became a useful source of product feedback. One of our apps surfaced 80+ distinct feature requests this way last month. Yedric uses a small JS SDK and MCP to connect to your app's capabilities. It's free, you bring your own LLM key, and you can get a basic implementation running in under 30 minutes. Let me know how you like it!

projects.summary: Hi HN, I been using LLMs for coding a lot and while they aren't awful at generating code they suck at debugging and spend endless tokens on a debugging loop. Eventually that frustrated me and I built a CLI that attempts to make AI debugging easier. How it works is any error you encounter you would run a simple command "paper run <cmd>" which would "capture" that error and log it in a incident_report and tell your agents.md that is the source of truth for the error. When you ask your agent to fix the error the agent will look at your incident_report and solve it. Once your done you can shelf your report. Currently the constraints are it does not prompt a LLM or call external APIs(only writes a local .md file), everything stays local, no background daemon and no third party packages. Thanks for reading. The npm package page is posted below if anyone is interested. https://www.npmjs.com/package/@varman96/paper

In total in separated it into 4 rungs - easy, medium, hard and frontier. Two more layers compound the savings: the Sol-Pi methodology based on the recently published paper which uses action fusion and observation packing and cuts roken usage within every tier. Doctrine injection loads your engineering standards into every session by default, so the agent writes code the way your team would. There is also a real control plane - escalation, permission and verification hooks so the agent surfaces uncertainty instead of being confidently wrong in silence. Run it using your own key from Openrouter or Vercel AI gateway key, we need this since one key is able to call the jev decision model as well as the llms for coding. One more thing I added was the ability to connect your Meta Muse to use this for coding tasks which has worked really well so far you can try it out by copying the promp for agent on the website. Two ways you can use it today is the Mac app and the cli. Honest limitations are documented, happy to take any questions. Repo: https://github.com/grist-ai/grist npm CLI: npm install -g grist-ai

projects.summary: LR-Agent 是一个 Python 编程 Agent 实验项目，关注“当前测试通过的补丁，遇到后续维护变化会怎样”。它在隔离工作区生成候选补丁并执行验证，再让仓库连续经历依赖、接口或功能变化，每一代重放原始检查，输出补丁生存和维护成本报告。适合对编程 Agent、软件测试和维护实验感兴趣的开发者；完整运行需要配置兼容模型接口。 亮点 候选补丁在独立工作区中修改与验证，比较依据包含实际命令退出码。 连续维护实验中，后一代继承前一代的代码，便于观察累积变化造成的回归。 原有测试和长期约束会被重新执行，保留可检查的实验工作区和报告。 提供 CLI、Web 界面、最小示例以及研究边界说明，欢迎提交最小反例。 目前是研究型工程原型。合成场景和维护成本指标属于启发式实验，不能证明现实未来正确性，也没有据此声称领先其他 Agent。完整实验会调用模型，时间与费用随配置而变化。 项目自荐，希望收集安装体验、维护场景设计和报告解释方面的反馈。

projects.title: Show HN: The Kio Programming Language
projects.author: jdevuyst
projects.summary: Kio is a statically typed, hosted language that is designed to be ultra-portable. Kio 0.1 supports eight host languages and more will be added in the coming weeks. Kio is based on polymorphic lambda calculus with higher-kinded types. Kio has type-driven macros (elaborators) and it can statically check asserted equivalences using a normalizer. Kio is a minimalistic language. It doesn't have built-in effectful functions and it doesn't even have built-in string or numeric types. Instead programs declare the capabilities they need and the host supplies them. The language is designed with AI, which is bound to raise some eyebrows, so I blogged about that here: https://jdevuyst.github.io/kio/blog/2026-10-01-introducing-k...

projects.title: Show HN: tokentape.io – A Bloomberg-style market terminal for the token economy
projects.author: turingfeel
projects.summary: I wanted a way to track the token economy the way you'd follow equities or other financial markets: who's gaining market share, who's cutting prices, which new models are actually getting used. OpenRouter publishes a lot of the live data, but it's spread across various pages and endpoints, mostly as snapshots, so I started collecting and organizing it. The historical data was the hard part. OpenRouter doesn't publish an archive, so I rebuilt it from the Wayback Machine. I indexed about 2 million archived OpenRouter URLs, downloaded close to a million captures, and wrote parsers for every page and API format the site has used since 2023. Most of the work was in reconciling the disparate feeds of data, iteratively building up and infilling the dataset via derivation. Hopefully some people might find it useful.

projects.title: Show HN: Ciao – Control coding agents from your phone
projects.author: bojanstef
projects.summary: Hi HN, I built Ciao to solve problems I was experiencing: 1. Connecting to a new host should be as seamless as possible. I SSH a lot nowadays, and I find the key sharing across devices cumbersome. 2. I get annoyed by setting up insert-your-favorite VPN on new machines. They're all great. I don't want to think about them. 3. There's a lot of harnesses: Claude Code and Codex now have decent mobile push notifications but what about Pi or xyz-shiny-new harness? The harness is another tool that should be abstracted out. 4. I want a single application that has the big picture of all of my agents. Tmux and Herdr are great but they don't have an overview of all my connected machines' agents. --- With Ciao you curl|sh the daemon --> run ciao pair --> point your phone's camera at the QR code --> and you're connected. It uses iroh for accountless and E2EE connection. There's an optional relay server for APNS which too is E2EE. One of my favorite aspects of agentic-engineering is being able to just have a lot of fun with programming. Among many features, I built a visually pleasing toggle between terminal-mode and native-chat-mode. If you install Ciao, come back here and tell me what you think. --- Full transparency: this is a repost from yesterday, it was a massive day in AI.

projects.title: Show HN: Perspica – A semantic diff for reviewing code
projects.author: sshah03

github.name: sshah03/perspica
github.description: Review code changes by what they do, not line by line.

projects.summary: I started using this a little over half a year ago to help me navigate through some large AI coded PRs people were submitting, because I felt like if I looked at the PR on Github I would just auto pass it through because I didn't want to deal with it. Thought I'd clean it up and share it in case this style of review was useful to anyone else. Obviously it relies on an LLM run to get true semantic groupings of what changes were done, and why, but can also be used without an LLM to get more mechanical groupings/group names of changes made, along with the right order to view them in. The manual tree-sitter parsed analysis is deliberately conservative for now, but if people want to avoid the LLM analysis I can spend more time on that. You can use it for other peoples PRs, or for your own when you've relied heavily on Claude Code or Codex for that particular PR. If the change came from your own Claude Code or Codex session, it reads your prompts and marks which changes you asked for and which the agent decided on its own as well to help you validate it before submitting for others to review. Demo video done on some public project PRs is in the repo; for a look at what it looks like when it pulls in information about your own claude/codex sessions you'll have to use it yourself for now, but I'll work on getting an example of that up soon so people can take a look before spending time to get this to work locally for themselves. I also added support for perforce style side by side diffing because I always kind of liked it, though it's not quite as slick yet.

projects.summary: MSL Desktop：医学联络官的日常工作台 项目自荐。MSL（医学联络官）的日常工作会留下很多零散信息：拜访时专家的一句话、研究项目的新进展、等待回复的问题、下次交流要准备的资料。记录散开以后，后续跟进很容易丢掉背景。 MSL Desktop 把专家交流、临床与非临床项目、任务、等待事项、日历和资料放在一起。设计时坚持一句话：不要让记录工作变成比工作本身更耗费时间的事。 使用时可以先留下一句原话，让秘书结合已有项目准备整理建议；用户可以修改、暂缓或确认，确认后再写入正式事项。用户对方向的调整会纳入后续整理。AI 嵌在这些步骤中，日常工作仍由用户决定。 专家交流可以积累为带来源的洞察，后续拜访能够找回背景。 项目问答、简报和周月报依据工作台已有记录起草，使用前仍需核对。 工作数据与安装目录分开保存，支持本地备份及云盘文件夹同步，关联目录中的源文件只读。 新版微信入口中，普通文字直接记入收件箱；发送「召唤秘书」才打开五项菜单，可发起全局整理、生成每日简报、查看进度与待确认数量，或退出菜单。接收电脑需联网并运行工作台，建议仍在桌面端确认。 技术栈为 Tauri 2、Rust、Svelte 和 SQLite。当前提供 Windows x64 安装包，macOS 版本正在开发。 使用边界：远程模型需要配置自己的 API Key，相关记录和资料会发送给所选服务商，并产生该服务商的调用费用。请遵守所在机构的数据与合规要求；生成内容需人工核对，不用于自动作出临床决策。微信账号接入情况以微信服务返回为准。

projects.title: [FormulaAI] 更新：新增 VBA 代码生成 + 免登录使用
projects.author: clarecui
projects.summary: 接上次上线帖，FormulaAI 做了一次比较大的更新。 产品地址： https://formulaai.net —— 新增功能 1. VBA 代码生成 用自然语言描述需求，AI 生成可直接运行的 VBA 代码。 比如"给当前工作表加个按钮，点击后自动汇总所有部门的销售额"，返回的代码可以直接复制粘贴到 Excel 宏编辑器里运行。 实现思路：把用户需求 + 当前表格的列名/表头信息传给 DeepSeek ，prompt 里约束了 VBA 语法规范、必须加注释、变量声明等，输出质量还不错。 2. 免登录使用 之前必须登录才能用，现在匿名用户也能直接体验。上传文件、描述需求、AI 处理，全程不需要注册。只有保存历史记录、开通会员时才需要登录。 技术上就是把"必须登录"的中间件去掉，给匿名用户也分配了一个临时额度。 —— 为什么做这两个功能 上线后收集反馈，这两个需求出现频率最高： "能不能给我代码，我自己改" → VBA 生成 ​ "能不能不注册就用" → 免登录 本质上都是用户想要更多掌控感：一个掌控数据处理方式，一个掌控个人信息。 —— 目前完整功能列表 生成表格：描述需求 → AI 生成完整 Excel ​ 编辑表格：上传文件 → 描述需求 → AI 修改 → diff 对比 → 确认下载 ​ 生成 VBA：描述需求 → AI 生成 VBA 代码 ​ 免登录体验：打开即用 ​ 隐私保护：文件本地解析，不上传服务器，处理完即删 技术栈：Next.js + DeepSeek API + SheetJS + Supabase + Cloudflare Pages + 虎皮椒（微信支付） —— 数据情况 上线到现在，免登录这个改动对新用户转化率提升比较明显，具体数字等再观察一段时间。 VBA 生成功能用的人还不多，可能是因为会用 VBA 的用户本身就少，但用过的反馈都还不错。 —— 接下来的计划 继续看反馈决定优先级，目前在考虑的方向： 支持更多文件格式（ CSV 、Google Sheets ） ​ 批量处理多个文件 ​ 导出处理历史记录 有什么建议欢迎评论区交流。

projects.summary: Switched to Fedora a year ago. And because I needed to transcribe interviews offline from time to time, I was looking for something like MacWhisper for Linux. projects.title: Show HN: Hypercolor – Epic RGB lighting control for everything
projects.author: hyperb1iss
projects.summary: Light it up with Hypercolor , a new RGB lighting orchestration platform for all platforms and all devices. Effects are web pages (or glsl), rendered by an internal browser GPU accelerated all the way to the pixels. It's pure rust from the Servo renderer to the WASM UI. Comes with 40+ effects, supports ambilight, display faces, system monitoring, screen casting, and audio. Device support is pretty good but it's early and this is where we need the most help! You can find the full support matrix on the site, and there is also an OpenRGB bridge as a fallback. There's support for a few unique devices too like the Ableton Push 2 and ROLI Blocks. My favorite thing about this engine is the ability to create multiple effect zones and manage them independently! My whole house runs on it now. It's Apache licensed, and a cloud service is coming with remote and smart home support. A Home Assistant integration is already available. The best way to set up Hypercolor is to just have an agent do it for you using the bundled skill. Just describe your setup, case type, hardware, etc, and it will find all the specs and configure it for you. Or just do it the good old-fashioned way in Studio! Please check it out and file and issue if you're looking for device support. I can only build drivers for devices I have access too, please open PRs if you're able to contribute! Agents can reverse engineer your hardware and build a driver easily, if you want to go that route (the repo is designed for agents). We have a full TypeScript effects SDK for easy effect creation too, and support existing Lightscript based html effects out of the box. I've had a lot of fun building this and I hope you enjoy it!

projects.title: AI Agent 的能力上限由模型决定，行为的可靠性与一致性由规则体系决定。
projects.author: tntin
projects.summary: 在使用 AI Agent 开发项目的过程中，我的一些理解 以及 推荐一下我开发的工具： ## 一句话总结版 模型决定能力上限，规则决定底线与一致性； Agent 规则文档是给智能体用的长期执行手册，拒绝直接抄模板，聚焦你反复遇到的问题，写死动作与验收标准，约束长任务每一步的判断。 ## 正文 | 维度 | 模型层 | 规则层 | |---|---|---| | **决定因素** | 理解、推理、创作、工具调用的能力边界 | 目标拆解、工具白名单、权限审批、可验证性 | | **典型约束** | 成本与速度（复杂任务需大模型，简单判断用小模型） | 把“必须”“禁止”变成程序必经节点，而非仅靠模型复述 | | **失败模式** | “能做但太贵太慢” | “写了却跳过”“自由发挥导致乱写” | 模型负责“能做什么”，规则负责“按什么流程做、做到什么程度算完成”。两者缺一不可：没有模型，Agent 没有能力；没有规则，Agent 没有纪律。 ### 一：能力上限 模型的能力边界直接决定了 Agent 能完成的任务类型。但关键在于，**不是所有任务都需要调用最大最强的模型**——复杂规划用大模型，简单判断用小模型，这既是成本控制，也是速度优化的必然选择。 ### 二：规则的本质 “规则决定会不会乱写” 规则层的核心机制包括： - **目标与边界**：通过任务拆解、工具白名单、权限审批点，将模型的“自由发挥”约束为“按流程执行”；； - **避免“写了却跳过”** ：把“必须”“禁止”等约束变成程序必经节点，而非仅靠模型在提示词中复述——这是规则从“建议”升级为“强制”的关键。 ### 三：Agent 规则文档是长期执行手册 Agent 规则文档的定位是**权重极高的长期持久提示词**，接近系统提示词，在长任务的每一步持续约束 Agent 的判断，一般用 Markdown 编写。这与“临时 prompt”有本质区别：临时 prompt 解决单次交互，规则文档解决**跨任务、跨会话的一致性**。 系统提示词是 Agent 的“核心规则基石”，负责定义模型的角色定位、应答规范与能力边界，为全程对话定下基础框架。规则文档正是这一理念的具体载体。 ### 四：好规则写动作与验收，坏规则写价值观 这是最具操作性的判断： - **坏规则**：写抽象形容词（“回答要有审美”“方案要高级”），无法让 Agent 落地判断； - **好规则**：从日常反复踩坑的真实工作问题出发，写清楚**遇到这类问题时下一步要执行什么动作，以及怎么验收结果**。 一个完整的 Agent 规范应定义角色、场景、输入、输出、可做/不可做、工具边界、人工确认、失败处理、验收标准，把可观察的 Agent 行为验收清楚。可落地、可校验，才是好规则的检验标准。 ### 五：知识库工具 [knloop]( https://knloop.com) 是一个 Agent 原生知识库，让你的规则成为 Agent 的长期执行手册——你定义动作与验收标准，Agent 在每一步对照执行，全程可审计、可回滚。 [knloop]( https://knloop.com) 让你把规范、SOP 、QA 、复盘写成持久化的 .md 文档，Agent 通过 MCP 读取，按你的规范执行，产出写回同一个库。

projects.title: Show HN: SFML – A markup language for software factories, Terraform for agents
projects.author: mcwhittemore
projects.summary: SFML is a language specification for defining software factories. You can think of it as Terraform for your software development lifecycle. I started from a language spec to help think through both how a factory is defined and how a conforming runner processes it. The push to do this comes from leading teams where everyone has a unique coding setup, which results in different agentic coding processes. People also want to work together on improving that process. Right now they do it through shared AGENTS.md files and, in some cases, committed Claude and Codex settings files. But it hasn't led to the collaboration we all want. SFML is my attempt to help make that happen. My core bet is that the Unix philosophy applies to agentic coding just like it applies to all other coding: small steps with clear inputs and outputs, composed together to get results. Most agentic setups lean on ever-growing AGENTS.md files that quickly become unwieldy. Breaking them up helps, but then the agent has to rediscover and reassemble your process on every run. I'm pretty early in thinking about what SFML should be, and I'm hoping to hear from dissenters and collaborators here today, to push me to think more critically and to show me directions I haven't imagined yet. Thanks in advance for your feedback.

projects.title: Show HN: Relay – a harness for AI coding agents that recover and verify
projects.author: rsathwik07
projects.summary: I'm tired of AI coding agents which are good for 30 seconds and then completely fail on the slightest hiccup: a failing test, a temporarily unavailable dependency, an incorrect assumption. Sometimes I end up having to babysit these agents anyway. Relay is a harness for coding agents which takes advantage of the fact that agents are often good at doing something slightly wrong, and not so good at doing something correctly and completely. Relay repeatedly tries the task and on each failure, uses the output to find a better way to do it. It does this by running the task in a loop: attempt the task, run the checks in a fresh sandbox, on failure read the error and retry instead, until the checks pass. What it learned from a run is retained, so that it doesn't repeat the same mistake, and when the checks eventually pass, it will ship the change as a normal git PR - no hidden state, no magic, the diff is human readable. A few specifics: - it runs locally, is free, and doesn't require an account to run the local agent - it uses a top-tier model to plan/review, and cheaper models to actually write code (for cost reasons) - happy to discuss why this is a good idea and why it isn't - the checks run in an isolated sandbox for each task, rather than "trusting" the agent - currently supports [list actual models/integrations - Opus 5.5, GPT-6, etc] - there's a paid tier for running this unattended across multiple repos with shared sandbox minutes, the actual agent is free. It's not magic, it's not AGI, and it will fail badly on some problems. Would appreciate feedback, particularly from people who've deployed agents unattended and found that they don't actually work, or have had to build substantial tooling around them to get useful results.

projects.title: Show HN: Aether: Check and fix web accessibility issues from your coding agent
projects.author: samy_patra
projects.summary: Hi, HackerNews! I'm Samy, co-founder of Allchemy Labs. We built Aether, an MCP server that enables engineers to check for, understand, and fix web accessibility issues all from their IDE. Your preferred coding agent can leverage Aether to open a webpage, scan it using axe-core and return a short, prioritized list of violations along with code fixes or guidance. Every suggested fix is re-tested in a real browser before you see it, and once you apply it, your agent can re-scan the page to verify it worked. You never need to open a browser, use multiple tools, or be an expert in WCAG criteria. Aether uses our own custom ontology architecture to provide grounded insights to any WCAG violations the scanner finds. Every WCAG technique the engine cites must pass our quality gate. Specifically, it must satisfy the violated success criterion, apply to that kind of element, and remediate that axe rule. If nothing passes, our engine will abstain rather than guess. We compared Aether against standalone coding agent on its own (Opus 5, 30 anonymized live sites, 111 targets). While the results were mixed we have published the results especially calling out specific wins and improvement opportunities for our insight engine. Read the study here: https://allchemylabs.substack.com/p/we-tested-our-own-access... Try Aether today, no signup needed. npx -y @allchemylabs/aether-wcag-scanner (any MCP client: Claude Code, Cursor, Codex…) Claude Code plugin: /plugin marketplace add https://github.com/allchemylabs/claude-plugins.git then /plugin install aether-wcag-scanner@allchemylabs Without a key you get the browser scan, local template fixes and verification. A free beta key adds the cloud engine: https://beta.allchemylabs.ai/?src=hn Feedback from people who have used accessibility scanners and/or suggestion engines would be highly valuable to us, as we aim to build a tool that solves real problems and makes people's lives easier. Happy to answer any questions and hope to hear from you. Note: Right now Aether only checks WCAG 2.1 AA. Sites behind bot protection (e.g. Cloudflare challenges) return a "blocked" result instead of a fake scan, so point it at localhost or staging.

projects.title: Show HN: Acceptodds a prediction market on which ICLR 2027 papers get accepted
projects.author: armstrongb
projects.summary: Hi, I built acceptodds, a prediction market on conference peer review. Every ICLR 2027 submission (42k papers) has a market: Accept vs. Reject. Like many in the ML community, I think the current conference/paper situation is a bit broken. I'm not sure how to fix it, but this is my attempt at building something fun to get the conversation started. Some details: - Prices come from Hanson's LMSR (logarithmic market scoring rule). - You can sell and/or rebuy at any time - There's a public leaderboard that ranks traders by P&L. - It uses an in-app currency called reputation. It can't be converted to money. - Bots can trade too, and they're encouraged. If you can get an LLM to predict the market, that would be cool! There's a public HTTP API with an OpenAPI spec (/api/v1/openapi.json). - Comments are pseudonymous, like on OpenReview ("User k3xm"), but they show the author's position. - There's also a 2D map of all submissions: https://acceptodds.com/map How would you extend this? How should ML conference reviews work? Is there something better than open review? Go find your own paper (if you have one), place a bet and LMK what you think :)

projects.title: Show HN: Meanwhile Map – what else was happening in the world at the same time
projects.author: 29b
projects.summary: When reading a history book, I sometimes have a hard time internalizing when the events are taking place. Sure, I know the dates, but it takes a bit of effort to put them in a broader context, to understand where in history they belong. What usually helps is to put them in relation to other contemporaneous events. To play around with this, I've made Meanwhile Map. You select a date and a time window, then scroll around the world map to see a list of contemporaneous events. For example, yes, the Mughal Empire was founded by Babur in the 1520s, but it paints a different picture in my head when I see that this roughly coincides with Cortés' capture of Tenochtitlan, or that it's close to the Siege of Vienna. Example link: https://meanwhilemap.com/#y=1520&m=1&span=120&off=founded,pe... On the technical side, the app is a single static web page. It uses Wikidata for data (via SPARQL) and OpenHistoricalMap to show the events on the political map of the time. It's open source ( https://github.com/ea/meanwhilemap/tree/main ), vibe coded as an experiment. All processing is client-side, and no data is tracked other than simple visitor counts.

projects.title: Show HN: Orrery, a Three.js solar system visualization powered by real NAIF data
projects.author: rybosome
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm excited to share a personal project that I've put a lot of love into. This is Orrery[0], a Three.js-based visualization of our solar system. It allows the positions of the major bodies to be played and scrubbed through the years 1950 - 2050, with optional orbit path displays and various other visualization options. The data comes from NAIF SPICE - a framework and set of open-source data kernels containing highly detailed space geometry data. I was inspired to set out on this project when learning that NAIF SPICE, originally written in Fortran and C, lacks highly standardized JavaScript bindings. There are great Python (SpiceyPy) and Rust (Anise) bindings, among other languages, but nothing for JavaScript. So, I developed tspice[1] to wrap the CSPICE library. It uses the Native API when running in Node, and an Emscripten binding around CSPICE when running in the browser. It uses a standardized backend abstraction that the runtime swaps in depending on which context its invoked with. tspice offers an API that is meant to be a near-literal translation of the C APIs, along with higher-level functionality in separate namespaces. It also offers web conveniences like a dedicated web worker client (calculations can be intensive, you don't want them on your render thread) and caching. tspice only wraps a subset of the CSPICE library, but it was enough that I wanted to build a simple visualization tool to test it. Eventually the visualization testbed became refined enough that it felt compelling on its own. Although this is a hobby project, I'd love to hear suggestions and feedback on either Orrery or the underlying tspice library. If there are any folks in the planetary science community in particular who might be interested in tspice, please let me know if there are features that would make this more useful for you. One feature I love is the ability to generate a share URL of a particular viewer state that you like. I'd really love to see any states that people find especially cool! One of my favorite views is this one[2]. Thanks for taking a look! [0] Orrery repo: https://github.com/rybosome/orrery [1] tspice repo: https://github.com/rybosome/tspice [2] favorite orrery view: https://orrery.ryboso.me/dVPLbtswEPwX9qoIol4UdWtaB22RNEbsoii...

projects.summary: 这是 LocHub 作者的自荐，文字由 AI 辅助整理。 LocHub 是一个 Unreal Engine 5.6–5.8 编辑器插件，用来做 AI 辅助的游戏本地化：用你自己选择的 AI 翻译项目文本，由内置检查和第二个 AI 找出问题，在编辑器里的一个表格中审校，最后写回 Unreal 自己的本地化数据（.archive、编译后的 .locres）。它不替代 Unreal 的本地化系统，随时可以停用。 从 1.2.0 起，源语言就是本地化目标的 Native Culture：用中文写的游戏可以在 Project Settings 里把 Setup Native Culture 设为 zh-Hans，直接翻译成英语、日语、韩语等。 能做什么 自带密钥接入 Claude、OpenAI、Gemini、DeepSeek、Grok，或任何 OpenAI 兼容接口（Ollama、LM Studio、vLLM 等）。使用本地模型时，文本不离开你的电脑。 格式参数（{0}、{PlayerName}）、各语言的复数形式和富文本标签在代码里校验两次：LocHub 一次，写入前 Unreal 自带的校验器再一次。有错的译文无法通过审校，手动也不行。 可选的第二个 AI 担任评审，检查含义、术语和语气，按严重程度标注问题并给出修改建议。 每条文本带上下文翻译：来源资产或 C++ 文件、开发者备注、同一界面已翻译的文本、项目简介和风格指南。 术语表与禁止翻译词、UI 长度检查、导出 XLIFF / CSV 给人工译者。 运行前估算费用，并可设置花费上限（Max USD）。人工修改永远不会被 AI 覆盖。 使用边界 源码公开，采用 Business Source License 1.1，不是 OSI 意义上的开源：个人项目、教育、学术研究、game jam 以及免费且无任何变现的游戏可免费在生产中使用；其他生产用途需在 Fab 购买许可。每个版本发布四年后转为 Apache 2.0。 在 Windows 上测试过；需要 Node.js 22.11 或更高版本。

projects.summary: 自荐一个刚开源的论文阅读器 PaperFold。我是作者 Xia Chen，目前在 TUM 做人机对齐方向的博士后研究。 读论文时，经常需要来回确认一段话在整篇论证中的位置。我做了一个可以逐层折叠、展开的阅读界面：先把论文缩成章节地图，再展开关心的部分，直到看到每个原文段落。 项目及缩放演示： 免安装体验： 阅读器有五档：全文、逐字摘取的关键句、要点及理由、一句话提要、章节主题地图。前两档使用作者原文，后三档由模型生成，以不同字体区分。缩放时，保留下来的词会移动到新位置；也可以只展开一个段落，其余部分继续折叠。提问后的回答会链接到所引用的段落。 Python 后端解析 arXiv 的 HTML，浏览器前端负责阅读和缩放；代码采用 Apache-2.0 许可。生成新论文需要该论文有 arXiv HTML 版本，并连接一个模型。生成后的论文可导出成独立 HTML 文件。 体验页提供数学、机器学习、医学等八个领域的论文，均标注了作者及 Creative Commons 许可，无需注册或配置模型即可体验阅读。AI 生成的提要仍可能出错，可以随时展开原文核对。 目前是早期版本，欢迎反馈解析失败的论文，以及长文阅读时的缩放、定位问题。

projects.summary: 每天一杯瑞幸，取餐时总会瞄一眼杯贴上的号码。某天意识到这其实是个每天免费开一次的数字盲盒：可能是 888 ，可能是顺子，可能正好是生日。但喝完杯子一扔，号码就没了。 所以给自己做了个收集册，叫「杯号」：000–999 一千个格子，每喝一杯，拍一下杯贴，点亮一格。 ![]( https://beihao.app/promo/recruit-2026-10/01-photo-to-sticker.jpg) 拍完几秒：认出品牌和取餐号，把号码贴纸从照片里"撕"下来、拉正、包白边，整杯也从背景里抠出来。每一格都必须用真实照片点亮，不能手填。 ![]( https://beihao.app/promo/recruit-2026-10/02-number-book.jpg) ## 想找什么样的人 瑞幸、星巴克是我自己天天喝的，已经比较稳。品牌表里还收了 50 多家，但每家杯贴长得五花八门，我手里样张很少，**尤其想找常喝 Manner 、M Stand 、Peet's 、喜茶、奈雪的朋友**。 你只需要：平时喝东西时顺手拍一下杯贴。认错了、卡住了、哪里难用，直接在帖子里回复就行。 ## 怎么加入 iPhone 上直接打开 TestFlight 公开链接（会先引导装苹果官方的 TestFlight ）： https://testflight.apple.com/join/pGpDNz5K 不想直接装的话，也可以先在 https://beihao.app/beta/ 填 4 道题（ 1 分钟），填完同样给链接，顺便帮我统计一下大家常喝什么。

projects.summary: 这是一个MIT许可的长文听稿工具箱，帮助把读书笔记、知识长文和AI草稿整理为适合听的文字。浏览器工具可生成请求、标出网址及表格等格式问题，并将正文与来源分别导出TXT；处理不上传文稿。另有纯文字Agent技能、三种中文起步请求，以及统计与历史两份完整听稿和AI音频。工具本身不调用AI、不合成语音，适合想先把材料讲清楚，再选择朗读工具的读者。 亮点 不把“适合听”简单理解成删表格或压缩摘要：改写示例保留数字、单位、来源归属和不确定性，原文格式只提示，不替用户删除。 在线使用或解压后直接打开HTML，不用注册、密钥或安装依赖。复制不可用时可手动复制或导出TXT；关闭页面不会保留输入。 两份中文完整示范可以直接听，也能查看原稿及来源。统计示范用原创虚构数据解释平均数与中位数；历史示范讲火车与时间制度。音频约8分17秒、8分05秒，由Mac上的本地模型生成，非iPhone录音，不承诺学习效果或手机性能。 纯文字听稿技能不执行脚本、不访问账号，也不在生成稿里加入产品广告；不用技能也能复制中文请求。AI内容仍需对照可靠材料核验。

projects.title: 开源 Bibo：成本极低，内置笔记、文件、任务和日历的 personal agent
projects.author: Peiiii
projects.summary: 我把 Bibo 开源了，MIT 协议。先说最想做好的三件事： 1. **成本极低。** 日常使用不需要常驻电脑，也不用一直开着 Linux 容器。只有需要运行代码时，才启动沙箱。 2. **内置个人管理工具。** 笔记、文件、任务和日历都有专门的界面。你可以直接查看、编辑和管理，也可以让 AI 来做。 3. **开源，可以自己部署。** 用自己的 Cloudflare 账号和模型 API Key ，数据存在自己的部署里，代码也可以自己改。 GitHub：[Peiiii/bibo]( https://github.com/Peiiii/bibo) 在线体验：[app.bibo.bot]( https://app.bibo.bot) 我希望它能成为每天都用得上的 personal agent 。想到什么可以随手记，需要做的事可以放进任务和日历，资料可以整理成文件；这些内容长期留着，之后还能接着用。 下面把界面都放出来。截图来自实际运行的 Bibo ，销售、订单和日程内容都是示例数据。 ### 概览 打开就能看到笔记、任务、日程和待处理信息。 ![Bibo 概览]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/v2ex-2026-10-04/bibo-overview.jpg) ### 对话 让 Bibo 阅读销售数据、总结重点，也可以让它继续整理报告和安排后续工作。 ![Bibo 对话与报告]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/v2ex-2026-10-04/bibo-chat.jpg) ### 笔记 笔记是可以直接编辑的 Markdown 文档。你自己写，或者让 Bibo 帮你整理，都能继续修改。 ![Bibo 笔记]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/v2ex-2026-10-04/bibo-notes.jpg) ### 文件 有独立的文件目录，可以打开、编辑文件。这里展示的是整理好的订单 CSV 。 ![Bibo 文件]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/v2ex-2026-10-04/bibo-files.jpg) ### 任务 任务有独立列表和详情，可以管理完成状态、优先级、描述和时间。分析出来的建议，可以接着变成待办。 ![Bibo 任务]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/v2ex-2026-10-04/bibo-tasks.jpg) ### 日历 日程直接显示在日历里，可以自己添加，也可以让 Bibo 帮你安排。 ![Bibo 日历]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/v2ex-2026-10-04/bibo-calendar.jpg) ### 收件箱 需要你关注和确认的内容放在这里，可以查看并标记处理。 ![Bibo 收件箱]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/v2ex-2026-10-04/bibo-inbox.jpg) ### 需要运行代码时，按需启动 Linux 沙箱 例如，用 Python 清洗订单表，去掉重复行，生成新的 CSV 和说明文档。下面这次演示实际运行了 Python ，文件已保存。 普通对话和个人管理功能由 Cloudflare Workers / Durable Objects 承载，文件保存在 R2 。需要运行 Python 、Shell 等代码时，才用 Cloudflare Sandbox ，不必为了日常使用维持一台常驻电脑。 ![Bibo 运行 Python 整理订单]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/bibo-sandbox-execution.png) ### 手机端 手机上也能继续对话、查看和管理任务。 ![Bibo 手机对话]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/bibo-mobile-chat.png) ![Bibo 手机任务]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/bibo-mobile-tasks.png) 自己部署需要 Cloudflare Workers Paid 、R2 、Sandbox 和模型 API Key ，具体步骤在仓库 README 。实际费用由模型调用、存储和沙箱使用量决定。 欢迎试用，也欢迎提 Issue 或 PR 。想听听大家：你最希望 personal agent 帮你处理哪件日常小事？

projects.title: [我的搜索-桌面版] 一款呼出搜索工具，支持网站/文本类/插件
projects.author: zhuangjie
projects.summary: ## 使用场景 项目开发最开始解决的问题是收藏了很多网站/软件/一些小教程(后面可能用到)，通过按规则写好源放到 github 上得到订阅然软件负责递归解析出数据项来搜索，有内置订阅，可制作自己订阅（[教程]( https://github.com/My-Search/my-search) | [官方源仓库-参考]( https://github.com/My-Search/official-subscribe)），桌面版有**插件功能** ![image]( https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/18476305640/typora@master/uploads/2026/10/03/1791035519022.png) ## 使用 **桌面版（订阅数据+插件）：基于 Rust 开发 [my-search-desktop]( https://github.com/My-Search/my-search-desktop)** 原版（订阅数据）：油猴脚本应用 [mysearch]( https://greasyfork.org/zh-CN/scripts/457020-%E6%88%91%E7%9A%84%E6%90%9C%E7%B4%A2) ## 当前有哪些可用的插件 | 插件名 | 描述 | |---|---| | Pi Agent | Pi 编码代理 - 支持多项目、多模型、模型配置面板、插件管理、流式对话与工具调用 | | 文件搜索 | 在粘贴/拖入的文件夹里按名称搜索文件：一直扫描、边扫边显示，随时可停止；回车或点击用系统默认程序打开 | | 插件市场 | 浏览、安装、更新与卸载插件 | | 录屏与水印 | 屏幕录制（可选实时叠加水印），并给已有视频批量添加文字/图片水印，支持九宫格定位与水印预设 | | 截图 | 全局快捷键截图：框选区域、标注后复制到剪贴板，并在前台查看最近 7 天的截图 | | MayeLite 快速启动 | 把常用文件/文件夹拖进来固定，随时一键打开；支持分类、排序与拖拽整理 | | 百度翻译 | 使用百度翻译 AI 能力，支持 200+ 语言互译，输入文本即译 | | GitHub 文件上传 | 将文件上传到 GitHub 仓库，支持拖拽、粘贴、选择文件与图片压缩 | | 剪贴板历史 | 自动记录你复制过的文本与图片，按快捷键呼出即可搜索、复制、删除、收藏。收藏的条目永久保留、不会被上限淘汰或清空。监听在后台原生完成，不干扰系统剪贴板。 | | 待办清单 | 本地待办清单：增删改查、优先级、标签、截止日期、筛选统计与 JSON 导出导入 | | 资源监控 | 每 5 秒采样整机 CPU / 内存 / 网络，按程序聚合，用可缩放时间范围的趋势图展示占用最高的 Top 10——快速定位 CPU 莫名 100%、内存暴涨、异常上传的程序 | 插件支持调整窗口大小，关闭自动恢复再打开时仍会按之前调试的宽度显示。 ## 如何开发新插件 AI 开发提示词： ``` 软件主体： https://github.com/My-Search/my-search-desktop 插件市场： https://github.com/My-Search/my-search-plugin-market 参考下面仓库开发出 my-search-desktop 插件。 需要开发插件的功能：xxx ``` 开发的插件通过设置里的挂载安装即可进行调试，当前开放的接口可能不多，需要可提 issues; 开发的插件可声明是否跟随软件启动，使用后退出是否后台运行，可声明在主体软件上快捷键使即使插件停止仍可通过快捷键激活插件功能； 插件市场运作说明： 插件都是在[插件市场 github 仓库]( https://github.com/My-Search/my-search-plugin-market)里定时自动索引的,按规范开发好，将仓库通过插件市场仓库提 issues 我看到会放到 index.json 会自动索引； ## 关于环境变量 用于多插件配置复用：通过直接在软件写好环境变量配置，在插件中直接通过环境变量授权给插件使用

projects.title: 【资源自荐】把 AI 长文整理成中文听稿：开源工具箱与完整学习案例
projects.author: GODGOD126
projects.summary: 自荐一个中文长文转听稿的开源资源：长文节目工具箱，源码和中文说明。 适合手里已有 AI 长文、研究资料或学习笔记，希望整理后用文字转语音工具收听的人。可以在浏览器内生成听稿提示词、标出网址/表格/长段落等需要人工检查的位置，将朗读正文和来源备注分别导出 TXT。不用注册或密钥，不上传输入；也可以下载整个工具箱离线打开。 它不调用 AI、不生成语音，不自动核查事实，也不擅自删除原文。网址、数字、比较条件和不确定性可能就是资料的重要信息，不能为了“适合听”直接丢掉。另有一份纯文字的 listening-script Agent 技能，用于保留这些边界的改写。 完整中文案例：平均数与中位数，包含原创朗读稿、可复制提示词和来源/数值核查说明。例子为虚构教学数据。2026-10-04补充了一份8分17秒完整中文AI合成音频，附实际生成稿与计算核查；在Mac端生成，非iPhone录音或真机性能演示，没有学习效果测量。工具箱本身仍不生成语音。正文和示范可独立使用，不要求购买任何App。 我是作者 Ryan Zhu，也是「自听」MyListen 开发者。工具箱代码、原创示例和提示词以 MIT 许可开放，由 AI 辅助编写；免费资源与 App 的商业条款分别适用。这次只自荐这份可独立使用的中文资源，供周刊编辑判断。

projects.title: Show HN: AstroHelm – Use your phone camera to aim a telescope or telephoto lens
projects.author: HeavenFox
projects.summary: Hello HN! As an amateur astronomer living in New York City, finding objects in the night sky has always been a huge challenge. I thought about using the smartphone's gyroscope and magnetometer, but the accuracy left a lot to be desired. Then I learned about plate solving: given a picture of the sky, we can determine exactly where in the sky the camera was pointing by identifying the star pattern. This was a much better fit - as long as the phone and the optics are rigidly connected, we can repeatedly photograph the sky and determine the pointing direction with very high accuracy. A lot of work was done to design an algorithm that works reliably with smartphone cameras, which have limited light sensitivity and wider field of view which includes buildings and trees. I experimented a lot with machine learning, and to my surprise, traditional CV methods actually performed better at extracting stars from the image. The result is AstroHelm, an iOS and Android app that helps figure out where your telescope or camera is pointing, and guides you to the object of your choice. Just follow an arrow on screen, and the object will land right in your eyepiece or viewfinder. Everything happens on device, and no internet connection is required. AstroHelm is free to use and comes with beginner-friendly objects selected for each night. Optional one time purchases unlock more objects and advanced features, such as interoperability with other astronomy software. I am also proud to partner with astronomy clubs and organizations to offer free licenses for outreach. I hope AstroHelm can make it a little easier to discover the wonders of the night sky, and I look forward to your feedback!

projects.title: 做了一组能在浏览器里直接玩的天文交互演示：从野餐垫上的 1 米放大到可观测宇宙
projects.author: my6666
projects.summary: 在做一个科普交互演示的网站「格物间」，最近整理出一个「宇宙与天文」专题，10 个演示，打开浏览器就能玩，看不用登录： https://gewujian.cn/topics/pMaEDfRrATvyqRT6FFfvWQ ![专题脑图]( https://gewujian.cn/v1/media/upXrlRF3S_LWkFEm8a37cQ.png) 几个我自己比较喜欢的： **宇宙的尺度**：一个小朋友躺在公园野餐垫上，方框从 1 米开始，每按一次放大 10 倍，27 步走到可观测宇宙的边（直径约 925 亿光年）。中间会经过城市卫星照片、此刻真实位置的行星、旅行者 1 号、真实恒星和星系的分布。 ![宇宙的尺度]( https://gewujian.cn/v1/media/ey7zePa82K7totsKODqKUg.png) **光速与光年**：太阳和日地距离按真实比例画，阳光按真实速度跑，可以真的等 8 分 17 秒看它到地球；也可以假设「太阳突然不亮了」，看地球上多久才发现。 ![阳光到地球]( https://gewujian.cn/v1/media/lzwuHMpZQDjlGfu5QF-pug.png) **引力与时空弯曲**：橡皮膜、三维网格、「时间也弯了」三种画法；中间可以换成中子星、黑洞；「射出星光」能看到 1919 年日全食测到的星光偏折，左下角是按当年星表画的毕星团。 ![1919 年星光偏折]( https://gewujian.cn/v1/media/L52ZSZMZrYtbrjRYzq6f4A.png) 其他还有：恒星的核聚变和一生、韦布望远镜怎么折叠发射和展开（轨道用的是 NASA JPL 的真实数据）、月相（按此刻真实位置，可以换城市看）、日食和月食、地球自转、太阳系、太阳的银河之旅。 一些做法： - 能用真实数据的都用真实数据：月亮、行星、旅行者号是此刻的真实位置，韦布的轨道来自 JPL Horizons ，1919 年那次日食用的是当年观测报告里的星表。 - 每个演示里的数字和说法都逐条联网核对过，有出处的写在每个演示右侧面板最后的「资料来源」里。核对时也改掉了一些常见的错误说法，比如「红移 1 的蓝光变成红光」（其实已经是近红外了）。 - 都支持中英文切换，切换时演示的状态不会重置。 - 电脑和平板体验最好，手机能看但不如大屏。

projects.title: 【工具自荐】LinkDigest：把抖音、小红书链接变成 AI 能读的文本，还能做「爆款拆解」
projects.author: jcaiagent7143-ui
projects.summary: 把小红书或抖音链接直接丢给 Claude、ChatGPT，它们基本读不到：小红书图文笔记的正文在图片里，抖音的内容在口播里，分享页本身只是一个“打开 App”的壳。 LinkDigest 是给 AI agent 用的 API / MCP 服务：一次调用，把小红书、抖音、TikTok、YouTube、X 的链接变成文本——带时间戳的逐字稿、画面上的文字（带出现时间）、每张图的描述和 OCR、要点。由服务器端去读，不需要你的 cookie，也不用你的账号，没有封号风险。 实测同一条小红书链接：直接抓取只拿到 860 个字符的可见文本，LinkDigest 返回 35,059 个字符。 新加了「爆款拆解」（breakdown: true，+1 积分）：钩子（开头原话逐字摘录）、带时间的结构节拍、标题公式、行动号召、目标人群、可复用模板。所有引用都和原文逐字核对，对不上的直接删掉并写明——一条 15 分钟的剪辑教程里，模型写出的 7 条“引用”原文里没有，都被删了。点赞、收藏、话题标签来自平台，不由模型编。加 translateto: "en" 可以直接拿到英文版拆解。 接入方式：Claude Code / Cursor 用 MCP；REST 一个 POST；批量 50 条带签名回调；Dify 插件、Apify；另有 /openapi.json（OpenAPI 3.0.3）。 注册送 10 积分（一次性）；任何人读过的链接再读免费；读不出内容不收费。加量包 ¥36 / 250 积分，支持支付宝。 （作者自荐。）

projects.title: Show HN: A critical thinking site for kids and teens
projects.author: Critikid
projects.summary: In 2019, I was teaching science at an international school in Chiang Mai. One day before class, one of my Grade 7 students asked me about flat earth. He had heard the idea from Kyrie Irving and then spent the night on flat earth sites. We walked through the claims and I explained why those arguments failed. He listened with interest. I was glad he'd come to me. He hadn't made up his mind yet; he was just curious. But this made me wonder if teaching the course content I was teaching was enough. To be clear: I do think teaching facts is important. For example, when students learn about gravity, physics, and space, they're better prepared to see why flat earth arguments are wrong. The problem is we can't teach facts fast enough to combat the wide variety of misinformation and manipulation kids face on the internet every day. This is what got me thinking that kids need to learn how to evaluate claims and information across a wide range of topics. While we can't prepare them for every false or misleading claim they might encounter, we can give them tools to assess them. That eventually led my husband and I to build Critikid, a site for teaching kids and teens. We've been working on it for 3 years now! He does the technical work (design and coding) and I do the educational content creation. By now, there are 5 interactive courses for ages 5-18 on logical fallacies, media literacy, emotional intelligence, statistical reasoning, and formal logic. There are also worksheets and lesson plans. I often teach through stories, as stories make abstract critical thinking concepts concrete (and they're fun!) If you'd like to try it, all of the courses have a free first lesson. Are there any other topics that you think should be included in kids' critical thinking education that I've missed?

Our protagonist Naxiah is stranded on a small, desolated planet. You're working for an intergalactic distributor of seeds and terraforming equipment, to kickstart new planets in far away galaxies. You must deliver seeds and utilities to an unchartered region, but on your way, you crash on a small planet. Luckily, you have some equipment with you in the ship, so you're able to spawn a base and survive. But for how long? And is the planet really deserted..? :) Well, of course not, there are aliens and other space creatures. And of course, there's ROBO RB-23, which accompanies your adventure. The game is written in Object Pascal and uses our own game engine PasVulkan, our own physics engine, as well as our own RISC-V 64-bit emulator PasRISCV. We love to build stuff, a lot of these things are FOSS. The emulator is quite complete (even with RVV, but that's way too slow emulated to be useful) and runs a stock kernel (6.18.3 as of today). We're using Alpine Linux for our base distribution. All our in-game programs to interact with the planet are native RISC-V Linux programs. We also have our own (free and open source) scripting language POCA (class and prototyped based, JS/Lua inspired, which makes it quite easy for us to script things like HUD, animal behaviour, our story flow graph, etc. We have most of the wiring ready for players to be able to program and reshape and populate the whole planet in automation, although it's not our primary concept for the game (building stuff by hand, making the planet beautiful is also fun). As it's a normal Linux system, you'll be able to use Ruby, Python, or even Rust, C, C++, and Go to change and automate your world. We're also thinking of making a bunch of small games which you can play inside the game, in the base on a computer, on an arcade machine, or in the spaceship. And of course, it also runs DOOM. We already prototyped a small 2D space shooter and a small arcade game, both playable within the game. We also feature a table with hologram games to be played, e.g. chess and a certain block game. We also plan to make this hologram game engine available from the computer, which means, you'll even be able to program own hologram style games. We generally want to make the in-game computer more hackable in future, so that people can create and share their own little games. Currently, it's only a sandbox game (with beginnings of automation), to build stuff with our pre-made items. You can also assemble these to other, ready-made and shareable bigger items. This is the foundation for us to further develop survival and complete our story mode. Our game is still under active development, and we finally got our Steam page ready. We have tons of other things planned, but right now, it's more about polishing and quality for the Early Access. You can watch some videos and screenshots on our website. And we'd love to read your thoughts about his. It has been quite a ride, so far..

projects.title: Show HN: Keel – Give your agent a typed strategy language, not a trading account
projects.author: zferland
projects.summary: I’ve been using AI agents to build systematic strategies on Hyperliquid for over a year, and slowly built up a reliable system to represent, test and deploy strategies. Typically there are a few options 1) llm in the execution loop, ie it makes decisions and trades, but that is slow, inconsistent and hard to audit 2) you have an agent write all the code, backtest etc, but it makes tons of subtle mistakes with time series data and diff timeframe etc, and is often not reusing bits. There are some ways to improve this of course with right frameworks and setups. But its still hard to be confident in its correctness and its hard for you to verify quickly. With Keel we built a small typed language (DSL) to represent strategies. It uses a well defined set of components to build a DAG of steps, it carries types and clocks. This allows agents to build these strategies with a really fast feedback loop as they can be quickly validated and many common errors avoided. In a DAG its also easy to inspect intermediate results. Valid strategies are fingerprinted and the exact same artifact runs in backtesting and live. These strategies are also much easier for humans to verify as they are self describing components, and mostly linear to read and reason about. Still trying to improve the space of how many types of different strategies can be represented in this and still trying to improve how well LLMs go from natural language to strategy. A lot of the improvements come from just giving the agents better and faster tools and faster feedback loops.

projects.title: Show HN: Breadcrumb, record everything on your mac + context manager for AI
projects.author: jv22222
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Justin. Breadcrumb records everything you do on your Mac (screen + meetings + AI transcripts + what you and your AI decided) and turns it into memory your AI can search. It's local and encrypted. You can also teach it rules by talking to it and it makes sure the right rules turn up in the right context. Works with Claude Code / Codex / Cursor / opencode. All of this is exposed to your AI as 30+ MCP tools (here's the definitions): https://innerloop.works/breadcrumb/mcp I started it in June because I wanted to understand what was going on with my AI dev work. Then it just kept growing as I jammed on it 10 hours a day for 3 months. I started by recording every screen so I could jump back to a moment and see what I'd been doing with the AI. Then I added MCP so the AI could search it. Then time tracking. Then meetings with transcripts and timestamped screenshots. After that I started feeding the data back in. At first it was just a few relevant memories in the prompt. Then I started adding rules and rules modules. Then I started recording the AI transcripts and all the other stuff the AI did (subagents, tools etc). I wanted a complete record so I could go back and see what the AI did and why. I found the more data the AI had the more useful it became. One example. I got off a zoom call with the team at the day job and said: "Review the meeting I just had, find all the bugs we discussed, and create JIRA tickets with screenshots." It read the transcript. Found every bug we mentioned, pulled the screens from the screen timeline, spun up my local server, diagnosed each bug, reviewed the code, created 14 tickets in JIRA with diagnosis and likely fixes, attached 12 screenshots as evidence, and created a nice Slack message to send to my colleagues. I never built a workflow for any of that. Claude had the meeting record, Breadcrumb tools, and rules I'd accumulated. It basically chained the steps together itself. My favorite thing about the system is observability of my own work as an AI developer. I can trace a bug all the way back to the first thing I said (or the first thing the AI did) that caused it. Then I can add a rule so it doesn't happen again. Anyway, my working system is simply Claude Desktop + Breadcrumb + Markdown. I find I don't need anything else. It's local software for one person. Local models for transcription and diarization. Data encrypted with SQLCipher and a passphrase. You can exclude any apps, websites, words and phrases. Breadcrumb itself only makes one network call which is a daily update check. (but of course your AI will use it and that is local or cloud depending on what you use). It runs cool about 12% of one core on average (M series mac has 8+). You can set it to just save OCR text or to save screenshots. If just OCR it's about 12mb day (a lot of telemetry, indexing etc). If you record screenshots on meetings it's about 120mb/hour (1 every 2 secs). It can also record screenshots of everything that's heavy at about 160mb/day. It does local classification/naming with ollama with Gemma 3 4B (2.5 GB). It's 100% free. There's no account you can just download and start using it. I'll monetize it via E2EE cloud sync and team sync. It's open beta. Just one developer working on it. Requires 16GB+ M Series Mac. Thanks for reading! https://innerloop.works/breadcrumb (homepage) https://innerloop.works/breadcrumb/download (direct download) https://innerloop.works/breadcrumb/mcp (mcp definition)

projects.title: Show HN: Web search engine built from the CommonCrawl corpus
projects.author: xoredev
projects.summary: Hello HN, I'm building an alternative web search engine. You can try the demo here: https://search.xorsoft.dev/ My goal was to reach 1% of Google's index. This is 4 billion pages across 33.5 million domains. I was inspired by the earlier attempts shared here: "Building a web search engine from scratch with 3B neural embeddings" [1] and "Crawling a billion web pages in just over 24 hours" [2]. I decided not to replicate them and instead used CommonCrawl corpus, built a pipeline, and threw the results into a classic full-text search index. First, I got my hands on a dedicated Hetzner server with 4x10TB HDDs. It allowed me to crunch CommonCrawl data and stay within my hobby budget. The backend is served from a similar "home-grade" server but with NVMe disks instead. The compressed index weighs just over 2TB because I cap content length at 4KB per page (p50=2.9KB, p99=46KB) to fit it on disk. I picked Rust for my project. After years of big data engineering on the JVM, Rust felt like a breath of fresh air. I ended up not using any special data processing libraries - the pipeline is relatively straightforward and runs without crashes. As for full-text search, tantivy was an obvious choice. It took some time to get single query latency down to an acceptable ~350ms, although concurrent requests quickly max out disk t/p at 6.1GB/s and latency starts to climb. The search algorithm is primitive by modern standards: top 1,000 candidates are retrieved using BM25 (text relevance signal) and then reranked with PageRank [3]. Turns out you can fit the whole internet in a single server rack. The challenge here, of course, is to keep it up to date, especially if you don't have unlimited (crawl) budget. Right now I'm looking for funding or sponsorship to get extra hardware. That would allow me to scale the project and keep it free to use. I can also periodically dump the index on HuggingFace for research purposes. Any suggestions are welcome. projects.title: Show HN: Quiet – exploring when an AI assistant should intervene
projects.author: roger05
projects.summary: I’m Ruggiero, a CS student working on a research project about humanComputer interaction and AI. I built QUIET because I’ve been thinking about a problem with current AI interfaces: they usually either wait for an explicit prompt, or try to take over a task. I wanted to explore a different relationship between humans and AI: an assistant that can understand when to stay out of the way, when to point something out, when to teach, and when to act. I’ve built a small interactive demo of this idea. It’s obviously still very early, and I want to understand whether the interaction itself makes sense before trying to build the actual AI system behind it. The prototype is intentionally not AI-powered yet. The four examples are scripted so I can test the interaction itself before spending time building the underlying AI system. The idea is that the assistant can choose different levels/forms of intervention: * stay silent * point at something * explain / teach * do the task The important question for me isn’t whether an AI can perform these actions. Current systems can already do many of them. I’m trying to understand whether an assistant that decides when and how much to intervene is actually useful. I’d particularly like feedback on: * Did the interventions feel helpful or annoying? * Would you want an assistant to behave this way? * When would you prefer it to teach you rather than do something for you? * Does this interaction model make sense even without the AI being there yet? I started working on this because I feel there is an increasing gap between what computers/AI are capable of and what users actually understand and can make use of. At the same time, AI systems are becoming increasingly capable of explaining and performing tasks for us. I’m interested in whether the interface itself should evolve to bridge that gap. Demo: https://quiet-hci.pages.dev I’d really appreciate any criticism, especially if you think the interaction model doesn’t make sense. projects.title: Show HN: Silta: family assistant on Matrix with continuity across context limits
projects.author: dmitry-markin
projects.summary: Silta is a self-hosted assistant serving multiple users from a single Matrix account, used by me, family, and close friends for the last three weeks. It runs on Claude Code with each person using their own Claude subscription. Silta answers everyday questions, conducts web research (presenting the results as PDFs), performs scheduled tasks to monitor/research something and notify you if needed. It uses a deliberate handoff & compaction procedure, writing the compaction summary itself with a custom prompt, so the thread of the conversation and its picture of the user is preserved across context limits. As it turned out, the assistant accessible in a continuous chat (contrary to ChatGPT / Claude Web sessions) builds up better context about you and your tasks, and provides more relevant answers and help. It runs on Claude Code as the only allowed way to use a personal Claude subscription. Using Claude Code also spares me developing a harness, at the cost of tracking changes as new versions of Claude Code are released. The assistant itself (the daemon, the channel plugin, the supervisor, and the deployment) is open-source, while the model and the harness are Anthropic's and proprietary. Silta is deployed to a dedicated VM with separate Linux users per session and systemd hardening, protecting sessions from each other. Claude Code's bubblewrap sandbox is used to protect the Claude credential and the harness's state from the agent. This does not protect from prompt injections coming from search results and potentially leaking user data. Matrix E2EE protects the conversation from a Matrix server operator, but everything in the context is of course sent to the model provider. Private content is never logged, and the operator is expected to respect the privacy and not read the session transcripts on disk. Additionally, it is recommended to use full-disk encryption and tell the users how their data is handled. Silta only works in its workspace with files explicitly shared by users in the chat. Giving it access to a user's own computer or services like email is not planned. Since Opus 5.5 has been released, it is possible to run a session on a $20 Claude Pro subscription. Before that, only Fable 5.1 was pleasant enough to talk to. When run on Anthropic API, a moderately used session extrapolates to $100-$150 per month, with each research run costing $6-$12. Silta is built with Claude Code and Silta itself. The design, review, deployment, and testing are mine.

In terms of implementation, it's basically a pipeline that processes a list of sources consisting of trade media and indie newsletters and blogs with RSS feeds, and tags them with Jev using a hierarchy of topics related to edtech. Users can follow and pin individual topics, like "higher ed", "Europe" etc., so we don't need any persistent profiles for personalization; preferences live in the browser. Articles are clustered using cloudflare's vector store, and related articles are also recommended with that. I have no doubt this will work even better with tech news, but there are plenty of alternatives out there, so I'm not going to indulge myself further. My takeaway is that Jev for content tagging is great so far. And edtech is kinda fun to keep up with. The project is called EdFountain at https://edfountain.com The goal is to create the water fountain for edtech. For those who like to follow edtech, maybe it's useful to you as well. projects.title: Show HN: Autobox – Make your agents sandbox themselves
projects.author: freakynit
projects.summary: https://github.com/freakynit/autobox First of all: this is NOT for folks who are already using a sandbox. The guarantees provided by Autobox are weaker. This is rather for folks who "hesitate" to use sandboxes. Autobox is built around two observations I kept making over past one year of seeing sandbox launches and their real-world usage: 1. There are many sandboxing options now, and they work well. But leaving a handful few, almost nobody uses them. The blocker isn't the technology, it's the setup friction — however small it looks on paper, it's enough that people skip it entirely. 2. LLMs mostly don't write harmful code or take destructive steps. They're not adversarial by default. Autobox bets on the second observation to remove the first. Instead of asking you to configure a sandbox, it's just there: every tool call carries its own permissions, and anything you don't explicitly allow is denied. Is it perfect? No - seatbelt filesystem rules are best-effort, and the strong isolation is the V8 path. Is it better than using no sandbox at all? Definitely yes. This is also for M-series Macs only. --- Oh, and the best part: "copy_then_sync": Using APPFS `clonefile`, Autobox can hand your agent a full, "writable" copy of a repo instantly (1-2 ms). The agent gets something it can freely "destroy", but, your actual working tree is untouched. Your agent can then verify things, and of all looks okay, in one command sync the changes back to host within milliseconds.

projects.title: Show HN: Read the Odyssey in Greek while learning Greek
projects.author: ethanedwards
projects.summary: I made a way to (sort of) read the Odyssey in Greek without all those years of learning Greek first. I’ve had a deep interest in reading great literature in its original language since I studied Latin in High School, but wanted to find ways of reading real literature quickly. I’ve used this method myself to read books in several languages including Italian, German, Chinese, Japanese, and Greek. You still have to do the grammar and vocabulary study over time to really comprehend it, but this method has worked far better than all my previous attempts. The goal is to eventually be able just to read the language without any aids, but do that while reading real stuff the entire time. I’ve found that I go from needing help on everything, to learning individual words, to phrases, and then gradually I get to understanding whole sentences without looking anything up. Using a translation helps to keep me honest. I made a little demo of some lines from the Odyssey Book 1 to share the method and see if other people might find it useful. This is a special version that has a lot of explanation to see if something as difficult as Homeric Greek can be approached from 0. The interlinear translation and notes are AI generated though I made sure to ground them in real translations and existing grammatical tags. The commentary won't be as good as an actual Classical scholar's work and can be overly simplistic, but I'm hoping it's enough to get started. There are other versions that feature progressive grammar learning and identification as well as flashcards. If people are interested I'm happy to share the rest of the book or other texts I've made and read myself. I have the New Testament in Greek and then a bunch of other works in lots of ancient and modern languages.
